dec0de-atari-st-deprotection.title: $DEC0DE — Atari ST deprotection
dec0de-atari-st-deprotection.notes: C tool removes documented protection schemes from ST programs, including Rob Northen Copylock series 1/2, Anti-bitos and several packers. Source and prebuilt binaries for ST and hosts are provided; each supported protection is listed in the README.

c64-15-second-format-disassembly.title: 15 Second Format
c64-15-second-format-disassembly.display_title: 15 Second Format — C64 and 1541 utility disassembly
c64-15-second-format-disassembly.notes: Dave McMurtrie disassembled a historical C64/1541 fast-format utility; 64tass source separates host and drive code. The README names a historical PRG and assembly command, without claiming byte-identical output or a verified run.

180-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

c64-rohingosling-3d-cube-commodore.title: 3D Cube
c64-rohingosling-3d-cube-commodore.notes: Author disassembled surviving VIC-20 and C64 PRGs of a historical personal 3D cube demo and recast them as modifiable Kick Assembler projects. Both computer builds and running instructions are documented; provenance is recovered own binary, not an original source archive.

deathchase-spectrum.title: 3D Deathchase
deathchase-spectrum.notes: Disassembly and annotation of the 1983 ZX Spectrum game Deathchase by Ritchie Swann.

8bit-analysers.title: 8-Bit Analysers
8bit-analysers.notes: Multi-platform analysis/annotation toolkit for 8-bit games. Includes Spectrum, C64 and CPC analysers, assembler export support and MCP analysis tooling; tracked as adjacent reverse-engineering infrastructure.

c64-mist64-80columns.title: 80columns
c64-mist64-80columns.notes: Reconstructed and optimized historical 80COLUMNS.PRG, whose original author is unidentified. cc65/exomizer build emits a 2.2 KB runnable C64 80x25 screen utility, with alternate character sets.

avtak-c64-unorig.title: A View to a Kill
avtak-c64-unorig.display_title: A View to a Kill — C64 reverse-engineered source
avtak-c64-unorig.notes: Slowly progressing reverse-engineering/decompilation of the C64 game. The repository keeps 6502bench analysis projects and assembly exported for 64tass, with game/map observations intended to support bug understanding and eventual fixes.

a2scsi-rom-gorlik.title: a2scsi-rom
a2scsi-rom-gorlik.display_title: Apple II SCSI Card ROM — annotated disassembly
a2scsi-rom-gorlik.notes: Commented disassembly of Apple II SCSI Card ROM revision 341-0437-A (rev. c), with sixteen 1 KiB banks and SourceGen project files. Its Makefile reassembles the complete ROM for EPROM programming or MAME; the README also documents driver interactions and firmware behavior. Byte-exact output is not asserted.

abm-apple2-6502disassembly.title: ABM
abm-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: ABM — Apple II game disassembly & engine analysis
abm-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II ABM disassembly covering the game, paddle-read routine and Applesoft loader/configuration programs. The SourceGen project uses an extension script to format heavy inline data and documents self-modifying code, floating-point use, collision behavior and incremental explosion rendering.

acorn-6502-copro-os-seddon.title: Acorn 6502 Second Processor OS
acorn-6502-copro-os-seddon.display_title: Acorn 6502 Second Processor OS — buildable ROM disassembly
acorn-6502-copro-os-seddon.notes: Buildable disassembly of Acorn's 6502 second-processor and Master Turbo OS ROMs. It builds 4 KiB ROM images on modern Windows/macOS/Linux systems and verifies supported 1.10/1.20 outputs against reference ROMs.

acorn-tube-client-acornaeology.title: Acorn 6502 Tube Client — ROM reconstruction
acorn-tube-client-acornaeology.notes: Annotated disassembly of external and Master Turbo internal v1.10 Tube Client ROM variants, generated from original bytes and reassembled with beebasm in CI.

acorn-adfs-acornaeology.title: Acorn ADFS 1.30 — ROM reconstruction
acorn-adfs-acornaeology.notes: Annotated ADFS 1.30 filing-system ROM disassembly, including disc and SCSI paths; README documents beebasm byte-for-byte reassembly and CI verification.

acorn-econet-bridge-acornaeology.title: Acorn Econet Bridge — firmware reconstruction
acorn-econet-bridge-acornaeology.notes: Annotated variant 1 bridge firmware disassembly from the standalone 6502-based network device; README documents beebasm byte-for-byte reassembly and CI verification.

acorn-mos-disassembly-seddon.title: Acorn MOS
acorn-mos-disassembly-seddon.display_title: Acorn MOS — Master-series ROM disassembly & reconstruction
acorn-mos-disassembly-seddon.notes: Work-in-progress disassembly of multiple released and unreleased Acorn MOS versions for the 8-bit Master family and derivatives. The shared source is intended to be modifiable and builds original ROM variants that are checked against the reference ROMs; the project also produces experimental refreshed MOS variants.

action-replay-5-amiga.title: Action Replay 5
action-replay-5-amiga.notes: Builds an expanded Amiga Action Replay debugger from Action Replay III and reverse-engineered ARIV/Action Replay IV material, combining original and newly authored code. README documents DeMoN cartridge, WinUAE, original cartridge and software modes; makefile assembles 68000 sources with vasm. A vasm build recipe is present, but a successful current build, output/runtime variants and binary equality have not been verified.

adf-opus-2025.title: ADF Opus 2025
adf-opus-2025.display_title: ADF Opus 2025 — Amiga disk image workbench
source_language: Amiga ADF and OFS/FFS disk structures
adf-opus-2025.notes: 2025 revival of the original 2003 ADF Opus source; offers disk-image browsing, raw bootblock inspection and Greaseweazle support for physical floppy reads/writes. Based on preserved source, not a claim to have reconstructed the old binary.

adf-reader-writer-js.title: ADF reader/writer
adf-reader-writer-js.display_title: ADF reader/writer — Amiga OFS/FFS image inspector
source_language: Amiga OFS/FFS filesystem and ADF/HDF images
adf-reader-writer-js.notes: Plain JavaScript OFS/FFS reader/writer for ADF and HDF images, with extraction and raw-sector access useful for recovering files from damaged images. Multi-partition HDFs are not supported.

adf7z-amiga-filesystem.title: Adf7z
adf7z-amiga-filesystem.notes: 7-Zip format plugin for extracting Amiga OFS/FFS files from ADF images. README limits it to read/extract operations: links and attributes are not supported, and ADF creation or modification is unavailable.

adflib-amiga-filesystem.title: ADFlib
adflib-amiga-filesystem.notes: Portable C implementation of Amiga OFS/FFS for ADF/HDF and disk diagnostics, with metadata, bitmap and salvage utilities. README labels native-device handling and RDB writing experimental and warns that dircache writing has limited test coverage.

after-shock-spectrum.title: After Shock
after-shock-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

akira-famicom-g0me3.title: Akira
akira-famicom-g0me3.notes: The author's Back From Source repository reconstructs the Famicom Akira program in banked assembly and includes a DASM build script for an NES image. RetroRE labels this a partial reverse engineering effort. Reassembly exists as a documented script; successful execution and byte identity have not been verified.

vs-sr-cd32-alfredchicken.title: Alfred Chicken — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-alfredchicken.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Alfred Chicken. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

ali-baba-apple2-xekri.title: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves — Apple II reconstruction
ali-baba-apple2-xekri.upstream_name: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
ali-baba-apple2-xekri.display_title: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves — Apple II reconstruction
subjects: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
ali-baba-apple2-xekri.notes: Literate reverse engineering of Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves for Apple II. The build tangles and assembles reconstructed sources and can rebuild/verify the full disk image byte-for-byte against the reference.

alien-spectrum.title: Alien
alien-spectrum.notes: Fully annotated disassembly; rebuilt image is byte-identical to the tape and a dependency-free web port has a parity suite.

alien-c64-python-remake.title: Alien (1984) — Python remake and disassembly
alien-c64-python-remake.notes: Playable Python reimplementation of the 1984 C64 Alien built from a complete disassembly of the original disk. The repository also includes alientools for NIB/G64/D64 decoding, CBM-DOS reconstruction, program extraction and disassembly, plus annotated RE documentation and an ORIGINAL mode intended to reproduce observed disk behaviour.

alien8-tcdev-spectrum.title: Alien 8 — tcdev
alien8-tcdev-spectrum.notes: tcdev reverse-engineering project; repository marks Alien 8 as WIP and aims for reassemblable/relocatable source.

alien-breed-3d-source-derived-pc-port.title: Alien Breed 3D I
alien-breed-3d-source-derived-pc-port.display_title: Alien Breed 3D — Amiga source-derived C port
alien-breed-3d-source-derived-pc-port.notes: Native C reimplementation of the original Amiga game's gameplay and renderer, using the historical 68000 assembly source as reference and preserving Amiga data formats. SDL2 desktop and Emscripten builds are documented. This is source-derived porting, not a disassembly of an Amiga binary; no Amiga executable is run by the port.

alien-breed-amiga-hitchhikr.title: Alien Breed — Amiga disassembly
alien-breed-amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Complete Amiga Alien Breed disassembly from the Disk 2 executable. The build extracts the original binary, assembles reconstructed hunks, joins them into an executable and provides emulator-based original/generated testing; the project also removes self-modifying code and comments large portions of the program.

alis-silmarils-vm.title: ALIS — Silmarils virtual machine
alis-silmarils-vm.notes: Reimplements Silmarils ALIS VM using original game data. Primary compatibility matrix marks multiple ST and Amiga versions playable (including Mad Show, Targhan, Colorado), while Manhattan Dealers and Operation: Cleanstreets are broken; playability is per game/version, not universal.

amaurote-128-spectrum-analyser.title: Amaurote 128
amaurote-128-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Amaurote128 directory contains an approximately 942 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.title: Amber Remix — Amiga Amberstar data decoder
amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.upstream_name: Amber Remix — Amiga Amberstar data decoder
amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.display_title: Amber Remix — Amiga Amberstar data decoder
amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.notes: Rust decoder/playback for original Amiga Amberstar containers, text, graphics, maps and Hippel-CoSo music; scripts and items only partially decoded. Credits Pyrdacor format documentation and related playback work; requires user-supplied data.

ambermoon.title: Ambermoon
ambermoon.notes: Binary and data-format research feeding the broader Ambermoon reconstruction ecosystem.

ambermoon-advanced.title: Ambermoon Advanced
ambermoon-advanced.notes: Unofficial Ambermoon extension. Track only changes that exercise or expose reverse-engineered knowledge of the original engine/formats.

ambermoon-re-tooling.title: Ambermoon reverse-engineering tooling
ambermoon-re-tooling.notes: Tools and documented methodology used to reverse engineer Ambermoon internals; feeds Ambermoon.net research.

ambermoon-net.title: Ambermoon.net
ambermoon-net.notes: Modern reimplementation substantially informed by reverse engineering of original Ambermoon behaviour and data.

ambermoon-sourceror.title: AmbermoonSourceror
ambermoon-sourceror.notes: Work-in-progress CLI tool that converts Ghidra ASCII exports of Ambermoon AM2_CPU/AM2_BLIT into valid Amiga assembler source.

amberstar.title: Amberstar
amberstar.notes: Research and format decoding across the Amiga, Atari ST and DOS versions.

amberworld-research.title: Amberworld
amberworld-research.display_title: Amberworld — Amber trilogy format & code reverse engineering
amberworld-research.notes: Oliver Gantert's long-running Amberworld project. Its site documents extraction/conversion tools and source releases for Amberstar, Ambermoon and Albion, extensive reverse-engineered file formats, and a later return to disassembled game-code analysis.

amiberry-mcp-server.title: Amiberry MCP Server
amiberry-mcp-server.display_title: Amiberry MCP Server — emulator control and debugging
amiberry-mcp-server.notes: Python MCP integration for the Amiberry emulator, including machine control, live memory access, save states, ROM identification and screenshots. Runtime controls require Amiberry built with USE_IPC_SOCKET=ON; its README limits the server to macOS and Linux.

jotd-amidar-amiga.title: Amidar — Amiga arcade port

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga 500
runtime_profiles.notes: README requires 1 MB and states 50 fps even on a 68000 A500.

evidence.excerpt: any 68k CPU; Kickstart 1.3, 1MB memory

jotd-amidar-amiga.notes: 1:1 Amiga 500 port in 68k assembly preserving original visuals, sounds, intro and 50 fps target.

amidisk-classic-amiga-preservation.title: AmiDisk — classic Amiga disk preservation
amidisk-classic-amiga-preservation.notes: Native AmigaOS 2.04+ disk imaging and copying project with trackdisk.device and ADF baseline. README distinguishes planned recovery, bootblock and filesystem features from current M0 baseline.

amiforensics-amiga-toolkit.title: AmiForensics — Amiga analysis toolkit
amiforensics-amiga-toolkit.notes: Fifteen native Amiga commands plus optional workstation workflows for HUNK, bootblock, resident, memory, disk and patch inspection. README documents a -m68000 AmigaOS 2.04+ intended baseline and `make check`; AROS/FS-UAE and host-side qualification are distinct from real Commodore AmigaOS qualification, which remains unclaimed.

amifuse-filesystem-emulation.title: AmiFUSE
amifuse-filesystem-emulation.notes: Mounts Amiga HDF/RDB and ADF images by executing native filesystem handler binaries through m68k emulation, including PFS3. ADF use requires an external driver. Documented as an alternative to reimplementing each filesystem format; not a reconstructed filesystem driver.

kickstart-11-a1000-disassembly.title: Amiga 1000 Kickstart 1.1 v31.34 disassembly
kickstart-11-a1000-disassembly.notes: PAL Amiga 1000 Kickstart 1.1 v31.34 disassembly used to reconstruct ROM relocation tables for a Seven Cities of Gold WHDLoad install.

amiga-basic-decompiler-djnice.title: Amiga BASIC Decompiler
amiga-basic-decompiler-djnice.notes: Standalone Python 3 decompiler for AmigaBASIC binary files. README documents extended token pairs, numeric constants, name-table resolution and Latin-2 text output; these breadth claims come from the project and are not independently validated. Distinct from seawolf’s earlier Go converter.

vscode-amiga-debug-bartmanabyss.title: Amiga C/C++ Compile, Debug & Profile
vscode-amiga-debug-bartmanabyss.display_title: VS Code Amiga C/C++ debugger & profiler
vscode-amiga-debug-bartmanabyss.notes: Self-contained VS Code Amiga C/C++/assembly toolchain with bundled cross-GCC/GDB and WinUAE/FS-UAE integration. Provides source/assembly debugging, memory/watchpoints, frame and DMA profiling, graphics/blitter/Copper inspection, executable-size profiling and source-correlated disassembly.

amiga-devbench-mcp.title: Amiga DevBench
amiga-devbench-mcp.display_title: Amiga DevBench — serial debugger and MCP development environment
amiga-devbench-mcp.notes: Host/target bridge over serial to a real or FS-UAE Amiga, with memory/register inspection, breakpoints, remote execution, a web dashboard and MCP tools. The optional patched FS-UAE enables a separate emulator-level debugger; ordinary FS-UAE still supports the serial bridge. Docker is used for the 68k cross compiler.

amiga-file-forge-workbench.title: Amiga File Forge
amiga-file-forge-workbench.display_title: Amiga File Forge — disk, ROM and Hunk analysis workbench
amiga-file-forge-workbench.notes: Web and Linux workbench for Amiga floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents RDB partition work, Amiga filesystems, resident modules, Hunk analysis, annotated 68k disassembly and exact-hash guarded patches. It is host-side tooling, not software running on an Amiga; some historical-media and emulator-dependent tasks require user-supplied inputs.

amigaghidra-scripts-caddy666.title: Amiga Ghidra annotation scripts
amigaghidra-scripts-caddy666.notes: Collection of 15 Ghidra scripts for Amiga exception vectors, library calls, resident structures, compiler clues and OCS/ECS/AGA plus Akiko/Gayle register maps. README merely calls them experiments; no tested compatibility or installation procedure is asserted.

amiga-imploder-decompiled-lab313ru.title: Amiga Imploder — decompiled compressor
amiga-imploder-decompiled-lab313ru.notes: Dr. MefistO describes the Imploder compression algorithm as decompiled and fully restored; repository contains implode/explode C and a Lazarus GUI. Hitchhikr credits its reversed routines as a basis for the separately tracked imploder executable packer. No byte-identical legacy binary rebuild is claimed.

amiga-lzx-rust.title: Amiga LZX — Rust reconstruction
amiga-lzx-rust.notes: Author describes LLM-assisted reconstruction: original compressor decompiled with Ghidra, a specification written, then Rust implementation built from the spec, with unlzx.c informing decompressor documentation. CLI/library create, list, extract and test Amiga LZX archives; runs on modern hosts.

amiga-sources-moon70.title: Amiga Sources
amiga-sources-moon70.display_title: Amiga Sources — Abyss demo source archive
amiga-sources-moon70.notes: Author-released ASM-One sources for multiple historical Abyss Amiga demos and music discs; some contributions are partial, so the collection is not represented as full source for every production.

amiga-re-rust-toolkit.title: amiga-re — Rust reversing toolkit
amiga-re-rust-toolkit.notes: Rust CLI and libraries for ADF file recovery, HUNK parsing, 68000 disassembly, bootcode tracing, IFF/ILBM/8SVX decoding and bounded emulated calls/frame capture. README advertises structured output for AI-assisted workflows; this alone does not establish that AI wrote or analysed the project.

amiga68ktools-jotd.title: amiga68ktools
amiga68ktools-jotd.notes: Collection of Amiga 68k analysis scripts. Its 68kchecker scans IRA-generated disassembly for branches with no memory writes, self-modifying code and supervisor/VBR accesses; tool documentation names IRA and Python 2.5 prerequisites.

amiga-hunk-parser-rust-emoon.title: amiga_hunk_parser — Rust HUNK parser
amiga-hunk-parser-rust-emoon.notes: Separate Rust crate by same author parses Amiga HUNK executables. Repository has Cargo.toml and src; capabilities and fidelity beyond parsing are not asserted.

amigaasm-ghidra-exporter.title: AmigaAsm
amigaasm-ghidra-exporter.notes: Amiga m68k assembly exporter for Ghidra; repository README is terse, so successful rebuilds and ROM fidelity are unverified.

amigabasic-binary-parser-seawolf.title: AmigaBASIC Binary-to-ASCII Converter
amigabasic-binary-parser-seawolf.notes: Go converter reads tokenized AmigaBASIC files, replaces known keyword codes, resolves names/labels from the file trailer and writes a text program. README and Go tests establish a working parser, without a claim of complete keyword or numeric coverage.

ida-amiga-debugger-lab313ru.title: amigadbg — IDA/Amitools Amiga debugger
ida-amiga-debugger-lab313ru.notes: IDA Pro AmigaOS debugger plugin designed to work with Amitools. This is a distinct live/debugging integration, not the Ghidra hunk loader.

amigaffh-formats.title: AmigaFFH — Amiga file formats
amigaffh-formats.notes: R package for reading Amiga native formats, including IFF images and tokenized AmigaBASIC programs. Repository is a CRAN mirror of pepijn-devries/AmigaFFH; install snippet in README unexpectedly names ProTrackR, so package installation was not verified here.

amiga-hunk-parser-c-emoon.title: AmigaHunkParser — C HUNK parser
amiga-hunk-parser-c-emoon.notes: C library and headers parse Amiga HUNK executables; Makefile and sample test program present. Separate from the author’s Rust crate, with no runtime or completeness claims from its short README.

php-amiga-iff-ilbm-converter.title: AmigaIFFConverter — ILBM writer
php-amiga-iff-ilbm-converter.notes: PHP JPEG/PNG to ILBM writer with HAM6 and ECS modes and optional ByteRun1 compression. README reports opening generated HAM6 output in DeluxePaint IV. Source-derived asset pipeline, not recovered historical code.

amigainfo-icon-tool.title: amigainfo
amigainfo-icon-tool.display_title: amigainfo — Amiga .info icon parser and converter
amigainfo-icon-tool.notes: Python library and CLI reads, modifies and writes classic, NewIcons, GlowIcons, ARGB and PowerIcons files; exposes tooltypes and icon metadata for preservation/inspection.

amigaos-kickstart-rcs-history-restoratio.title: AmigaOS Kickstart — RCS source-history restoration
amigaos-kickstart-rcs-history-restoratio.notes: Rebuilds a Git timeline from surviving original AmigaOS 3 RCS source revisions. Tags represent approximate inferred states from pre-1.0 through 3.1; early source trees are especially incomplete and ordering can be uncertain. This is archival source-history reconstruction, not source recovered from ROM binaries; no reproducible build is claimed.

amiga-quarterback-extractor.title: AmigaQB_extract
amiga-quarterback-extractor.notes: Recovers Central Coast Software Quarterback backups from ADF images, including damaged or catalogless sets. README documents v4.x through v6.x, compressed markers, catalog layout and format research checked against original GPL Quarterback source. Host-side recovery tool, not an Amiga executable.

amiquake-c2p-reconstruction.title: AmiQuake GCC Port
amiquake-c2p-reconstruction.display_title: AmiQuake — Quake port with recovered C2P routine

runtime_profiles.name: GCC port
runtime_profiles.notes: 68040 or 68060 with FPU; no minimum RAM established.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga with 68040/68060 CPU + FPU

amiquake-c2p-reconstruction.notes: GCC port of AmiQuake based on awinquake 0.9. An 842-byte NovaCoder chunky-to-planar routine was extracted from AmiQuake 1.36 and rewritten as readable 68k assembly; the author reports working console, palette and viewport tests. AI assistance is asserted without naming a model/tool.

amitools-amiga-toolkit.title: amitools
amitools-amiga-toolkit.display_title: amitools — Amiga binary, ROM & filesystem toolkit
amitools-amiga-toolkit.notes: Host-side toolkit for classic 68k AmigaOS binaries and storage formats. Includes hunktool/Hunk libraries for inspecting and relocating Amiga binaries and object files, romtool for dissecting/building Kickstart ROMs, ADF/HDF/RDB/OFS/FFS tooling, and vamos, an API-level AmigaOS emulator with library-call, structure and memory tracing useful for analysing old executables and running historical development tools.

amostools-kyz.title: amostools
amostools-kyz.notes: dumpamos extracts AMOS source and memory banks, listamos renders AMOS source as plaintext, and unlockamos unlocks procedures. Third-party AMOS extensions may be needed to decode tokens correctly.

cpc-basic-1-1.title: Amstrad CPC BASIC 1.1
cpc-basic-1-1.notes: Completed 'unassembly' into relocatable/modifiable source; generated ROM output is compared with the original and intended to be identical.

cpc464-rom-disassembly.title: Amstrad CPC464 Firmware ROM
cpc464-rom-disassembly.notes: Richard Lloyd's CPC464 operating-system ROM disassembly, generated with Disark then hand-finished and labelled for reassembly with MAXAM.

cpc6128-firmware-source.title: Amstrad CPC6128 Firmware
cpc6128-firmware-source.notes: Bread80's relocatable/modifiable firmware unassembly; assembled output is checked against and intended to exactly match the original ROM.

ancient-legacy-decompressor.title: Ancient
ancient-legacy-decompressor.notes: Modern C++ decompressor/library for a broad collection of legacy compression formats used heavily on Amiga, Atari and other 1980s/1990s systems. It cleanly reimplements many historically awkward or undocumented algorithms, including PowerPacker, XPK backends, CrunchMania, StoneCracker, RNC, DMS, ByteKiller and numerous clones, and tests implementations against a large corpus of legacy files.

ancipital-c64.title: Ancipital
ancipital-c64.notes: Reverse-engineered commented source; README explicitly states the game compiles and plays.

another-world-js-dos.title: Another World JS
source_language: Another World DOS demo/anniversary game data
another-world-js-dos.notes: Browser port interprets the game’s 26 bytecode opcodes and converts DOS demo/anniversary assets. Its Amiga palette option does not imply Amiga disk-data support. This is a distinct browser implementation alongside the tracked raw(gl) engine.

another-world-vm-tools.title: Another World VM Tools
another-world-vm-tools.notes: Pure-Rust Another World VM resource unpacker, bytecode disassembler and assembler across several releases including the Amiga, with OFS ADF extraction and byte-identical bytecode round-trip documented. Byte-identical VM bytecode round-trip does not imply an Amiga executable rebuild.

another-world-cross-port-archaeology.title: Another World — cross-port archaeology
source_language: original release executables and game data
another-world-cross-port-archaeology.notes: Active comparative archaeology of Another World releases, with checksum provenance, extractors and bytecode disassemblies. Includes the original Amiga lineage. Original game fixtures are expected from a separate sibling archive; do not infer that every release has been completely decoded. The CPU fields are intentionally not applicable: the cross-port comparison currently disassembles the game's virtual-machine bytecode and produces research artifacts, rather than reconstructing a native host instruction set.

another-world-cross-port-reconstruction.title: Another World — cross-port source reconstruction
another-world-cross-port-reconstruction.notes: Active work toward one conditional source tree for multiple release lineages, including Chahi's 1991 Amiga bytecode. README and PLAN document byte-identical round trips for 29 levels across five ports. Current outputs are Another World VM bytecode resources: engine binary reconstruction and whole-port packaging are explicitly outside the present scope, so native source and target CPUs are not applicable. Depends on sibling archaeology and external VMTools.

apple-ii-system-software-cmosher.title: Apple ][ System Software Source Code
apple-ii-system-software-cmosher.display_title: Apple II system software and DOS — reverse-engineered source
apple-ii-system-software-cmosher.notes: Christopher Mosher describes this package as reverse-engineered source code for Apple II series system ROMs and DOS. Exact build equivalence, supported ROM variants, and runnable hardware minimums still need review.

apple-ii-desktop-a2stuff.title: Apple II DeskTop
apple-ii-desktop-a2stuff.display_title: Apple II DeskTop — disassembly and enhanced ProDOS GUI

runtime_profiles.name: Apple II DeskTop on 8-bit Apples
runtime_profiles.notes: README lists 8-bit Apple II models and clones with 128 KiB; mouse is optional.

evidence.excerpt: 8-bit Apples and clones with 128k of memory

apple-ii-desktop-a2stuff.notes: The project disassembles and extends Mouse Desk / Apple II DeskTop, a ProDOS 8 GUI. Its README identifies 128 KiB 8-bit Apple systems and clones and links build/running instructions and disk images. No narrower CPU or chipset minimum is asserted.

apple2-plus-rom-james-davis.title: Apple II Plus ROM
apple2-plus-rom-james-davis.display_title: Apple II Plus ROM — full-system annotated disassembly
apple2-plus-rom-james-davis.notes: James P. Davis independently annotated the Apple II Plus emulator ROM image across $C000–$FFFF, identifying errors in the image and extensively editing/integrating earlier Apple, Sander-Cederlof, McFadden and other reference material. The listing explicitly credits those predecessors; it is not presented as original Apple source. SourceGen project file is linked from the ROM index.

applevision-apple2-6502disassembly.title: AppleVision
applevision-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of Bob Bishop's AppleVision demo, split into its Integer BASIC and embedded machine-language components, with commented listings and SourceGen project files/binaries.

follin-music-source-archive.title: ARCHIVE-FOLLIN
follin-music-source-archive.display_title: Follin music archive — recovered C64 and CPC/Spectrum source
subjects: Tim and Geoff Follin music and sound drivers
follin-music-source-archive.notes: Recovered Tim and Geoff Follin period music and driver source from Tatung Einstein floppies. Author reverse-engineered a 6502 detokenizer and began modern Z80 assembler builds for AY music examples; this is source recovery, not a game disassembly.

archon-c64-reconstruction.title: Archon — C64 source reconstruction
archon-c64-reconstruction.notes: Reverse-engineered reconstruction of the C64 Archon game logic as extensively commented, relocatable Kick Assembler source. Original addresses are retained as documentation while variables, constants and routines are renamed and reorganised for readability rather than binary identity.

arkanoid-msx-disassembly-mcolom.title: Arkanoid
arkanoid-msx-disassembly-mcolom.notes: Manually annotated disassembly of Taito's MSX Arkanoid. The source header documents its z80dasm origin, z80asm rebuild command and the SHA-1 expected from the rebuilt ROM.

armalyte-c64-analyser.title: Armalyte
armalyte-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Armalyte directory contains a large Analysis.json annotation database (~803 KB) plus saved analyser/emulator state and configuration. This is tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

asteroids-arcade-6502disassembly.title: Asteroids
asteroids-arcade-6502disassembly.notes: SourceGen reconstruction of Asteroids rev 4 based on earlier Computer Archeology/Nick Mikstas analysis, covering the 6502 program and vector-generator command ROM. The project adds a DVG disassembler, project files/binaries and binary-construction instructions.

atari-osb-ntsc-source-restoration.title: Atari 8-bit OS-B NTSC ROM
atari-osb-ntsc-source-restoration.display_title: Atari OS-B NTSC — paper-source restoration and verified ROM build
subjects: Atari 400/800 Operating System Revision B NTSC ROM

runtime_profiles.name: OS-B NTSC ROM
runtime_profiles.notes: The primary README identifies this 10 KiB OS-B NTSC ROM for Atari 400 and 800 machines; no RAM minimum is stated.

atari-osb-ntsc-source-restoration.notes: Restores Atari's published OS-B source listing by scanning, OCR and proofreading, then converts it to ca65 syntax. The Makefile compares the generated listing bytes with the paper-derived path and checks the result against the included 10 KiB ROM.

atari-file-forge-workbench.title: Atari File Forge
atari-file-forge-workbench.display_title: Atari File Forge — ST disk and ROM analysis workbench
source_language: ST floppy, hard-drive, ROM and 68000 binaries
atari-file-forge-workbench.notes: Web and Linux workbench for Atari ST through Falcon floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents GEMDOS editing, AHDI/ICD partitions, STX protection reports, flux containers and 68000 analysis. It is host-side tooling, not a native Atari ST application; the Amiga File Forge sibling handles a different platform and formats.

atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.title: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.upstream_name: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.display_title: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
subjects: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.notes: Comparative annotated BIOS/XBIOS assembly listings for TOS 2.06, TOS 3.06 and the STBook ROM, plus STBook ROM disk and POWER.PRG analysis. The README says the listings integrate comments from available original source; they should not be mistaken for a wholly new byte-exact ROM reconstruction.

atari-st-copy-protections.title: Atari ST Copy Protections
atari-st-copy-protections.notes: Reverse-engineered disk protections from multiple Atari ST applications and games.

vscode-atari-st-dev-dgis.title: Atari ST Dev — VS Code debugger and toolchain
vscode-atari-st-dev-dgis.upstream_name: Atari ST Dev — VS Code debugger and toolchain
vscode-atari-st-dev-dgis.display_title: Atari ST Dev — VS Code debugger and toolchain
vscode-atari-st-dev-dgis.notes: Extension bundles a cross-toolchain and Hatari for ST/TT/Falcon development, with live CPU, memory, hardware and graphics inspection through cppdbg/GDB. README notes TRAP step-over and GEMDOS filename limitations; this is development and analysis tooling, not a reconstructed historic program.

atari-st-floppy-toolkit-gem.title: Atari ST Floppy Image Toolkit GEM
atari-st-floppy-toolkit-gem.upstream_name: Atari ST Floppy Image Toolkit GEM
atari-st-floppy-toolkit-gem.display_title: Atari ST Floppy Image Toolkit — disk and sector inspector
source_language: ST/MSA floppy images and file formats
atari-st-floppy-toolkit-gem.notes: Browser-style GEM workbench claims ST/MSA floppy browsing, FAT12 extraction and sector editing. This entry records those published capabilities without asserting the broader README's emulator and packer features have been independently tested.

atari-st-reverse-engineer-skill.title: Atari ST Reverse-Engineering Skill
atari-st-reverse-engineer-skill.display_title: Atari ST Reverse-Engineering Skill — 68000 binary-analysis pipeline
atari-st-reverse-engineer-skill.notes: Claude Code skill with a bundled Python Capstone disassembler, Atari PRG/TOS header parsing, GEMDOS/BIOS/XBIOS/GEM call annotation, data-region heuristics and an annotation/documentation pipeline. README describes intended workflow; no independent run was verified.

stbook-diagnostic-cartridge-analysis.title: Atari STBook/STylus diagnostic cartridge analysis
stbook-diagnostic-cartridge-analysis.notes: Annotated disassembly and detailed test-by-test analysis of STBook/STylus diagnostic cartridge firmware, including memory maps, LED fault codes and motherboard checks. Repository also archives ROM images and IDA projects; no rebuild claim.

jotd-atari-tetris-amiga.title: Atari Tetris — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: AGA Amiga
runtime_profiles.notes: README explicitly describes the transcode as for 68020/AGA Amiga.

evidence.excerpt: for 68020/AGA amiga

jotd-atari-tetris-amiga.notes: Transcode of Atari's Tetris arcade version for 68020/AGA Amiga; README explicitly credits jotd with 6502→68000 conversion.

tos100fr-ghidra.title: Atari TOS 1.00 French Ghidra analysis
tos100fr-ghidra.notes: Ghidra archive of the French TOS 1.00 192 KB ROM, intended to document internals, find bugs and support Atari ST software. README documents importing the archive; no reassembled ROM or byte-identical output is claimed.

tos14-uk-disassembly.title: Atari TOS 1.4 UK hand disassembly
tos14-uk-disassembly.notes: Hand disassembly of the UK TOS 1.4 ROM. GNU m68k assembler and a Python preprocessor are used; byte-identical reassembly is an explicit project goal, not a verified build result. The master README identifies the wip2 branch for work; the later wip3 branch contains additional BIOS disassembly and is tracked for activity.

tos3x-atari-tos-rom-reconstruction.title: Atari TOS 2.06/3.06 ROM reconstruction
tos3x-atari-tos-rom-reconstruction.notes: Reassembles scattered and incomplete historical Atari TOS sources into buildable TOS 2.06/2.08/3.06 ROM trees. Includes disassembler listings, restored Alcyon tools, and a make check target that compares generated images with reference ROMs; byte-exact success is not assumed for every configuration.

fighter-pilot-atari8-sarnau.title: Atari-Fighter-Pilot
fighter-pilot-atari8-sarnau.display_title: Fighter Pilot — Atari 8-bit Lenslok/cassette reverse engineering

runtime_profiles.name: Atari 8-bit release
runtime_profiles.notes: The project README explicitly names Atari 400/800/600XL/800XL/130XE machines with at least 48K.

evidence.excerpt: Fighter Pilot for the Atari 400/800/600XL/800XL/130XE with at least 48K.

fighter-pilot-atari8-sarnau.notes: Analysis of the protected Atari cassette release, including media recovery, block extraction, Lenslok study and scripts that generate protected and decoded XEX forms.

atari-hd-image-builder.upstream_name: atari-hd — Atari ST disk image builder

atari-hd-image-builder.notes: TUI and CLI build raw Atari ST bootable disk images; implements AHDI, PPDRIVER and HDDRIVER partition layouts. README states byte-level validation against ICDFMT/PPTOSDOS reference disks. Host utility, not a recovered TOS system source.

jumpman-atari8-sarnau.title: Atari-Jumpman
jumpman-atari8-sarnau.notes: Independent preservation-oriented analysis of the Atari 8-bit Jumpman disk format, protection scheme, level data, graphics and per-level enemy logic. The repository includes a from-scratch 6502 emulator and ANTIC renderer used to boot the game and reproduce all 30 level maps; it is analysis tooling around the original game rather than a claimed source reconstruction.

goonies-atari8-sarnau.title: Atari-The-Goonies
goonies-atari8-sarnau.notes: Reverse engineering of the Atari 800 release from its cassette image, with extracted binaries, architecture documentation and reusable Ghidra setup/annotation scripts. The README describes the project as a complete reverse-engineering effort while its own coverage table still marks some graphics, sound/data tables and dynamically loaded level code as only partially analysed, so the tracker does not overstate completion.

atari-m68000-disasmb-codaway.title: AtariM68000_DisAsmb — Atari ST disassembler
atari-m68000-disasmb-codaway.notes: README describes a C disassembler that follows instructions and branches from the executable entry point; author used it to investigate copy protection and says output is imperfect. Build and runtime unverified.

athena-spectrum-analyser.title: Athena
athena-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Athena directory contains an approximately 534 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

atic-atac-pobtastic-spectrum.title: Atic Atac — Pobtastic disassembly
atic-atac-pobtastic-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

attack-mutant-camels-c64.title: Attack of the Mutant Camels
attack-mutant-camels-c64.notes: Repository contains a byte-exact labelled/commented reconstruction plus a separately restructured version.

attack-mutant-camels-mwenge.title: Attack of the Mutant Camels — 8-bit reconstructions
attack-mutant-camels-mwenge.upstream_name: Attack of the Mutant Camels — 8-bit reconstructions

subjects: Attack of the Mutant Camels — 8-bit reconstructions
attack-mutant-camels-mwenge.notes: Llamasoft Source Project reconstruction of the C64 and Atari 8-bit versions of Attack of the Mutant Camels. The same repository also preserves the separately available original Konix work-in-progress source, which is not treated as reverse-engineering evidence.

audio-sculpture-st-ipl-analysis.title: Audio Sculpture 1.5 — IPL protection analysis
audio-sculpture-st-ipl-analysis.notes: Project-specific Hatari debugging walkthrough and files for analyzing Audio Sculpture 1.5 IPL protection, especially physical track/sector checks. README refers software anti-debugger detail to the Son Shu Shi analysis; no standalone reconstructed application is claimed.

auf-wiedersehen-monty-spectrum-analyser.title: Auf Wiedersehen Monty
auf-wiedersehen-monty-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Auf Wiedersehen Monty — ZX Spectrum analyser project
auf-wiedersehen-monty-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The aufmonty directory contains an approximately 2538 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus four custom Lua viewers/analysis scripts. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

albank1-avenger-c64-disassembly.title: Avenger
albank1-avenger-c64-disassembly.notes: Ultimax cartridge listing; header identifies lives at $3D and changes DEC to LDA for infinite lives. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

aviator-bbc-micro-moxon.title: Aviator — BBC Micro reconstruction
aviator-bbc-micro-moxon.notes: Geoff Crammond's Aviator reconstructed by hand from the BBC Micro release binary; build verification reports the compiled binary matching the original.

back-to-skool-spectrum.title: Back to Skool
back-to-skool-spectrum.notes: Complete maintained RAM disassembly; changelog records first public release in 2001.

backgammon-fds-to-nes-g0me3.title: Backgammon
backgammon-fds-to-nes-g0me3.notes: Assembly reconstruction and conversion of Nintendo's FDS Backgammon into a NES cartridge image. The repository separates demo, final, main, game, computer-player and sound modules and includes a build path; commit history records reaching a fully working conversion, but this audit did not independently execute it. The cartridge output is not a byte-identical FDS rebuild.

jotd-bad-dudes-amiga.title: Bad Dudes vs. DragonNinja — Amiga arcade port
jotd-bad-dudes-amiga.display_title: Bad Dudes vs. DragonNinja — Amiga arcade port
jotd-bad-dudes-amiga.notes: AGA Amiga port that runs the original arcade 68000 code with patches redirecting graphics and sound operations to Amiga hardware rather than retranscoding the game.

jotd-bagman-amiga.title: Bagman — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-bagman-amiga.notes: Bagman was resourced from the Z80 arcade game; the Amiga version uses approximately 99% transcoded original code. README credits jotd with Z80 reverse engineering and Z80→68k transcode.

balloon-fight-nes-luigiblood.title: Balloon Fight
balloon-fight-nes-luigiblood.notes: USA NES Balloon Fight disassembly. Primary build instructions assemble the PRG or a complete iNES image with ARM9's bass fork, inserting a user-provided original CHR ROM.

vs-sr-cd32-banshee.title: Banshee — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-banshee.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Banshee. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

batalyx-c64.title: Batalyx
batalyx-c64.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1986 C64 game Batalyx. The current source compiles and plays; character/sprite data is separated while game-logic labelling remains in progress.

batman-spectrum-analyser.title: Batman
batman-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Batman directory contains a 2790 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and Skool source, exported assembly and multiple Lua viewers/formatters. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

batman-return-joker-gb-mixup.title: Batman: Return of the Joker
batman-return-joker-gb-mixup.display_title: Batman: Return of the Joker — Game Boy JavaScript reconstruction
batman-return-joker-gb-mixup.notes: Mixup hand-translates the Game Boy ROM disassembly into JavaScript and reports complete title-to-credits behavior checked frame by frame against PyBoy. Behavioral bit-exactness is not identical original-platform binary output.

batman-the-movie-amiga.title: Batman: The Movie
batman-the-movie-amiga.notes: Extensive reconstruction covering all five levels plus loader, boot, graphics, sound and support components.

battle-squadron-amiga-recomp-crownpark.title: Battle Squadron
battle-squadron-amiga-recomp-crownpark.display_title: Battle Squadron — Amiga overlay disassembly and recompilation
subjects: Battle Squadron: The Destruction of the Barrax Empire

execution_paths.name: Playable reference runner
execution_paths.notes: Runs original 68000 loader and game code in Musashi with a Battle Squadron-focused OCS compatibility host.

execution_paths.name: No-Musashi recompilation preview
execution_paths.notes: Runs translated code through live combat without a guest CPU interpreter; full audio sequencing and unreached paths remain unfinished.

tags: Battle Squadron: The Destruction of the Barrax Empire
battle-squadron-amiga-recomp-crownpark.notes: Analyzes a user-supplied Amiga WHDLoad install, its BOND-compressed overlays and three partially decoded 68000 modules that reassemble byte-for-byte. A playable Musashi/OCS host still executes original game code; a separate native no-Musashi translation has progressed into live combat but is not a finished whole-game recompilation. Distinct from the tracked Battle Squadron music replayer.

rkplay-battlesquadron-music.title: Battle Squadron music replay — rkplay
source_language: Battle Squadron Amiga music and replay routine
rkplay-battlesquadron-music.notes: README describes a reverse engineered replayer for Ron Klaren’s Battle Squadron Amiga music, with WAV/raw PCM output. C source, Makefile and song format module present; fidelity to original routine unverified.

battletech-c64-static-recomp.title: BattleTech: The Crescent Hawk's Inception — C64 static recompilation
battletech-c64-static-recomp.display_title: BattleTech: The Crescent Hawk's Inception — C64 static recompilation
battletech-c64-static-recomp.notes: Native Windows static recompilation of BattleTech: The Crescent Hawk's Inception. The original executable paths were analysed into a fixed generated C catalog of 21,637 exact blocks; the production runtime executes only admitted blocks and supplies game-specific C64 memory, VIC-II, CIA, SID and 1541/IEC/GCR behaviour without an emulator fallback.

battlezone-arcade-6502disassembly.title: Battlezone
battlezone-arcade-6502disassembly.notes: Detailed Battlezone rev 2 disassembly covering the 6502 program, vector-generator ROM commands and math-box interface, with SourceGen files/binaries plus extensive documentation of 3D objects, rendering, hardware interaction and revision differences.

battlezone-spectrum.title: Battlezone
battlezone-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

batty-spectrum.title: Batty
batty-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

bbc-basic-ii-acornaeology.notes: Annotated BBC BASIC II interpreter ROM disassembly; README documents beebasm byte-for-byte reassembly and CI verification.

albank1-bcs-quest-for-tires-c64-disassem.title: BC’s Quest for Tires
albank1-bcs-quest-for-tires-c64-disassem.display_title: BC’s Quest for Tires — C64 cartridge disassembly
albank1-bcs-quest-for-tires-c64-disassem.notes: Cartridge listing includes cold/warm vectors, character data and location of the lives value. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

beebjit-bbc-emulator.title: beebjit
beebjit-bbc-emulator.display_title: beebjit — BBC Micro JIT emulator, debugger & preservation test bench
source_language: BBC Micro disk and tape images
beebjit-bbc-emulator.notes: BBC Micro/Master emulator focused on very fast 6502 JIT execution while retaining enough hardware fidelity for original protected media. The README documents FSD/HFE handling, 8271/1770 emulation, deterministic capture/replay, experimental rewind and a built-in 6502 debugger, including preservation-oriented protected-media examples.

beermon-045-reconstructed.title: BeerMon v0.45 — reconstructed Amiga monitor
beermon-045-reconstructed.notes: Carnivore / BeerMacht / TRSI is credited for the historical BeerMon v0.45 monitor and debugger. Volker Schwaberow's reconstructed Moni.s explicitly selects mc68030, uses the 68020/68030 MSP/CACR/CAAR control-register path, and contains guarded 68040 and FPU probes. The source is therefore recorded at the explicitly documented m68k family level while m68030 records the reconstruction/output assembler mode, not a claimed minimum runnable Amiga. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established.

beneath-steel-sky-delirium-cracktro.title: Beneath a Steel Sky — Delirium cracktro reconstruction
beneath-steel-sky-delirium-cracktro.upstream_name: Delirium Beneath a Steel Sky cracktro
beneath-steel-sky-delirium-cracktro.display_title: Beneath a Steel Sky — Delirium cracktro reconstruction
subjects: Delirium Beneath a Steel Sky cracktro
beneath-steel-sky-delirium-cracktro.notes: Wayne Mendoza / Delirium is credited for the historical Delirium Beneath a Steel Sky cracktro. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header credits Wayne Mendoza and identifies Volker Schwaberow's reconstruction; annotated Exec and custom-chip offsets follow. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

berzerk-arcade-scott-tunstall.title: Berzerk — original Z80 arcade disassembly
berzerk-arcade-scott-tunstall.notes: Scott Tunstall's annotated original arcade Berzerk Z80 reverse engineering; the listing credits MAME debugger and documents shared logic found by translating recovered Frenzy 8085 source to Z80. JOTD's repository carries a copy and no independently evidenced Amiga conversion. Build identity remains unverified.

betrayal-at-krondor-dos-byte-match.title: Betrayal at Krondor
betrayal-at-krondor-dos-byte-match.display_title: Betrayal at Krondor — byte-matched DOS source reconstruction
betrayal-at-krondor-dos-byte-match.notes: Reconstructs the 1993 game from DOS binaries and reports full byte matches for both 1.00 floppy and 1.02 CD-ROM releases. Build recreates a Borland/TASM toolchain and requires user-supplied original game files for play; project also includes a browser-based asset viewer. The author says source cleanup and documentation remain ongoing.

budge-3d-module-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Bill Budge 3-D Graphics System and Game Tool
budge-3d-module-apple2-6502disassembly.upstream_name: Bill Budge 3-D Graphics System and Game Tool

subjects: Bill Budge 3-D Graphics System and Game Tool
budge-3d-module-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of a generated module from Bill Budge's 3-D Graphics System and Game Tool, covering its scale/rotate/position/draw library, page flipping, XOR rendering and character-generator support.

bird-strike-bbc-micro-fixed-disassembly.title: Bird Strike
bird-strike-bbc-micro-fixed-disassembly.display_title: Bird Strike — BBC Micro disassembly and crash repair
bird-strike-bbc-micro-fixed-disassembly.notes: Disassembled BIRDSK2 with WFDis/Beebdis and reassembled it with BeebAsm. Diagnoses and repairs graphical corruption after level 13 and a crash at level 23; includes playable binary, disk image and emulator save states. Later comments incorporate labels from the author's original sources.

bloodwych.title: Bloodwych / Extended Levels
bloodwych.display_title: Bloodwych — Amiga source reconstruction / Extended Levels
bloodwych.notes: Re-sourcing of Bloodwych and Extended Levels with growing labels, extracted data and supporting tools.

blues-brothers-engine-cyxx.title: Blues Brothers — reimplemented Titus game engine
blues-brothers-engine-cyxx.upstream_name: Blues Brothers — reimplemented Titus game engine
blues-brothers-engine-cyxx.display_title: Blues Brothers — reimplemented Titus game engine
blues-brothers-engine-cyxx.notes: Rewritten engine for Blues Brothers, Jukebox Adventure and Prehistorik 2. The Blues Brothers path accepts original Amiga or DOS data; the other two documented data paths require DOS files. README distinguishes gameplay changes from the original DOS executables. Source CPU is not applicable because the rewrite consumes game data and reimplements behavior rather than translating or reconstructing native executable instructions.

bobby-bearing-spectrum-analyser.title: Bobby Bearing
bobby-bearing-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Bobby Bearing — ZX Spectrum analyser project
bobby-bearing-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The BobbyBearing directory contains a 1445 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and exported Z80 assembly. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

boing-amicus-amiga-reconstruction.title: Boing Ball AMICUS — Amiga demo reconstruction
boing-amicus-amiga-reconstruction.upstream_name: Boing Ball AMICUS — Amiga demo reconstruction
boing-amicus-amiga-reconstruction.display_title: Boing Ball AMICUS — Amiga demo reconstruction
boing-amicus-amiga-reconstruction.notes: Source reconstructs the AMICUS Disk 9 variant from Harry Sintonen’s disassembly. README describes working vasm/vlink and FS-UAE path requiring separately supplied ROM, OS headers and mathtrans.library. Two deliberate deviations mean resulting build is not strictly byte-identical.

boing-amicus-browser-port.title: Boing Ball AMICUS — browser port
boing-amicus-browser-port.notes: Standalone browser port derived from the separate mbackschat/amiga-boing analyzed AMICUS assembly. Uses Canvas2D and WebAudio; live demo and npm build documented. Distinct implementation from the Amiga source reconstruction.

bomber-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Bomber
bomber-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Andy McFadden's disassembly of the original 1978 non-score-keeping Apple II Bomber release. The project publishes a disassembly listing plus SourceGen project files and binaries and documents the game's pixel-level object representation.

booty-spectrum.title: Booty
booty-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

borland-hlp-atari-st-converter.title: Borland HLP — Atari ST format converter

borland-hlp-atari-st-converter.display_title: Borland HLP — Atari ST format converter
borland-hlp-atari-st-converter.notes: Independent Python converter and byte-level specification for Borland Help System 2.0 .HLP files, outputting HTML, Markdown or text. Related th-otto/pc_help reconstructs original compiler tools; this is a separate decoder implementation.

bosconian-amiga-jotd.title: Bosconian — Amiga 68k translation
bosconian-amiga-jotd.notes: Project-specific Bosconian Z80 listing and 76 KB Amiga driver contain a named Bosconian core/high-score path. README and driver retain Rally-X template text; this is real in-progress source work, but successful assembly and playable output remain unverified.

bruce-lee-atari8-disassembly.title: Bruce Lee
bruce-lee-atari8-disassembly.notes: Sparse repository documentation, but the primary engine.asm is a substantial annotated 6502 listing that names Bruce/Yamo/Ninja state, Atari display-list, POKEY audio and player/missile register behavior. No reproducible build or exact-output claim was found.

bruce-lee-spectrum.title: Bruce Lee
bruce-lee-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

bubble-bobble-c64-analyser.title: Bubble Bobble
bubble-bobble-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Bubble Bobble directory contains an Analysis.json annotation database (69 KiB), saved analysis state (40 KiB), emulator save state and project configuration. Tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

bubble-bobble-c64-rebb64.title: Bubble Bobble
bubble-bobble-c64-rebb64.display_title: Bubble Bobble — exact C64 source reconstruction
bubble-bobble-c64-rebb64.notes: Author reports all executable C64 game code converted to documented cc65 assembly, with make verify comparing the rebuilt raw PRG byte for byte against the original. Raw image needs a startup/packing step for auto-run; labelled relocatability is still in progress. Distinct source reconstruction from the tracked 8-Bit Analysers annotation project.

bubble-ghost-atari-st.title: Bubble Ghost
bubble-ghost-atari-st.notes: 132 named functions reconstructed and verified; reconstructed BUBBLE.PRG is play-tested under Hatari. One secondary program remains outside the reconstruction.

buggy-boy-atari-st.title: Buggy Boy
buggy-boy-atari-st.notes: Readable C reconstruction with function-level verification against original 68000 execution.

bumpys-arcade-fantasy-dos-decompilation.title: Bumpy's Arcade Fantasy
bumpys-arcade-fantasy-dos-decompilation.display_title: Bumpy's Arcade Fantasy — DOS decompilation and playable build
bumpys-arcade-fantasy-dos-decompilation.notes: Reconstructed C engine for the 1992 DOS English release, with format decoders and documentation. Two Open Watcom targets: structure-faithful BUMPY.EXE is link-only and byte-compared but not run; BUMPYP.EXE adds a host layer and plays in DOSBox with user-supplied game files. Author explicitly describes Claude-led work; no byte-identical final build claim.

jotd-burgertime-amiga.title: BurgerTime — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-burgertime-amiga.notes: BurgerTime arcade transcode for Amiga; README explicitly credits game reverse engineering and 6502→68000 conversion and states the game uses original code/sound/graphics.

c64-re-agent-marcellmajor.title: C64-RE Agent
c64-re-agent-marcellmajor.notes: LangGraph-based research workbench accepts a 64 KB C64 memory dump and question, combines static Capstone disassembly with optional VICE MCP introspection and maintains an evidence-backed knowledge base. Separate from the tracked C64RE/TRX64 projects.

c64re-mcp-workbench.title: C64RE
c64re-mcp-workbench.display_title: C64RE — MCP-assisted C64 software analysis workbench
c64re-mcp-workbench.notes: C64-specific disk/cartridge/PRG forensic and semantic-disassembly workbench with MCP interface and project knowledge graph; verification workflow assembles and compares bytes. README states emulation runtime is supplied by the separate TRX64 project, so C64RE itself should not be catalogued as an emulator.

caverns-freitag-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Caverns of Freitag
caverns-freitag-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Caverns of Freitag — Apple II mixed-language disassembly
caverns-freitag-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Caverns of Freitag archaeology covering the Applesoft programs, machine-language graphics/ampersand routines, map and object data, with a SourceGen project set for the binaries.

cd32launch-jotd.title: CD32Launch
cd32launch-jotd.notes: Runs OS-compliant Amiga games with CD32 joypad remapping, memory/chipset downgrading, VBR patching and optional small patchlist slaves. Its readme contains copied CD32Load option text after the introductory launch-specific section; avoid treating those options as independently verified CD32Launch behavior.

cd32load-jotd.title: CD32Load
cd32load-jotd.notes: CD32/IDE loader for WHDLoad slaves. README reports selected A600 installs with 1 MB chip RAM and testing on real CD32 and A1200; this is game dependent, not a universal 1 MB minimum.

cdtv-os-235-patch.title: CDTV OS 2.35 patch
cdtv-os-235-patch.notes: Public bsdiff patch transforms a user-supplied Commodore 2.30 Extended ROM into unofficial 2.35 images. Author says original modules were reconstructed as byte-matching assembly after Ghidra/vasm analysis; that source and complete ROM images are not published, so exactness is an upstream claim rather than independently verified here.

amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.title: CDTV U62 — front-panel controller firmware analysis
amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.upstream_name: CDTV U62 — front-panel controller firmware analysis
amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.display_title: CDTV U62 — front-panel controller firmware analysis
amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.notes: Annotated LC6554H U62 controller ROM listing with address/raw bytes and a Python disassembler. Covers CDTV front panel, remote-control link and CD-drive behavior. Listing is expressly for reading, not assembling; one BANK interpretation remains unproven.

cdtv-u75-rom-disassembly.title: CDTV U75 controller ROM disassembly
cdtv-u75-rom-disassembly.notes: 6500/1 U75 controller ROM disassembly documents IR remote, keyboard and CDTV front-panel protocols. Original pre-production ROM dump is credited to CDTV Land (2022); this repository analyzes that dump rather than claiming to have made it.

cdtvload-jotd.title: CDTVLoad
cdtvload-jotd.notes: Loader for non-DOS games from CD using WHDLoad slaves. Source contains an IRA-derived partial reversal of an earlier Psygore loader; no general build or runtime result established.

centipede-arcade-6502disassembly.title: Centipede
centipede-arcade-6502disassembly.notes: Centipede rev 4 arcade ROM disassembly with SourceGen project files/binaries, binary-construction instructions and substantial analysis of graphics, entity behavior, difficulty progression and cocktail-mode display handling.

championship-lode-runner-c64.title: Championship Lode Runner
championship-lode-runner-c64.notes: Commented reconstructed source including copy protection; repository description states the goal is a bit-for-bit identical recreation.

championship-manager-italia-st-decompila.title: Championship Manager Italia — ST reconstruction
championship-manager-italia-st-decompila.notes: Reconstructed the hard-drive install executable in assembly using Ghidra and Fred’s disassembler. Author documents a VASM build tested in Hatari, with code approximately 99% covered and an optional copy-protection bypass; rebuilt program is explicitly not 100% accurate to the original. The CMAN93 folder contains English 1993 game binaries, without a second published source reconstruction.

chaos-guesser-szeliga-spectrum.title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Guesser/szeliga
chaos-guesser-szeliga-spectrum.display_title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Guesser/szeliga
chaos-guesser-szeliga-spectrum.notes: Incomplete commented Chaos disassembly by Guesser and szeliga, preserved in Michael Cook's archive and rendered at zxnet.co.uk.

chaos-lewis-lane-spectrum.title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Lewis Lane
chaos-lewis-lane-spectrum.display_title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Lewis Lane
chaos-lewis-lane-spectrum.notes: Modern annotated Chaos disassembly with extensive engine/data documentation and explicit Claude Code assistance.

chase-hq-spectrum.title: Chase H.Q.
chase-hq-spectrum.notes: Function-by-function readable C reconstruction developed alongside the Spectrum disassembly.

chase-hq-spectrum-analyser.title: Chase H.Q.
chase-hq-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Chase H.Q. — ZX Spectrum analyser project
chase-hq-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The ChaseHQ directory contains an approximately 1193 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus a custom Lua viewer script. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

chiller-c64-unorig.title: Chiller
chiller-c64-unorig.notes: Reverse-engineered/decompiled C64 Chiller source. Current documentation says the project has moved to Regenerator 2000 for analysis and preserves/analyzes both known soundtrack variants.

chip-and-dale-2-nes-g0me3.title: Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers 2
chip-and-dale-2-nes-g0me3.display_title: Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers 2 (NES) — Back From Source
chip-and-dale-2-nes-g0me3.notes: Back From Source reconstruction with separate program banks, script/text material and DASM assembly scripts producing a NES image. RetroRE classifies the disassembly as partial; no byte-exact equivalence or minimum hardware profile is asserted.

choplifter-apple2-reconstruction.title: ChoplifterReverse
choplifter-apple2-reconstruction.display_title: Choplifter — Apple II clean-room source reconstruction
choplifter-apple2-reconstruction.notes: Full clean-room reverse engineering of the 1982 Apple II Choplifter from the disk binary alone. The reconstructed game code is documented and builds/runs; the game portion is described as binary-identical, while the original custom floppy loader was intentionally replaced with a new ProDOS loader, so the complete produced disk is not treated as byte-exact.

chuchu-rocket-atari-st-reforged.title: Chu Chu Rocket
chuchu-rocket-atari-st-reforged.display_title: Chu Chu Rocket — Atari ST byte-matched disassembly
chuchu-rocket-atari-st-reforged.notes: Complete, named 68000 source for Reservoir Gods' Atari ST Chu Chu Rocket 1.18 LITE. Default build reproduces CHUCHU.TOS and CHUCHU.LNK byte-identically; optional Reforged optimizations and fixes deliberately differ. README reports tests in Hatari and on a real Mega STe and explicitly credits Claude assistance. This is distinct from the original game's development source.

chzpart-atari-disk.title: CHZ Atari Disk Partitioning Tool
chzpart-atari-disk.notes: Partitions Atari-compatible disks on hardware with XHDI or prepares disk-image files on other systems. Supports TOS-era layouts and FAT16 initialization; this is original modern tooling rather than a reverse-engineered historical utility.

classic-mac-rom-source-reconstruction.title: Classic Macintosh ROM source reconstruction
classic-mac-rom-source-reconstruction.notes: Fully commented buildable source tree for five classic Macintosh ROM variants (128K, 512K and three Plus ROMs). The build explicitly verifies all five outputs as bit-identical to their reference ROMs.

cobra-spectrum-analyser.title: Cobra
cobra-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Cobra directory contains an approximately 2645 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus project configuration and graphics metadata. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

coco-image-viewer-atari-tiny.title: CoCo Image Viewer
coco-image-viewer-atari-tiny.display_title: CoCo Image Viewer — Atari ST Tiny picture decoder
coco-image-viewer-atari-tiny.notes: Cross-platform viewer/converter primarily for TRS-80 Color Computer formats; separately documents and implements Atari ST Tiny compressed image decoding across low, medium and high resolutions. The ST record is limited to Tiny graphics support, not general Atari disk filesystem coverage.

commando-c64.title: Commando
commando-c64.notes: Fully commented disassembly of the original Commando is preserved on the repo's orig branch; default branch adds the Commando 2084 modification.

commando-spectrum.title: Commando
commando-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Not finished.

jotd-commando-amiga.title: Commando — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-commando-amiga.notes: Capcom Commando port for Amiga AGA; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode, graphics conversion and sound conversion.

c64-mist64-dos1541.title: Commodore 1541 DOS ROM
c64-mist64-dos1541.display_title: 1541 DOS — historical source restoration and ROM build
c64-mist64-dos1541.notes: Modern cc65 adaptation of reconstructed original Commodore DOS source, preserving original comments and symbols across 1540–1541-II revisions. Builds differ at two checksum bytes and one signature byte; this is historical source restoration, not a fresh binary-derived disassembly.

c64-mist64-c64rom.title: Commodore 64 BASIC and KERNAL
c64-mist64-c64rom.notes: Original Commodore BASIC/KERNAL sources reorganized into editable cc65 segments while retaining the original symbols and comments. README reports exact BASIC 901226-01 and KERNAL 901227-03 binary outputs; lineage is recovered original source, not binary-derived disassembly.

compunet-amiga-client.title: Compunet Amiga client

runtime_profiles.name: Compunet Reborn TCP/IP client
runtime_profiles.os: Kickstart 2.04 or later; bsdsocket-compatible TCP/IP stack

evidence.excerpt: The reconstructed client runs online with a bsdsocket TCP/IP stack on Kickstart 2.04+.

compunet-amiga-client.notes: Recovered 1989 native client reconstructed as vbcc C; modem/cnet.device communication replaced with TCP/IP. The repository also hosts C64/server clients; this record tracks the Amiga directory only.

contact-sam-cruise-spectrum.title: Contact Sam Cruise
contact-sam-cruise-spectrum.notes: Complete maintained RAM disassembly distributed with source Skool/Ref files.

contra-nes-vermiceli.title: Contra
contra-nes-vermiceli.notes: Annotated US NES Contra disassembly with cross-platform build scripts that explicitly reassemble to a byte-for-byte match. The project incorporates and restructures Trax's earlier IDA disassembly, documents every bank and major subsystem, and emits debugger symbols; it can also build PAL Probotector.

cookie-spectrum.title: Cookie
cookie-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

copperline-amiga-emulator.title: Copperline
copperline-amiga-emulator.notes: Cycle-driven OCS/ECS/AGA Amiga emulator in Rust with reverse stepping, GDB/DAP source debugging, profiling, headless automation and direct WHDLoad/executable launching. Tracked as adjacent reverse-engineering/development tooling.

coppershock-amonia-reconstruction.title: Coppershock — Amonia demo reconstruction
coppershock-amonia-reconstruction.notes: coppershock.S identifies an AsmOne reconstruction of the 1990 Amonia demo from a packed executable; source and assets are present. Reassembly and equivalence have not been independently checked.

dos-cosmore.title: Cosmore
dos-cosmore.notes: Reconstructs v1.20 using Turbo C 2.0 and TASM 1.0. Author reports 96.30% identical load-image bytes after excluding EXE headers/relocations; remaining mismatch includes uninitialized data, so do not mark byte-exact.

crossroads2-c64-markrdgox.title: crossroads-2-disassembly
crossroads2-c64-markrdgox.notes: Reverse engineering of Steve Harter's C64 Crossroads 2. The pristine build reproduces the original PRG exactly, while optional build switches expose patches and dead-code experiments. Documentation covers tricky instruction sequences, interrupt code, self-modifying routines, hidden credits and the game's adaptive timing.

crudnes-hitchhikr.title: crudNES
crudnes-hitchhikr.display_title: crudNES — NES tracing emulator & automatic disassembly workbench
crudnes-hitchhikr.notes: NES emulator modified specifically for reverse engineering. Its tracer records code and data accesses while a game runs and generates disassembly plus the supporting files needed to recreate the ROM image; mapper-aware disassembly coverage expands as execution is observed.

crunchmania-python.title: Crunch-Mania — Python format tools
crunchmania-python.notes: Python package exposes four documented Crunch-Mania variants, including delta forms; can scan ADF for embedded CrM blocks and unpack obfuscated variants used in Amiga demos/games. Distinct implementation from the already tracked Ancient format collection.

way-exploding-fist-electron-loader.title: custom-tape-loader-WotEF
way-exploding-fist-electron-loader.display_title: The Way of the Exploding Fist — Acorn Electron tape-loader disassembly
subjects: The Way of the Exploding Fist
tags: The Way of the Exploding Fist
way-exploding-fist-electron-loader.notes: Focused disassembly of the Acorn Electron custom tape loader for The Way of the Exploding Fist. The annotated source reconstructs its PRNG-driven decryption, tape block loading, event/vector setup, screen loading and handoff to the main game.

cyberdyne-warrior-c64-analyser.title: Cyberdyne Warrior
cyberdyne-warrior-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. Tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

cybernoid-2-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers.
