cybernoid-ii-spectrum-analyser.title: Cybernoid II
cybernoid-ii-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Cybernoid II — ZX Spectrum analyser project
cybernoid-ii-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Cybernoid II directory contains an approximately 1185 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus graphics-set metadata. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

cybernoid-amiga-horace.title: Cybernoid — Amiga reverse engineering and editor/repacker
cybernoid-amiga-horace.display_title: Cybernoid — Amiga reverse engineering and editor/repacker
cybernoid-amiga-horace.notes: Reverse engineering of the Amiga Cybernoid binary and data formats. The repository documents a lossless GAME → project → GAME workflow, byte-for-byte round-trip verification, decoded maps/graphics/tables and editor tooling; a fuller 68000 disassembly remains future work.

d68k-amiga-disassembler.title: D68k — Amiga m68k disassembler
d68k-amiga-disassembler.notes: Denis Ahrens disassembler source for AmigaOS 2+ includes documented A68k/SLink and vasm assembly commands; source traverses hunks and uses passes for labels and disassembly. No runtime verification.

dalek-attack-amiga-horace.title: Dalek Attack — Amiga WHDLoad reverse engineering
dalek-attack-amiga-horace.display_title: Dalek Attack — Amiga WHDLoad reverse engineering
dalek-attack-amiga-horace.notes: Reverse engineering and extension of the Amiga Dalek Attack WHDLoad installation. The repository documents disk/resource maps, Pack-Ice decoding, character/portrait structures and runtime selectors, and implements optional external-character support while preserving the original game path.

daley-supertest-spectrum-analyser.title: Daley Thompson's Supertest
daley-supertest-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Daley Thompson's Supertest — ZX Spectrum analyser project
daley-supertest-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Daley Thompson's Supertest directory contains an approximately 169 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

dan-dare-spectrum-analyser.title: Dan Dare
dan-dare-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Dan Dare — ZX Spectrum analyser project
dan-dare-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Dan Dare directory contains a 3286 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and two exported Z80 assembly listings plus Lua formatter/viewer tooling. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

deathmaze-5000-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Deathmaze 5000
deathmaze-5000-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Deathmaze 5000 — Apple II disassembly & data analysis
deathmaze-5000-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Deathmaze 5000 disassembly with SourceGen project files/binaries, walkthrough maps generated from game data structures, word/message extraction and analysis of the maze-rendering implementation.

dos-zeliard-decomp-awkto.title: decomp-zel
dos-zeliard-decomp-awkto.display_title: Zeliard — independent DOS analysis and SDL port
dos-zeliard-decomp-awkto.notes: Independent repository with SAR/resource tools, original-binary disassembly scripts, documented town/fight systems, SDL port and author-described playthrough. CI tests without game files; parity/playthrough checks need original files. Separate from nolanvenhola's bit-perfect MASM reconstruction.

decopper-amiga.title: DeCopper — Amiga Copper-list inspector
decopper-amiga.notes: Reads an extracted binary Copper list and prints WAIT, SKIP and register moves; README shows an example and a VBCC build. It is a focused inspection tool, not a general 68000 disassembler.

delirium-liberation-cracktro.title: Delirium Liberation intro
subjects: Delirium Liberation: Captive II crack intro
delirium-liberation-cracktro.notes: Individual source identifies the Delirium crack intro for Liberation: Captive II and gives a vasm binary build command. No project-specific binary hash or rebuilt-output comparison is documented; the assembly is research material.

demons-are-forever-amiga.title: Demons Are Forever demo
demons-are-forever-amiga.notes: Disassembled and slightly modernized 1988 D.O.C. Amiga demo using ReSource, with extracted graphics/music. Repository supplies assembly source and assets; rebuild and byte identity are not explicitly established.

c64-jblang-demotools.title: demotools
c64-jblang-demotools.display_title: demotools — BoozeLoader C64 demo extraction tools
c64-jblang-demotools.notes: D64 extractor and decruncher for BoozeLoader trackmo chains using ByteBoozer 1.1/2.0, created during Uncensored disassembly. Author verified Uncensored and part of Remains against VICE dumps; separate program.py disassembler handles BASIC tokens and simple traces but is experimental.

dos-dethrace.title: Dethrace
dos-dethrace.notes: Buildable native Carmageddon reimplementation that replaces original assembly with C function by function. Historical Watcom symbols exist but README says they do not match released code positions. Completeness and playable parity remain unverified.

die-dunkle-dimension-c64-maps.title: Die Dunkle Dimension
die-dunkle-dimension-c64-maps.display_title: Die Dunkle Dimension — C64 map and graphics format analysis
die-dunkle-dimension-c64-maps.notes: Python extraction and documented analysis of original game map, charset, tile and sprite data. Scope is game data; no disassembly or playable reconstruction is claimed.

albank1-dig-dug-c64-disassembly.title: Dig Dug
albank1-dig-dug-c64-disassembly.notes: Cartridge listing documents startup, KERNAL calls, CIA and VIC registers. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

jotd-dig-dug-ii-amiga.title: Dig Dug II — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-dig-dug-ii-amiga.display_title: Dig Dug II — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-dig-dug-ii-amiga.notes: Amiga port of Dig Dug II with arcade-perfect gameplay; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

dig-dug-amiga-jotd.title: Dig Dug — Amiga 68k translation
dig-dug-amiga-jotd.notes: Project-specific 223 KB Dig Dug Z80 listing, 70 KB Amiga driver and ECS/AGA directories support a separate Amiga conversion. README describes Dig Dug II and some source headers retain predecessor names; these do not establish gameplay or a completed release.

dis64-c64-6502-disassembler.title: Dis64
dis64-c64-6502-disassembler.notes: Original JavaScript 6502 disassembler for C64 and VIC-20 binary/PRG files. Its README describes VIC bank and screen labels, system symbols, range and code/data controls, and KickAssembler output. It credits OldSkoolCoder for the later VIC-20 modification; catalogued at the original repository.

amiga-dis68k-rust.title: dis68k — Amiga Hunk disassembler
amiga-dis68k-rust.notes: Rust HUNK parser and 68000 disassembler with optional 68020+ decode, symbol/LVO annotations, CLI and library. README states Claude Opus 4.6 researched and implemented the project, and warns it is an AI experiment without correctness guarantees; advanced cross-references remain planned.

dis68k-modernized-tomharte.title: dis68k — modernized 68000 disassembler
dis68k-modernized-tomharte.notes: Modernizes W. de Waal’s public-domain 1991 disassembler for modern compilers, command-line use, and configurable ROM load/execution addresses via map files. Generic 68000 input; it does not claim Amiga or Atari ST executable-container awareness.

atari2600-disassemblies-debro.title: Disassemblies
atari2600-disassemblies-debro.display_title: Atari 2600 disassemblies — Dennis Debro exact-ROM reconstruction collection
atari2600-disassemblies-debro.notes: Large Atari 2600 reverse-engineering collection by Dennis Debro. The title READMEs identify the sources as analyzed, labeled and commented reverse-engineering projects and state that the code assembles into the exact game ROM. The tracker treats the collection as one record rather than fabricating separate activity histories for each title directory.

c64-esshahn-disawsm.title: disawsm
c64-esshahn-disawsm.notes: Browser-based C64 PRG disassembler with code/data entry points, editable labels/comments, project persistence and ACME/Kick Assembler exports. README documents a Vite build and working interface; search and undo remain unimplemented.

disk-ii-boot-apple2-sourcegen.title: Disk II boot firmware
disk-ii-boot-apple2-sourcegen.display_title: Disk II BOOT0/BOOT1 — Apple II disk boot analysis
disk-ii-boot-apple2-sourcegen.notes: Andy McFadden’s annotated SourceGen disassemblies of the 256-byte Disk II controller BOOT0 firmware and a DOS 3.3 BOOT1 sector. BOOT0 explains its decoding table and sector-read behavior; the linked BOOT1 listing traces loading RWTS. The ROM index supplies the paired project set. BOOT1 is one sample from a disk image, not a claim to cover every DOS version.

disk-utilities-amiga.title: Disk Utilities — Amiga disk analysis
subjects: Amiga disk images and track loaders
tags: Amiga disk images and track loaders
disk-utilities-amiga.notes: Collection reads and converts flux and sector disk images (including ADF, Extended ADF and IPF), reads Amiga ADF files and boot blocks, and includes a limited Amiga emulator plus m68k disassembler to run track-loader/protection code and dump decrypted Copylock output. IPF/CTRaw support depends on CAPS library.

diskflashback-amiga-atari.title: DiskFlashback
diskflashback-amiga-atari.display_title: DiskFlashback — Amiga/Atari filesystem mounts and imaging
diskflashback-amiga-atari.notes: Windows virtual-drive and real-floppy utility with Amiga OFS/FFS/PFS and Atari GEMDOS FAT access. README lists ADF/ST/HDF mounts and read-only DMS/MSA/SCP, plus DrawBridge/Greaseweazle/SuperCardPro hardware integration. Uses other libraries for much of its format handling.

dodonpachi-daioujou-arcade-mixup.title: DoDonPachi DaiOuJou
dodonpachi-daioujou-arcade-mixup.notes: Mixup translates IGS PGM Black Label Version-B ROM code into JavaScript and compares against MAME. Current README describes five-stage static preflight and ongoing round-two progression, while game.json retains older W179 stage coverage. End-to-end playability is not established.

c64-wallneradam-dolffydos.title: Dolffy DOS
c64-wallneradam-dolffydos.notes: Replacement C64 KERNAL combines publicly disassembled DolphinDOS-derived code with a separately written JiffyDOS-compatible serial protocol. This is a derivative firmware development project, not a reconstruction of an original complete Dolffy binary.

jotd-donkey-kong-amiga.title: Donkey Kong — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-donkey-kong-amiga.notes: Arcade Donkey Kong transcode for Amiga; README credits Z80 reverse engineering and jotd's Z80→Amiga 68000 conversion, and describes gameplay as 100% identical.

c64-vic20-doswedge-disassembly.title: DOS Wedge
c64-vic20-doswedge-disassembly.notes: Annotated original DOS 5.1 Wedge for C64 and a distinct VIC-20 Wedge in per-platform directories, with original reference images and build scripts. Included as system-software source recovery; exact match and runtime tests were not independently verified.

dos-re-recovery-framework.title: dos_re
dos-re-recovery-framework.display_title: dos_re — DOS game recovery and port framework
dos-re-recovery-framework.notes: Modular Python 3.11+ framework for recovering DOS games and developing native source ports. Combines static facts, original-executable oracle runs, deterministic replays and partial generated or authored implementations; it is a framework, not a completed port of a specific game or a universal decompiler.

tristar-double-action-reconstructed.title: Double Action v1.0 — reconstructed Amiga packer
tristar-double-action-reconstructed.display_title: Double Action v1.0 — reconstructed Amiga packer
tristar-double-action-reconstructed.notes: Vince / Tristar is credited for the historical Tristar Double Action v1.0 packer. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header credits Vince/Tristar and describes a fully reconstructed packer by Volker Schwaberow; labelled file and disk operations follow. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

runtime_profiles.notes: README states the AGA version runs on an A1200 with 4 MB Fast RAM.

jotd-double-dragon-amiga.notes: AGA Amiga Double Dragon port; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

dpaint-js-amiga-st-graphics.title: DPaint.js
dpaint-js-amiga-st-graphics.display_title: DPaint.js — Amiga IFF/ADF and ST Deluxe Paint graphics editor
dpaint-js-amiga-st-graphics.notes: Browser image editor with Amiga icon, ILBM, ANIM and ADF read/write support plus documented Atari ST Deluxe Paint compression modes and ST palette limits. dos-dr-riptide-dissected.title: Dr. Riptide Dissected
dos-dr-riptide-dissected.display_title: In Search of Dr. Riptide — DAT viewer and editor
dos-dr-riptide-dissected.notes: Viewer/editor for original DAT resources, maps, sprites, images, music, sound, text and triggers. Credits srtuss for the map format and joint research; game executable remains original.

dragon-warrior-nes-nmikstas.title: dragon-warrior-disassembly
dragon-warrior-nes-nmikstas.display_title: Dragon Warrior — NES complete source reconstruction
dragon-warrior-nes-nmikstas.notes: Completed and commented reverse engineering of NES Dragon Warrior. The repository's build assembles the reconstructed source into bank binaries and checks their hashes against the original binaries; the README describes the project as finished and the output banks as identical.

vs-sr-cd32-dragonstone.title: Dragonstone — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-dragonstone.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Dragonstone. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

drawbridge-amiga-floppy.title: DrawBridge
drawbridge-amiga-floppy.display_title: DrawBridge — Amiga disk imaging and emulator floppy bridge
drawbridge-amiga-floppy.notes: Arduino firmware and host applications for raw floppy-track capture and Amiga DD reading/writing, integrated with WinUAE and Amiberry. The README mentions Atari ST as a raw-track/third-party format path; bundled host applications specifically target Amiga DD disks. Some IPF/SCP writing and accurate flux capture remain experimental.

driller-amiga-hitchhikr.title: Driller — Amiga disassembly
driller-amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Amiga Driller reconstruction beginning with exact reassembly of the executable decryption code, then decrypting the game and driving ReSource in an emulator to obtain a working disassembly.

drol-apple2-xekri.title: Drol — Apple II byte-perfect reconstruction
drol-apple2-xekri.notes: Literate reverse engineering of Broderbund's 1983 Apple II Drol. Project instructions define annotated 6502 source that assembles to byte-perfect matches, with ongoing control-flow diagrams and game/graphics analysis.

dos-duke2-reconstructed.title: Duke2Reconstructed
dos-duke2-reconstructed.display_title: Duke Nukem II — byte-exact DOS source reconstruction
dos-duke2-reconstructed.notes: Author reports the reconstructed executable is byte-for-byte identical for the documented LZEXE shareware and registered builds. Separate from the same author's modern RigelEngine port; shares historical engine lineage with Cosmore.

dun-darach-spectrum.title: Dun Darach
dun-darach-spectrum.notes: Lunysoft/Luny Dun Darach disassembly preserved in Michael Cook's source collection.

dynamite-dan-2-spectrum.title: Dynamite Dan II
dynamite-dan-2-spectrum.notes: BadBeard's historical Dynamite Dan II disassembly, preserved in Michael Cook's source collection.

electroniq-acorn-electron-emulator.title: Electroniq
electroniq-acorn-electron-emulator.notes: Browser-based Acorn Electron emulator supporting tape, disk and MMB media plus configurable ROM/RAM banks. It is directly paired with the Electroniq VS Code debugger extension, making it useful as reproducible Electron development and software-archaeology infrastructure.

electroniq-vscode-debugger.title: Electroniq Debugger Extension
electroniq-vscode-debugger.display_title: Electroniq — VS Code source-level Acorn Electron debugger
electroniq-vscode-debugger.notes: VS Code debugger extension for Electroniq. It consumes max65 source maps and provides source-level 6502 breakpoints, stepping, watches, label hover information and register inspection against the browser-based Acorn Electron emulator.

jotd-elevator-action-amiga.title: Elevator Action — Amiga arcade port
jotd-elevator-action-amiga.notes: Amiga remake/port with README crediting jotd for reverse engineering, 68000 transcode, graphics conversion and sound conversion.

elite-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Elite
elite-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Elite — Apple II disassembly & platform-specific analysis
elite-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Elite disassembly based on the 4am crack. The project reconstructs a binary from descrambled runtime content, documents all Apple II-specific code plus some shared 6502 code, and publishes SourceGen project files together with analysis of ships, meshes and tokenized messages. The author explicitly notes that much shared code remains uncommented.

elite-bbc-kieranhj.title: Elite
elite-bbc-kieranhj.display_title: Elite — BBC Micro original-source restoration to BeebAsm
elite-bbc-kieranhj.notes: Converts the surviving original BBC Elite BASIC-assembler sources into a readable, reproducible BeebAsm/Python build. The build process reconstructs checksum/encryption steps and documents CRC verification against binaries extracted from the historical source archive.

runtime_profiles.name: Plus/4

elite-harmless-c64-kroc.title: Elite
elite-harmless-c64-kroc.display_title: Elite Harmless — C64 Elite disassembly and enhancement
elite-harmless-c64-kroc.notes: Independent CA65 disassembly and enhanced C64 Elite research by Kroc Camen; the original GitHub repository is an archived relocation notice and points to Codeberg. The relocated source could not be inspected in this pass, so no current build, completeness or exact-match state is asserted.

elite-spectrum-analyser.title: Elite
elite-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Elite directory contains an approximately 2486 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus custom Lua viewer, formatter and globals scripts. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

elite-128k-spectrum.title: Elite 128K
elite-128k-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

elite-128k-ataribaby42.title: Elite 128K — ataribaby42 reconstruction
elite-128k-ataribaby42.notes: Independent reconstruction of the 48K-address-space Elite 128K-compatible release. The default TAP is documented as byte-for-byte identical to the supplied reference; annotation/documentation is still in progress.

elite-demo-bbc-micro-moxon.display_title: Elite Demonstration Disc — BBC Micro reconstruction
elite-demo-bbc-micro-moxon.notes: Source reconstructed by hand from the Acornsoft Elite Demonstration Disc binaries; build verification reports all compiled binaries matching the originals.

runtime_profiles.notes: Repository explicitly includes BBC Master 128 Econet Elite.

runtime_profiles.name: 6502 Second Processor
runtime_profiles.notes: Repository explicitly includes the 6502 Second Processor version.

elite-over-econet-moxon.notes: Network-enabled Elite variants that load over Econet and add live multiplayer scoreboards. The repository assembles source variants and builds DSD/SSD images; BBC Micro and Master bases include reconstructed source lineages.

elite-universe-editor-moxon.display_title: Elite Universe Editor — multi-platform in-game universe editor

elite-universe-editor-moxon.notes: Game-specific editor integrated into BBC Master, 6502 Second Processor and C64 Elite. The BBC variants modify documented source; the C64 variant patches original binaries while sharing a common editor library.

elite-acorn-electron-moxon.title: Elite — Acorn Electron reconstruction
elite-acorn-electron-moxon.notes: Hand-reconstructed from an Acorn Electron Elite disassembly. The game code is verified against the reference, but the generated cassette binaries intentionally do not match the encrypted originals.

elite-atari-st-ataribaby42.title: Elite — Atari ST source reconstruction
elite-atari-st-ataribaby42.notes: Reconstructs a modern independently buildable Atari ST Elite source tree from the surviving historical archive. The project explicitly notes that the executable is not byte-identical because the assembler, branch encoding and launcher differ.

elite-bbc-master-moxon.title: Elite — BBC Master reconstruction
elite-bbc-master-moxon.notes: Hand-reconstructed BBC Master Elite source with checksum/reference verification; the documented default build reports all compiled binaries matching the original SNG47 variant.

elite-bbc-micro-disc-moxon.title: Elite — BBC Micro disc reconstruction
elite-bbc-micro-disc-moxon.notes: Mark Moxon's fully documented source reconstruction, rebuilt by hand from a disassembly of the BBC Micro disc binaries; the default verified build reports all compiled binaries matching the originals.

elite-amiga-ataribaby42.title: Elite — enhanced Atari ST and Amiga builds (ataribaby42)
elite-amiga-ataribaby42.display_title: Elite — enhanced Atari ST and Amiga builds (ataribaby42)

runtime_profiles.name: Enhanced Atari ST build
runtime_profiles.notes: The root README describes the enhanced Atari ST MC68000 build and Atari floppy/TOS distribution. No minimum RAM is stated here.

evidence.excerpt: Buildable Elite sources for the MC68000: the enhanced Atari ST version in src_atari, a separate native Amiga port in src_amiga, and the preserved original Atari ST version in src_orig.

runtime_profiles.name: Default OCS build
runtime_profiles.os: Kickstart 1.3; Workbench 1.3 or later for icon launch
runtime_profiles.notes: The documented baseline is PAL OCS with 512 KB Chip RAM plus 512 KB expansion RAM. The delivered image runs on a stock MC68000 and switches to wider routines automatically on 68020+ CPUs.

Double-click it to launch the game from Workbench 1.3 or later.

runtime_profiles.name: 68020-only build
runtime_profiles.notes: The explicit cpu=68020 build assembles only the native 68020 forms. The README does not restate a separate RAM minimum for this variant, so RAM is left unspecified.

evidence.excerpt: cpu=68020 still assembles the native forms only, for a tighter image that needs an MC68020.

techniques: shared Atari ST and Amiga regression testing
elite-amiga-ataribaby42.notes: The repository root builds an enhanced Atari ST version from the corrected historical source and a separate native Amiga port, sharing gameplay changes but keeping independent source trees. It also contains an independent preserved-original Atari ST build in src_orig, catalogued separately. The enhanced Atari output uses a TOS launcher and disk image; the Amiga version supplies native bitplanes, input, Paula audio and AmigaDOS handling. The documented Amiga baseline is PAL OCS/MC68000, Kickstart 1.3 and 512 KB Chip plus 512 KB expansion RAM; an explicit 68020-only variant is available. The original build is explicitly not byte-identical; do not infer byte identity for the enhanced versions. Real Amiga hardware remains unverified.

elite-nes-moxon.title: Elite — NES reconstruction
elite-nes-moxon.notes: Hand-reconstructed NES Elite source from original binaries; build verification reports the compiled PAL binaries matching the originals.

emetic-skimmer-movers-cracktro.title: Emetic Skimmer — The Movers cracktro reconstruction
emetic-skimmer-movers-cracktro.display_title: Emetic Skimmer — The Movers cracktro reconstruction
emetic-skimmer-movers-cracktro.notes: The Movers is credited for the historical The Movers Emetic Skimmer cracktro. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header dates the cracktro to 1988 and identifies reconstructed annotated vasm source with a HUNK assembler command. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

emutos-atari-tos-reimplementation.title: EmuTOS
source_language: Atari TOS/GEM API and hardware behavior
emutos-atari-tos-reimplementation.notes: Free TOS-compatible operating-system/ROM implementation for Atari systems. Included as reproducible legacy-development and emulation infrastructure: it provides a redistributable TOS-compatible environment and is actively tested against legacy Atari software and hardware behavior. It is not classified as a reconstructed proprietary Atari ROM.

c64-air-encounter.title: Encounter
c64-air-encounter.display_title: Encounter — C64 game analysis and WebGL remake
c64-air-encounter.notes: Playable-in-browser partial WebGL recreation of the C64 game, with author-documented extraction of some SID frequencies from original C64 memory via ICU64. Feature checklist documents incomplete accurate sound, enemy AI and collisions.

engine9000-debugger.title: ENGINE9000 — multi-system 68k/Z80 debugger
engine9000-debugger.notes: Debugger/profiler integrating fork-derived emulators for Amiga, Neo Geo and Mega Drive. README documents source-level stepping, memory watchpoints, frame rewind, hardware visualizers and reproducible frame/audio smoke tests; author warns it is under heavy development and Linux/Windows testing is limited.

epoch-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Epoch
epoch-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Epoch — Apple II work-in-progress disassembly & graphics-engine analysis
epoch-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Epoch disassembly with SourceGen files/binaries, object definitions and graphics-engine analysis. The disassembly itself is explicitly marked work in progress because some of the mathematics remains unexplained.

everyones-a-wally-spectrum.title: Everyone's A Wally
everyones-a-wally-spectrum.notes: Complete RAM disassembly by Ritchie Swann; later/current mirrors also exist in the Pobtastic SkoolKit collection.

everyones-wally-spectrum-analyser.title: Everyone's A Wally
everyones-wally-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Everyone's A Wally — ZX Spectrum analyser project
everyones-wally-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Everyone's a Wally directory contains a 1976 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and exported Z80 assembly, Lua exporter/viewer tooling and extensive decoded graphics/screens. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

exile-c64-analyser.title: Exile
exile-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Exile directory contains a large Analysis.json annotation database (~1.43 MB) plus saved analyser/emulator state and configuration. This is tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

exile-bbc-micro-chriskillpack.title: exile-beebasm
exile-bbc-micro-chriskillpack.notes: Work-in-progress disassembly of the BBC Micro game Exile, using BBC disk/disassembly tooling and BeebAsm. It is an independent title-specific reconstruction effort distinct from other Exile disassemblies.

exolon-spectrum-analyser.title: Exolon
exolon-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Exolon directory contains a 3645 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and large annotated analysis database. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

exploring-another-world-dos.title: Exploring Another World
exploring-another-world-dos.display_title: Another World — DOS resource and VM exploration
exploring-another-world-dos.notes: Haskell research into Another World PC/DOS data layout and virtual-machine resources, with concrete MEMLIST and BANK parsing. An Amiga ADF is cited as background, not as proof of Amiga-media decoding; no full game rebuild is claimed.

dos-f15se2-re.title: F-15 Strike Eagle 2 source code reconstruction
dos-f15se2-re.upstream_name: F-15 Strike Eagle 2 source code reconstruction
dos-f15se2-re.display_title: F-15 Strike Eagle II — DOS executable reconstruction
dos-f15se2-re.notes: Reconstructs v451.03 game C code and most related executables with a functionally equivalent loader. C routines can match original instructions when compiled with Microsoft C 5.1, but executable layout differences and remaining assembly mean no whole-binary exactness claim. Modern port is a separate derivative.

fairlight-spectrum-krumlinde.title: Fairlight
fairlight-spectrum-krumlinde.notes: Commented and labelled Fairlight disassembly reconstructed from a 48K memory snapshot. The source assembles cleanly with sjasmplus and is explicitly verified byte-for-byte against the full $4000-$FFFF RAM image. Supporting analysis documents the room bytecode, render pipeline, sprites, textured fill, collision, text and main loop.

fairlight2-spectrum-wilson.title: Fairlight II
fairlight2-spectrum-wilson.display_title: Fairlight II — ZX Spectrum completion-bug reverse engineering
fairlight2-spectrum-wilson.notes: Active investigation of the ZX Spectrum 48K version of Fairlight II, focused on documenting its data structures and behaviour to determine why the game appears impossible to complete and whether a plausible fix can be recovered from the original design. Current work documents room and dynamic-object formats.

c64-esshahn-c64-fairlight.title: Fairlight intro
c64-esshahn-c64-fairlight.notes: Unpacked C64 Fairlight intro source with staged generated, cleaned and enhanced ACME listings and a build script. Later versions fix and change the original, so no exact rebuild of the initial intro is asserted.

feud-spectrum-analyser.title: Feud
feud-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Feud directory contains an approximately 456 KiB Analysis.json annotation database, plus custom viewer script and decoded map image; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

feud-amiga-hitchhikr.title: Feud — Amiga disassembly
feud-amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Partial Amiga Feud disassembly covering all 68000 code and supporting multiple disk versions. Some versions reassemble to the exact same executable while others do not, so project-wide byte exactness is intentionally left unknown.

c64-mist64-final-cartridge.title: Final Cartridge III
c64-mist64-final-cartridge.display_title: Final Cartridge III — partial ROM source reconstruction
c64-mist64-final-cartridge.notes: Reconstructed bank 0 and the lower part of bank 3 of the December 1988 C64 cartridge, including editor, speeder, freezer and monitor components. Repository claims an identical fc3.bin with make test; annotations and source reconstruction cover only the stated banks.

c64-mist64-fc3-geos.title: Final Cartridge III with GEOS
c64-mist64-fc3-geos.display_title: Final Cartridge III with GEOS — ROM adaptation
c64-mist64-fc3-geos.notes: Build script places the separately reconstructed GEOS 2.0 KERNAL and a loader in Final Cartridge III ROM bank 2. Produces CRT images from GEOS source plus an original FC3 cartridge image; distinct derivative integration, with deskTop still loaded from disk.

final-fantasy-nes-disch.title: Final Fantasy
final-fantasy-nes-disch.display_title: Final Fantasy — NES fully documented disassembly
final-fantasy-nes-disch.notes: Version 1.0 describes a complete, fully commented/documented, reassemblable disassembly of the US NES Final Fantasy. The repository includes all material required to generate a ROM and extensive bug/format commentary.

vs-sr-cd32-fireandice.title: Fire & Ice — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-fireandice.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Fire & Ice. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

firelord-spectrum-analyser.title: Firelord
firelord-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Firelord directory contains an approximately 1305 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus project configuration. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

firestaff-dungeon-master-engine.title: Firestaff
firestaff-dungeon-master-engine.display_title: Firestaff — Dungeon Master / Chaos Strikes Back engine reconstruction

runtime_profiles.name: Apple Silicon macOS host smoke
runtime_profiles.notes: PROJECT_STATUS explicitly records a native macOS host smoke and Apple Silicon macOS boot for Dungeon Master 1. This is a verified host configuration, not a general minimum CPU or memory requirement for Firestaff.

evidence.excerpt: Dungeon Master 1 | Playable/source-locked V1; native macOS host smoke verified ... Apple Silicon macOS boot

firestaff-dungeon-master-engine.notes: Clean-room, source-faithful engine for Dungeon Master, Chaos Strikes Back, Dungeon Master II, Dungeon Master Nexus and Theron's Quest. Dungeon Master 1 PC/DOS 3.4 is playable/source-locked; CSB and DM2 retain bounded verified real-media routes. Current Theron evidence includes authenticated US and JP Track 02 boots with source-backed early runtime and scripted movement plus bounded in-memory title-audio handling, explicitly not complete parity. A fresh-start DM1 C37 save round-trip is verified, while authentic Atari v1.0 resume remains fail-closed pending an Atari-specific tail/champion/queue adapter. Nexus remains active real-data bring-up and full suite parity is not claimed.

flashback-atari-st-reminiscence.title: Flashback — Atari ST REminiscence port
flashback-atari-st-reminiscence.notes: Ports the REminiscence Flashback engine to Atari ST using original Amiga installation data and STDL. README states 2 MB minimum (4 MB recommended), hard disk, STE-only sound effects; the work is a derivative port of the already tracked engine.

flashfloppy-amiga-st.title: FlashFloppy
flashfloppy-amiga-st.notes: Open firmware for Gotek hardware exposes USB disk images as a floppy drive to Amiga and Atari ST hosts. Official documentation lists ADF and ST support. This is drive emulation rather than a title reconstruction; compatibility with protection/extended formats varies and should not be inferred from ordinary ADF/ST support.

fluxfox-amiga-atari-disk.title: fluxfox
fluxfox-amiga-atari-disk.display_title: fluxfox — Amiga/Atari bitstream and flux-image library
fluxfox-amiga-atari-disk.notes: General-purpose floppy image library primarily focused on PC formats. Its README documents initial Amiga, Macintosh and Atari ST support, an Amiga trackdisk schema and Atari FAT12 access. Support is partial; custom Amiga protection tracks are not decoded by its Amiga schema and the API remains under development.

flying-shark-atari-st.title: Flying Shark
flying-shark-atari-st.notes: 254 functions named with all ten subsystems reconstructed and verified; playable PRG/floppy under Hatari, real joystick/iron testing still pending.

flying-shark-spectrum.title: Flying Shark
flying-shark-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: In progress.

albank1-frogger-c64-disassembly.title: Frogger
albank1-frogger-c64-disassembly.display_title: Frogger — C64 cartridge disassembly and lives patch
albank1-frogger-c64-disassembly.notes: C64 Frogger cartridge disassembly aimed at lives patches; author describes JC64dis, VICE monitor and DASM/cartconv. README command names FroggerInfLives.asm while the tree contains FroggerInfLive.asm, so the documented command needs correction before build verification.

frontier-vm-atari-st.title: Frontier: Elite II / FrontierVM
frontier-vm-atari-st.display_title: Frontier: Elite II — Atari ST VM/reimplementation
frontier-vm-atari-st.notes: Historical Atari ST decompilation intended to remove OS/hardware dependencies and make Frontier portable.

frontier-renderer-amiga.title: Frontier: Elite II renderer/audio reconstruction
frontier-renderer-amiga.display_title: Frontier: Elite II — Amiga renderer/audio reconstruction
frontier-renderer-amiga.notes: C reconstruction of Frontier's renderer/audio plus model compiler/decompiler tooling; not a full-game reconstruction.

frontier-amiga-face-editor.title: Frontier: Elite II — Amiga portrait editor
frontier-amiga-face-editor.upstream_name: Frontier: Elite II — Amiga portrait editor
frontier-amiga-face-editor.display_title: Frontier: Elite II — Amiga portrait editor
frontier-amiga-face-editor.notes: Browser editor decodes face components from a specified Amiga Frontier executable, edits palette and indexed graphics, and writes a modified working executable. README identifies reference executable SHA-256; other versions unproven.

fsuae-remote-debug-patch.title: FS-UAE remote patch
fsuae-remote-debug-patch.display_title: FS-UAE remote patch — HTTP, GDB and MCP debugger
fsuae-remote-debug-patch.notes: Independent patch and C++ source for FS-UAE that add HTTP/JSON-RPC, WebSocket debugger events, a GDB remote stub, Amiga library annotations and an optional 26-tool MCP adapter. Integrated optionally with Amiga DevBench; the patch must be applied to an FS-UAE source build.

fujiboink-amiga-port.title: FujiBoink!
fujiboink-amiga-port.display_title: FujiBoink! — Atari ST demo converted to Amiga
fujiboink-amiga-port.notes: Documented 1:1 Amiga conversion of the Atari ST FujiBoink demo with scripts regenerating animation and color data and Amiga assembly source. It is a new native implementation; no binary-derived disassembly or byte-exact port claim.

dos-fuzzy-golf-analysis.title: Fuzzy's World of Miniature Space Golf Decomp
dos-fuzzy-golf-analysis.upstream_name: Fuzzy's World of Miniature Space Golf Decomp
dos-fuzzy-golf-analysis.display_title: Fuzzy's Space Golf — partial DOS resource decoding
subjects: Fuzzy's World of Miniature Space Golf
dos-fuzzy-golf-analysis.notes: README calls a full Ghidra-derived reimplementation a goal; current UTILS contain music player/converter, resource extractor and graphics format work. Do not report a completed decompilation or playable port.

gadf-amiga-bootable-images.title: gadf
gadf-amiga-bootable-images.display_title: gadf — bootable Amiga ADF image builder
gadf-amiga-bootable-images.notes: Go command-line tool creates 880 KB bootable AmigaDOS OFS images for executables and accompanying files, with startup-sequence and bootblock. README specifies Kickstart 1.2+; shell suppression is only effective on Kickstart 2.0+.

jotd-galaga-amiga.title: Galaga — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-galaga-amiga.notes: Transcode of the original Galaga Z80 arcade game to 68k assembly. README credits Glenn Neidermeier's Z80 reverse engineering and jotd's Z80→68k transcode/Amiga work.

galaxian-68k-jotd.title: Galaxian
galaxian-68k-jotd.notes: Galaxian arcade-to-68k transcode with Amiga and Neo Geo targets. The project-specific README credits Z80 reverse engineering and 68000 transcoding, reports the Amiga build fully playable with sound, and documents rebuild procedures for both target families.

jotd-game-relocations.title: GameRelocs
jotd-game-relocations.notes: Collection of game-specific reverse engineering to extract relocations from fixed-address Amiga games so they can run in fast RAM; repository explicitly calls some targets work in progress.

c64-mist64-geos.title: GEOS 2.0
c64-mist64-geos.notes: Reverse-engineered GEOS 2.0 KERNAL and disk/input drivers for C64 and C128. Default GEOS 64 build is author-reported binary identical; Wheels and C128 variant sources compile but do not yet boot as documented.

c64-ytmytm-geos-atari.title: GEOS Atari port
c64-ytmytm-geos-atari.notes: Substantial Atari 8-bit port of the reconstructed C64/C128 GEOS 2.0 source, with an XEX bootable via RAM disk on 128K+ Atari computers. README details binary compatibility limits, lack of SIO disk support, and application-specific display issues.

c64-mist64-geowrite.title: geoWrite 2.1
c64-mist64-geowrite.notes: Reconstructed English/German C64 geoWrite 2.1 VLIR records and protected sector; standard builds are author-reported identical to the bundled distribution versions. Commenting remains partial across several modules.

gfa-detokenizer-atari-st.title: GFA Detokenizer
gfa-detokenizer-atari-st.display_title: GFA Detokenizer — Atari ST GFA-BASIC source recovery
gfa-detokenizer-atari-st.notes: Decodes tokenized GFA-BASIC 3.x .gfa files into readable .lst source; validates selected output against independent editor/compiler fixtures. Builds on Peter Backes' gfalist format research but is a separate Python parser with version detection and source formatting. Does not handle GFA-BASIC 1.x/2.x or protected PSAVE files.

gfa-tokenizer-atari-st.title: GFA Tokenizer
gfa-tokenizer-atari-st.display_title: GFA Tokenizer — Atari ST GFA-BASIC source encoder
gfa-tokenizer-atari-st.notes: Companion to GFA Detokenizer: encodes readable .lst programs as tokenized .gfa files accepted by historical GFA-BASIC editor/compiler. Author reports all 423 statement keywords and a ~5,900-line corpus verified with the real editor under Hatari. This is a source authoring/round-trip tool, not a disassembly of the editor.

gfalist-gfa-basic-decoder.title: gfalist — GFA BASIC token decoder
gfalist-gfa-basic-decoder.notes: Fixed fork of Peter Backes/ONS gfalist converts Atari ST tokenized GFA BASIC 3.x files to text and can serve as Git textconv. Preserves original tool provenance; not a new binary-derived reconstruction.

ghidra-amiga-hunk-loader.title: Ghidra Amiga hunks loader
ghidra-amiga-hunk-loader.notes: Original Amiga executable hunk loader for Ghidra; this is the upstream project rather than a Pyrdacor fork.

ghidra-scripts-atari.title: Ghidra Scripts for Atari
ghidra-scripts-atari.notes: Ghidra scripts specifically for Atari TOS software analysis. Imports PRG/TOS/TTP/APP binaries with TEXT/DATA/BSS maps and relocation handling, TOS ROM images at their correct address ranges, and Atari a.out objects with symbols; also includes MiNTLib Function ID data and system-variable symbols to improve identification of unknown code.

ghidra-retro-machines.title: ghidra-retro-machines
ghidra-retro-machines.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware C64, C128, PET and NES loaders
ghidra-retro-machines.notes: Ghidra extension configures system memory maps, ROMs, hardware registers and symbols from per-machine descriptors. Primary README says C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES loader pipeline works, with supported discrete and protocol mappers; advanced mapper coverage is still developing.

ghostbusters-c64-unorig.title: Ghostbusters
ghostbusters-c64-unorig.notes: C64 Ghostbusters reverse-engineering repository containing large 6502bench/64tass source exports and reconstructed program binaries. Its build script assembles the source with 64tass, packs it with Exomizer and launches the result in C64 debuggers.

jotd-ghosts-goblins-amiga.title: Ghosts 'n Goblins — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: A1200 version
runtime_profiles.notes: README requires an A1200 with Fast RAM; the amount is not stated.

runtime_profiles.name: CD32 version
runtime_profiles.notes: README states a vanilla CD32 is supported.

jotd-ghosts-goblins-amiga.notes: AGA/CD32 Ghosts 'n Goblins port with exact arcade gameplay; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

vs-sr-cd32-gloom.title: Gloom — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-gloom.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Gloom. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

gods-deluxe-amiga-remake-jotd.title: Gods Deluxe — modern Gods remake
gods-deluxe-amiga-remake-jotd.notes: Substantial Java remake of Gods with reworked graphics, a level editor, four completed levels and explicitly observed differences from the Amiga/Sega originals. Author documents empirical study of puzzles, bonuses, scoring and videos, and says monster AI differs because the original source is unavailable. Beta is not a claim of full original-game parity.

golden-voyage-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Golden Voyage
golden-voyage-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Scott Adams Adventures / Golden Voyage — Apple II interpreter disassembly
golden-voyage-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of Scott Adams Adventure #12, Golden Voyage, chosen to study the common Apple II adventure interpreter. The project publishes the disassembly, SourceGen files/binaries and detailed documentation of the game database format and interpreter implementation.

albank1-gorf-c64-disassembly.title: Gorf
albank1-gorf-c64-disassembly.notes: Cartridge listing documents startup vectors and interrupt/device setup. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

gradius-nes-mixup.title: Gradius
gradius-nes-mixup.notes: Mixup translates NES Gradius ROM routines to JavaScript. The current root README reports all seven stages playable and game end/loop, checked against Mesen; its game.json retains an older stage-one blurb. No identical rebuilt NES ROM is claimed.

graduate-cpm-rom-cpc.title: Graduate CP/M ROM — Amstrad CPC disassembly
graduate-cpm-rom-cpc.upstream_name: Graduate CP/M ROM — Amstrad CPC disassembly
graduate-cpm-rom-cpc.display_title: Graduate CP/M ROM — Amstrad CPC disassembly
graduate-cpm-rom-cpc.notes: Graduate Software's two-ROM CP/M Plus boot and add-on-ROM system is being disassembled with z80-smart-disassembler. The repository contains cpm1.asm, cpm2.asm, labels and relocation notes. The unrelated AMSDOS directory preserves a predecessor's listing.

amigta-amiga.title: Grand Theft Auto — AmiGTA
amigta-amiga.notes: Native AmigaOS 68k reimplementation of Grand Theft Auto's engine, written from scratch and driven by the original game's behaviour/data as specification. Liberty City's first missions are playable; later missions and sound remain incomplete.

jotd-gravitar-amiga.title: Gravitar — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-gravitar-amiga.notes: Gravitar arcade transcode for Amiga; README credits disassembly merged with available original sources and 6502→68000 conversion.

greaseweazle-floppy-workbench.title: Greaseweazle Floppy Disk Workbench
greaseweazle-floppy-workbench.display_title: Floppy Disk Workbench — Amiga/Atari flux recovery
greaseweazle-floppy-workbench.notes: Python/PyQt Greaseweazle workbench for flux inspection, image writing and recovery; README lists Amiga DD/HD and Atari ST MFM formats. Hardware recovery claims are taken from project documentation, with no local device test.

green-beret-fds-to-nes-g0me3.title: Green Beret
green-beret-fds-to-nes-g0me3.notes: Project-specific assembly and build scripts convert the Famicom Disk System release into a UNROM NES cartridge image. The source tree includes all program banks, maps and detailed fix notes, including language selection and conversion-specific fixes. Modified cartridge output is intentionally not byte-identical to the FDS original; playability was not independently tested.

green-beret-c64-cadaver.title: greenberet-disassembly
green-beret-c64-cadaver.display_title: Green Beret — C64 disassembly and source reconstruction
green-beret-c64-cadaver.notes: Active disassembly and source-level reconstruction of Ocean/Imagine's C64 Green Beret. The author recovered the loaded game binary in VICE, used Regenerator for initial code/data classification, then identified routines and variables through live execution analysis. The reconstructed source builds a working PRG and includes optional fixes for two original game bugs.

gridrunner-c64-oldskoolcoder.title: Gridrunner
gridrunner-c64-oldskoolcoder.notes: Independent tutorial-oriented KickAssembler reconstruction with named routines and C64 constants; source differs in structure from the catalogued mwenge 64tass reconstruction. README does not state byte matching or an exercised build.

gridrunner-multi.title: Gridrunner
gridrunner-multi.notes: Part of the broader Llamasource reconstruction effort, including an Atari ST version.

gsos-dos33-fst-apple2gs-6502disassembly.title: GS/OS DOS 3.3 FST
gsos-dos33-fst-apple2gs-6502disassembly.display_title: GS/OS DOS 3.3 FST — Apple IIgs system-component disassembly
gsos-dos33-fst-apple2gs-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of the GS/OS System 6.0.1 DOS 3.3 File System Translator. The project exposes undocumented GS/OS/FST interfaces and partial 400KB-image support, with a SourceGen project set and binary.

vs-sr-cd32-guardian.title: Guardian — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-guardian.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Guardian. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

vs-sr-cd32-gunship2000.title: Gunship 2000 — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-gunship2000.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Gunship 2000. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

jotd-gyruss-amiga.title: Gyruss — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-gyruss-amiga.notes: Gyruss Amiga port; README explicitly credits game reverse engineering and M6809/Z80→68000 conversion plus Amiga graphics/sound conversion.

hansmanns-lode-runner-c64.title: Hansmanns Loderunner
hansmanns-lode-runner-c64.display_title: Hansmann's Lode Runner — C64 RE-derived modification
hansmanns-lode-runner-c64.notes: Substantial modified C64 Lode Runner built from Piddewitt's reverse-engineered source. The repository explicitly describes itself as modified assembler source of the reverse-engineered version, documents every source change, adds gameplay/debug/editor features and collected Apple/MSX/C64 levels, and includes 64tass scripts that assemble source into PRG output.

hansmanns-castles-dr-creep-c64.title: Hansmanns-Castles-of-Dr-Creep
hansmanns-castles-dr-creep-c64.display_title: Hansmann's Castles of Dr. Creep — C64 RE-derived modification
hansmanns-castles-dr-creep-c64.notes: Substantial modified C64 Castles of Dr. Creep built from Piddewitt's reverse-engineered source. The repository explicitly describes modified assembler source of the reverse-engineered version, documents source changes, modifies/enhances all castles, adds a new castle and intro, and includes 64tass scripts that assemble source into program output.

hdbackup-atari-st-recovery.title: Harddisk Utility backup — Atari ST recovery tools
hdbackup-atari-st-recovery.upstream_name: Harddisk Utility backup — Atari ST recovery tools
hdbackup-atari-st-recovery.display_title: Harddisk Utility backup — Atari ST recovery tools
source_language: ASH Harddisk Utility backup disk images
hdbackup-atari-st-recovery.notes: Reverse engineered older ASH Harddisk Utility backup stream with missing catalogue disk; pipeline carves .st images, reassembles fragments, recognizes file types and converts DEGAS assets. README explicitly credits Claude Code-assisted analysis and tooling.

harrier-attack-spectrum.title: Harrier Attack
harrier-attack-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

harrier-attack-reloaded-cpc.title: Harrier Attack Reloaded
harrier-attack-reloaded-cpc.notes: CP Soft decompiled/disassembled the original Harrier Attack in WinAPE and rebuilt it as an enhanced Amstrad Plus/GX4000 edition.

hatari-atari-emulator-debugger.title: Hatari
source_language: Atari hardware and TOS software behavior
hatari-atari-emulator-debugger.notes: Core Atari ST/STE/TT/Falcon emulator with a built-in debugger, conditional breakpoints, disassembly, symbol support, CPU/DSP profiling and remote-control facilities. Tracked as foundational software-archaeology and reproducible Atari development infrastructure.

sarnau-hatari-68k-disassembler.title: Hatari 68k disassembler component
sarnau-hatari-68k-disassembler.notes: Original author’s C 68k disassembler for Hatari covers 68k variants and FPU/PMMU. README says it requires the Hatari source to compile and is not a standalone runnable tool.

haunted-house-atari2600-disassembly.title: Haunted House
haunted-house-atari2600-disassembly.notes: Work-in-progress reverse engineering and commented disassembly of Atari 2600 Haunted House. The README documents a DASM make/build path that produces haunted.bin for execution in Stella and includes decoded sprite/font observations.

head-over-heels-cpc.title: Head Over Heels
head-over-heels-cpc.notes: CPC reverse engineering includes code, room data and sound/music work; closely related Spectrum analysis is a useful cross-reference.

head-over-heels-spectrum.title: Head Over Heels
head-over-heels-spectrum.notes: Disassembly is repeatedly checked by recompiling back to the original Spectrum memory image.

head-over-heels-spectrum-analyser.title: Head Over Heels
head-over-heels-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Head Over Heels — ZX Spectrum analyser project
head-over-heels-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The HeadOverHeels directory contains an approximately 1008 KiB Analysis.json annotation database, plus custom overlay/viewer scripts; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

hellgate-vic20.title: Hellgate
hellgate-vic20.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1984 VIC-20 game Hellgate, with a reproducible 64tass build and runnable/browser version.

vs-sr-cd32-heroquest2.title: HeroQuest II: Legacy of Sorasil — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
