vs-sr-cd32-heroquest2.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of HeroQuest II: Legacy of Sorasil. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

highway-encounter-spectrum.title: Highway Encounter
highway-encounter-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Not finished.

hissoft-devpac-cpc.title: HiSoft DEVPAC (GENA/MONA)
hissoft-devpac-cpc.notes: Reverse engineering of the CPC DEVPAC assembler/editor and disassembler/debugger; both reconstructed listings reproduce their binaries byte-for-byte.

hlipa-amiga-ataribaby42.title: Hlípa — Atari ST to Amiga reconstruction/port
hlipa-amiga-ataribaby42.display_title: Hlípa — Atari ST to Amiga reconstruction/port
hlipa-amiga-ataribaby42.notes: Native Amiga conversion of Hlípa built from reconstruction of the original Atari ST program; the repository retains the supplied historical disassembly as read-only reference and adds native AmigaOS graphics, sound and input.

hlipa-zx-ataribaby42.title: Hlípa — PMD 85 to ZX Spectrum reconstruction/port
hlipa-zx-ataribaby42.display_title: Hlípa — PMD 85 to ZX Spectrum reconstruction/port
hlipa-zx-ataribaby42.notes: Reconstructs and relocates the PMD version's game logic for a native ZX Spectrum 48K port. Extensive execution/regression tests cover gameplay through victory; some original presentation/audio features remain unported.

hode-heart-of-darkness.title: hode
hode-heart-of-darkness.display_title: Heart of Darkness — reimplemented Windows engine
source_language: Heart of Darkness Windows demo/CD data
hode-heart-of-darkness.notes: Source reimplementation of the Heart of Darkness engine for original Windows demo/CD data. Documentation lists concrete resource files and tested releases; no original Amiga or Atari ST edition is asserted.

hollywood-poker-spectrum.title: Hollywood Poker
hollywood-poker-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.title: hopper — Atari TOS and Falcon DSP disassembler
hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.upstream_name: hopper — Atari TOS and Falcon DSP disassembler
hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.display_title: hopper — Atari TOS and Falcon DSP disassembler
subjects: Atari TOS executables and Falcon DSP programs
tags: Atari TOS executables and Falcon DSP programs
hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.notes: Separate hopper68 and hopper56 command-line disassemblers decode Atari TOS 68000 executables and Falcon DSP program files. Instruction decoding lives in reusable libraries; shell build scripts and a Visual Studio project are present. No game-specific runtime or execution layer.

hover-bovver-c64.title: Hover Bovver
hover-bovver-c64.notes: Reverse-engineered and commented-source project for Jeff Minter's C64 Hover Bovver. The repository states that the game compiles and plays, while further cleanup and labelling remain.

hunchback-c64-mark.title: Hunchback
hunchback-c64-mark.display_title: Hunchback — C64 byte-exact reverse engineering & restructure
hunchback-c64-mark.notes: C64 Hunchback reverse engineering with two lines of work: an explicitly byte-exact labelled reconstruction of the original game and a restructured variant with code tweaks, routine merging and data reorganisation.

hydrofool-spectrum.title: Hydrofool
hydrofool-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

hyp2gdos-source-reconstruction.title: Hyp2GDOS — Atari ST source reconstruction
hyp2gdos-source-reconstruction.notes: Author readme.txt describes reconstructed sources for the 1997 Hyp2GDOS 1.1 binary that compile to an almost identical result. Disassembly listings and C source included; register allocation differs in places, so byte identity is not claimed.

hyper-sports-spectrum-analyser.title: Hyper Sports
hyper-sports-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Hyper Sports — ZX Spectrum analyser project
hyper-sports-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Hyper Sports directory contains an approximately 807 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

jotd-hyper-sports-amiga.title: Hyper Sports — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-hyper-sports-amiga.notes: Hyper Sports / Hyper Olympic '84 remake for AGA/ECS Amiga; README credits transcode, Amiga port, graphics and sound conversion.

ida-amiga-hunk-loader-lab313ru.title: IDA Amiga Hunk loader
ida-amiga-hunk-loader-lab313ru.notes: IDA Pro loader for Amiga Hunk executables; the repository contains the Python loader and a relocation fix. Distinct from the same author’s separately tracked Ghidra Amiga loader.

ida-atari-st-gemdos-loader.title: IDA Atari ST GEMDOS loader
ida-atari-st-gemdos-loader.notes: IDA loader for Atari ST GEMDOS executables: maps TEXT/DATA/BSS, relocates data and imports global DRI/GST symbols, including extended names. README reports testing with IDA Pro 7.2 on macOS; other hosts are an upstream expectation rather than verified here.

ida-stuff-retro-loaders-g0me3.title: ida_stuff
ida-stuff-retro-loaders-g0me3.display_title: ida_stuff — retro-console IDA loaders and analysis scripts
ida-stuff-retro-loaders-g0me3.notes: Multi-console IDA toolkit containing C++ loaders for iNES/FDS, Game Boy and Master System images, source and prebuilt loader binaries, CDL import/autorun scripts for NES, Game Boy, SNES and Genesis, and numerous title-specific analysis scripts. The source also includes 65816, m68000 and SH-4-oriented helpers. Visual Studio project files establish a source build path, but supported IDA/Windows versions were not documented.

idris-atari-st-reconstruction.title: Idris OS — partial Atari ST reconstruction
idris-atari-st-reconstruction.upstream_name: Idris OS — partial Atari ST reconstruction
idris-atari-st-reconstruction.display_title: Idris OS — partial Atari ST reconstruction
idris-atari-st-reconstruction.notes: Partial reconstructed Idris OS source tree: kernel holds original xidris/idrisk1a binaries and large .orig.s listings, plus C and assembly modules and a cross-toolchain GNUmakefile. Build and fidelity unverified.

iff2bpl-amiga-bitplane-converter.title: iff2bpl — Amiga bitplane converter
iff2bpl-amiga-bitplane-converter.notes: Two C command-line tools convert ILBM to interleaved/non-interleaved Amiga bitplanes or chunky data and raw bitplanes back to ILBM. README notes reverse direction currently uses a largely fixed palette.

iffshow-amiga-image-inspector.title: IFFshow — Amiga ILBM inspector
iffshow-amiga-image-inspector.notes: Python/PyGame viewer decodes Amiga ILBM including EHB, HAM6/8 and deep-color modes; also writes 24-bit and HAM IFF from modern images. Author notes PyGame can load IFF directly but this code implements decoding.

ik-plus-atari-st-reforged.title: IK+ Reforged
ik-plus-atari-st-reforged.display_title: IK+ — Atari ST compatibility and three-player patches
ik-plus-atari-st-reforged.notes: Builds a new loader, version-guarded patches for the Ator-cracked ST game, a simultaneous third-player mode and a joystick test utility. Fixes TOS 2.06/STE/Mega STE compatibility and requires the user's exact original input file; the game itself is not distributed or built by CI. Patched output is not an original byte-match.

image-rider-stx.title: image-rider
image-rider-stx.display_title: image-rider — exploratory Atari ST STX parser
image-rider-stx.notes: Rust parser detects STX and its example can output track/sector image data. README explicitly says no listed image format is fully parsed and unknown input may fail; record limited to implemented exploratory extraction rather than complete STX decoding.

imogen-bbc-zornslemma.title: Imogen
imogen-bbc-zornslemma.notes: Large BBC Micro reconstruction using py8dis plus BeebAsm/ACME. The build script regenerates source for the loader, main game, auxiliary code and level/data components, reassembles them and compares reconstructed components against the original binaries.

imploder-hitchhikr.title: Imploder
imploder-hitchhikr.notes: Packs Amiga and X68000 executables or raw data using an implementation based on lab313ru reversed implode/explode routines; the 68000 decruncher was adapted from a Team17 game. Windows and Amiga executables are provided.

indy3-st-copy-protection.title: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade ST protection
indy3-st-copy-protection.upstream_name: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade ST protection
indy3-st-copy-protection.display_title: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade ST protection
subjects: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
indy3-st-copy-protection.notes: Analyzes the Atari ST Kixx release SCUMM room-92 printed Translation Table check from three floppy dumps, reconstructing its coordinate-to-symbol computation and supplying annotated disassembly, card generator and optional patcher. No game reconstruction is claimed.

indy-heat-amiga-horace.title: Indy Heat — Amiga reverse engineering and track editor
indy-heat-amiga-horace.display_title: Indy Heat — Amiga reverse engineering and track editor
indy-heat-amiga-horace.notes: Active reverse engineering of Indy Heat's Amiga track/race structures and runtime behaviour, with browser-based editing/visualisation tooling and WHDLoad integration. Current work covers track resources, waypoints/AI, race presentation, graphics and custom-track workflows.

infiltrator-conversion-tools.title: Infiltrator conversion utilities
infiltrator-conversion-tools.display_title: Infiltrator conversion tools — C64 disassembly/asset export
infiltrator-conversion-tools.notes: Python tools convert Infiltrator’s disassembly text, sprites and character-set binaries into KickAssembler and CBM PRG Studio source, with labelled example output. This is an export bridge for C64 binary analysis, not a stand-alone Infiltrator game reconstruction.

infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.title: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.upstream_name: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.display_title: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
subjects: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.notes: The original author recovered his lost 1992 demo source by disassembling the disks. Primary README documents a reassembled runnable original version plus a later single-disk adaptation with a new loader and compression; original recovered source and modified edition are distinct.

integer-basic-apple2-santa-maria.title: Integer BASIC
integer-basic-apple2-santa-maria.display_title: Integer BASIC — Apple II ROM disassembly
integer-basic-apple2-santa-maria.notes: Paul R. Santa-Maria’s independently authored Integer BASIC disassembly, ported by Andy McFadden into a SourceGen project with a few further labels. The binary comes from the DOS 3.3 system master; the project page distinguishes this earlier disassembly from Wozniak’s handwritten original source and notes additional red-book-based documentation by Sean Gugler. This record represents the underlying disassembly, not a second independent SourceGen reconstruction.

into-the-eagles-nest.title: Into the Eagle's Nest
into-the-eagles-nest.notes: Complete Amiga disassembly, debugged and reassemblable to a working game according to the upstream README and source. A prior duplicate catalogue entry incorrectly attributed an Atari ST reconstruction to this Amiga-only repository; its README, assembly header and tree document only Amiga work.

into-eagles-nest-cpc.title: Into the Eagle's Nest — CPC analysis
into-eagles-nest-cpc.display_title: Into the Eagle's Nest — CPC analysis
into-eagles-nest-cpc.notes: Amstrad CPC disassembly/analysis project investigating game logic such as enemy respawn and comparing CPC map structures with the Amiga version.

ipf-flux-native-decoder.title: ipf-flux
ipf-flux-native-decoder.display_title: IPF flux — native Amiga/Atari preservation decoder
ipf-flux-native-decoder.notes: Pure Rust CAPS/IPF track decoder, independently compared with libcapsimage across a stated 5,569-image corpus. Decodes magnetic cells, timing, write splice and weak spans; no KryoFlux stream or multi-revolution support. IPF encompasses Amiga and Atari ST, but the README does not claim native ST filesystem decoding.

ira-amiga-reassembler.title: IRA — Amiga 68k reassembler
ira-amiga-reassembler.notes: Portable Amiga Hunk and raw 68k disassembler/reassembler by Tim Ruehsen, Christian Wasner, Ilkka Lehtoranta and Frank Wille. Aminet lists version 2.11 dated February 2025; AmigaOS cross-toolchain documentation identifies its executable/library/device/raw input coverage. The CPU choices describe decoded code, not a machine minimum for running the tool.

iridis-alpha-c64.title: Iridis Alpha
iridis-alpha-c64.notes: Reverse-engineered and commented source; builds to a C64 PRG and has playable Windows/web variants.

jack-nipper-ii-spectrum-analyser.title: Jack the Nipper II
jack-nipper-ii-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Jack the Nipper II — ZX Spectrum analyser project
jack-nipper-ii-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Jack the Nipper II directory contains a 2498 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and exported Z80 assembly, map/viewer scripts and decoded graphics/map assets. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

jackal-nes-rayofjay.title: Jackal
jackal-nes-rayofjay.notes: Full commented NES Jackal disassembly. The README states all code is completely disassembled and that ASM6n builds the source to the original Jackal ROM when the original graphical data is supplied.

jotd-jail-break-amiga.title: Jail Break — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-jail-break-amiga.notes: Beta Amiga Jail Break remake; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

vs-sr-cd32-jamespond2.title: James Pond 2: Codename RoboCod — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-jamespond2.display_title: James Pond 2: Codename RoboCod — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-jamespond2.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of James Pond 2: Codename RoboCod. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

jasons-gem-spectrum.title: Jason's Gem
jasons-gem-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

jetpac-spectrum.title: JETPAC
jetpac-spectrum.notes: Fully annotated cartridge-ROM disassembly; SkoolKit output can be assembled with Pasmo into a working Spectrum tape image.

jetpac-pobtastic-spectrum.title: JETPAC — Pobtastic disassembly
jetpac-pobtastic-spectrum.notes: Independent Pobtastic/SkoolKit JETPAC disassembly; tracked separately from Michael Cook's JETPAC project.

jewels-of-babylon-spectrum.title: Jewels Of Babylon
jewels-of-babylon-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

joe-blade-spectrum.title: Joe Blade
joe-blade-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

jst-amiga-loader.title: JOTD Startup (JST)
jst-amiga-loader.notes: JOTD Startup game-specific slave loader for hard-disk installations of non-DOS Amiga games, with OS emulation and optional WHDLoad compatibility. The included v4.8 guide documents the architecture.

jotd-whdload-slaves.title: JOTD WHDLoad slave source collection
jotd-whdload-slaves.notes: Large source collection of game-specific WHDLoad slaves and patches; these are installations and compatibility fixes, not evidence that every included game has a complete reconstructed source. Collection record complements separately tracked full game reconstructions.

joust-atari-st.title: Joust
joust-atari-st.notes: Readable C reconstruction in the reusable atari_reverse framework.

jrpacman500-maze-converter.title: Jr. Pac-Man
jrpacman500-maze-converter.display_title: Jr. Pac-Man — Amiga maze and sprite conversion script
source_language: Jr. Pac-Man arcade screenshot and sprite art
jrpacman500-maze-converter.notes: A 15 KB Python script detects walls and dots in MAME maze screenshots and writes assembly and sprite data for an Amiga conversion. The public repository contains only assets/ and no generated src tree or working game; scope is the conversion script, whose inputs and dependencies are not bundled.

jsbeeb-mcp-kieranhj.title: jsbeeb-mcp
jsbeeb-mcp-kieranhj.display_title: jsbeeb-mcp — BBC Micro emulator MCP automation server
jsbeeb-mcp-kieranhj.notes: MCP server exposing headless jsbeeb sessions to AI assistants. It can boot BBC B/Master machines, run BASIC and disc images, capture text/screenshots, inspect or modify memory, inspect 6502 registers, drive exact cycle counts and control the keyboard, making it useful for automated reverse-engineering and regression workflows.

juggler-ssg.title: Juggler raytracer / ssg
juggler-ssg.display_title: Juggler / SSG — Amiga raytracer binary/source analysis
juggler-ssg.notes: Ghidra analysis of the original ssg executable alongside surviving source.

jungle-king-arcade-disassembly.title: Jungle King
jungle-king-arcade-disassembly.notes: Repository contains a 256 KB Jungle King Z80 listing with a Taito SJ hardware map and a post-processing script. It has no Amiga port source or executable; classified as arcade analysis only.

albank1-jupiter-lander-c64-disassembly.title: Jupiter Lander
albank1-jupiter-lander-c64-disassembly.notes: Ultimax cartridge listing identifies fuel, landing speed and safe-landing branch. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

k240-amiga.title: K240
k240-amiga.notes: Heavily annotated disassembly of the v2.000 main executable; README documents reassembly with vasm and use with the original game files.

k240-amiga-bugfix-disassembly.title: K240 Bugfix
k240-amiga-bugfix-disassembly.display_title: K240 — Amiga disassembly and gameplay repairs
k240-amiga-bugfix-disassembly.notes: Independent, heavily annotated disassembly of K240's play executable, reassembled with vasm as a drop-in replacement for the original game files. Repairs ship, fleet, economy and UI bugs and credits tetracorp's separate K240 analysis for assistance. The patched output is deliberately different from the original, so no original byte-match is asserted.

jotd-karate-champ-amiga.title: Karate Champ — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-karate-champ-amiga.notes: Original arcade Z80→68k transcode. README explicitly credits jotd with Z80 reverse engineering, Z80→68k transcode and Amiga code/assets.

c64-mist64-kernalemu.title: kernalemu
c64-mist64-kernalemu.notes: C reimplementation of Commodore KERNAL API with 6502 interpreter for command-line PET/C64/C128/TED/C65 PRGs; examples run C64 BASIC V2. Tape, RS-232 and IEEE-488 functions are explicitly unsupported or incomplete.

kickoff2-tactical-editor.title: Kick Off 2 — tactic file editor
kickoff2-tactical-editor.notes: Java editor for original Kick Off 2 tactic files. README identifies both game releases; no claim of game-code reconstruction or verified interchange between their specific file variants.

kings-valley-msx-annotated-disassembly.title: King's Valley
kings-valley-msx-annotated-disassembly.display_title: King's Valley — annotated MSX ROM disassembly
kings-valley-msx-annotated-disassembly.notes: Annotated disassembly of Konami's RC727 game. Sjasm can assemble either ROM version using VERSION2; version 2 contains bug fixes. The source file documents the original/version differences; the README does not claim byte-identical builds.

knight-lore-tcdev-spectrum.title: Knight Lore — tcdev
knight-lore-tcdev-spectrum.notes: tcdev Knight Lore reverse engineering in a repository designed for reassemblable and relocatable source.

knight-tyme-spectrum.title: Knight Tyme
knight-tyme-spectrum.notes: Complete 48K RAM disassembly by Philip M. Anderson; source preserved in Michael Cook's ZX Spectrum games archive.

knightmare-amiga.title: Knightmare
knightmare-amiga.notes: Ongoing reverse-engineering and analysis of Tony Crowther's 1991 Amiga RPG.

kung-fu-master-c64-analyser.title: Kung Fu Master
kung-fu-master-c64-analyser.display_title: Kung Fu Master — C64 analyser project
kung-fu-master-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The KungFuMaster directory contains an Analysis.json annotation database (644 KiB), saved analysis state (1235 KiB), emulator save state and project configuration. Tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

l-packer-amiga-atari.title: L-Packer
l-packer-amiga-atari.display_title: L-Packer — Atari ST and Amiga executable cruncher
source_language: Amiga HUNK and Atari executable formats
l-packer-amiga-atari.notes: Author distributes a v0.99 beta executable compressor for Atari ST and Amiga with benchmark and usage documentation. GitHub repository currently holds a binary, not the promised full source; buildability and implementation details are unverified. Included as directly relevant development tooling with that limitation visible.

abadia-crimen-cpc.title: La Abadía del Crimen
abadia-crimen-cpc.notes: Preservation/reverse-engineering project containing the historical CPC disassembly plus modern asset extraction, script decompilation and Python/JavaScript reconstruction tooling.

lander-archimedes-moxon.title: Lander — Acorn Archimedes reconstruction
lander-archimedes-moxon.notes: David Braben's Lander reconstructed by hand from Arthur/RISC OS binaries. The build system reports all compiled binaries matching the originals for both variants.

laser-zone-c64-bumblingcoda.title: Laser Zone
laser-zone-c64-bumblingcoda.notes: The author explicitly presents this as an in-progress disassembly of Jeff Minter's C64 Laser Zone. The repository contains substantial assembly across game-loop, enemies, screen, initialization and asset files, but gives no verified build or runtime claim.

laserwarp-cpc.title: Laserwarp
laserwarp-cpc.notes: Full annotated disassembly from a CRC-verified original cassette image; round-trip reconstruction reproduces the complete 18,688-byte game image exactly.

albank1-lemans-c64-disassembly.title: Le Mans
albank1-lemans-c64-disassembly.notes: Independent cartridge listing marks a bonus/difficulty table and makes a small correction; author explicitly compares the deeper Ricardo Quesada project rather than deriving from it. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

lemans-c64-ricardoquesada.title: Le Mans
lemans-c64-ricardoquesada.display_title: Le Mans — C64 full disassembly & patchable reconstruction
lemans-c64-ricardoquesada.notes: Full C64 Le Mans disassembly based on the original cartridge, with comments and optional patches for rumble, joystick control, typo correction and conversion from cartridge to PRG. The README provides a current disk image and a 64tass make/run workflow.

legacy-of-the-ancients-c64-redux.title: Legacy of the Ancients
legacy-of-the-ancients-c64-redux.display_title: Legacy of the Ancients — C64 data research and browser adaptation
source_language: C64 disk images and game binaries
legacy-of-the-ancients-c64-redux.notes: Research-led browser adaptation with original C64 disk inventory, loader/resource decoding, recovered maps, and emulator-verified gameplay observations. Public README describes first playable views but links to a private preview, and the full game remains in development; this record covers demonstrable format research and partial reimplementation.

legend-amiga-horace.title: Legend / Four Crystals of Trazere — Amiga resource reverse engineering
legend-amiga-horace.display_title: Legend / Four Crystals of Trazere — Amiga resource reverse engineering
legend-amiga-horace.notes: Reverse-engineering investigation of Legend / Four Crystals of Trazere. The project reconstructs the PAC decompression algorithm from the supplied Amiga resources and 68000 loader, decodes 93 PAC resources / 296 blocks, and rebuilds structured graphics and scene assets while retaining unresolved areas as research targets.

vs-sr-cd32-legends.title: Legends — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-legends.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Legends. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

lemmings-amiga-html5-editor.title: Lemmings — Amiga game-data editor
lemmings-amiga-html5-editor.notes: Browser editor imports LHA, disk images and loose Amiga data; parses Lemmings file table and graphics/level formats. README reports byte-identical round trips of 100 unmodified level records, but edited output is not yet a bootable replacement package.

level9-l9dev-toolchain-reconstruction.title: Level 9 l9dev toolchain reconstruction
level9-l9dev-toolchain-reconstruction.display_title: Level 9 l9dev — reconstructed Atari ST authoring toolchain
level9-l9dev-toolchain-reconstruction.notes: Level 9 development tools recoded in C from Atari ST 68000 assembler. Includes compiler, finisher, squasher and table-generation tooling, compatibility modes and regression runs against salvaged game sources.

level9-next-amiga-st-bitmap-converter.title: Level 9 Spectrum Next bitmap converter
source_language: Amiga and Atari ST Level 9 bitmap files
level9-next-amiga-st-bitmap-converter.notes: Spectrum Next port of Glen Summers’s reverse-engineered Level 9 interpreter. Its convert_bitmap tool transforms original Amiga and ST Level 9 bitmap images to NXI; this record highlights the verified asset bridge, not a native Amiga/ST runtime. V1 story format is deliberately omitted in the constrained Next port.

vs-sr-cd32-liberation.title: Liberation: Captive II — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-liberation.display_title: Liberation: Captive II — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-liberation.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Liberation: Captive II. c64-light-fantastic-broadcast-recovery.title: Light Fantastic C64 reverse engineering
c64-light-fantastic-broadcast-recovery.display_title: Light Fantastic — C64 TV broadcast receiver disassembly
subjects: Light Fantastic tuning and receiver programs
c64-light-fantastic-broadcast-recovery.notes: Disassembled C64 tuning and receiver programs from the 1985 Light Fantastic televised software-transmission experiment and documented receiver behaviour; the author says the recovered receiver appears to lack the storage part.

light-force-spectrum-analyser.title: Light Force
light-force-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Light Force — ZX Spectrum analyser project
light-force-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Light Force directory contains an approximately 596 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

lime-juice-mes-tooling.title: lime-juice
lime-juice-mes-tooling.display_title: lime-juice — PC-98 MES compiler/decompiler and image toolkit
lime-juice-mes-tooling.notes: C++ port and expansion of tomyun's Juice tool. It decompiles MES scripts to readable RKT and compiles them back, while juice-img round-trips GP4, GPC and GPA images; unresolved opcodes remain explicit raw commands rather than guessed semantics.

little-computer-people-st-analysis.title: Little Computer People
little-computer-people-st-analysis.display_title: Little Computer People — byte-identical Atari ST C reconstruction
little-computer-people-st-analysis.notes: Current CLAUDE.md and source/tools/run_all.sh document a complete Alcyon C reconstruction of the shipped Atari ST executable, byte-identical across the 123,352-byte PRG. The original build is byte-compared; emulator runtime tests use a separate gated build to bypass original copy protection. Root README and source/STATUS.md describe earlier stages and are stale.

livingstone-spectrum-analyser.title: Livingstone I Presume
livingstone-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Livingstone I Presume — ZX Spectrum analyser project
livingstone-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Livingstone I Presume directory contains an approximately 1933 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus five custom Lua debug/formatter/room/scenery/sprite viewers. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

jotd-lock-n-chase-amiga.title: Lock 'n' Chase — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-lock-n-chase-amiga.notes: Lock 'n' Chase arcade transcode for Amiga; README explicitly credits reverse engineering and 6502→68000 conversion while retaining the original game code/sound/graphics.

lode-runner-c64.title: Lode Runner
lode-runner-c64.notes: Commented reconstructed source including copy protection; repository description states the goal is a bit-for-bit identical recreation.

lode-runner-apple2-xekri.title: Lode Runner — Apple II byte-perfect reconstruction
lode-runner-apple2-xekri.display_title: Lode Runner — Apple II byte-perfect reconstruction
lode-runner-apple2-xekri.notes: Literate reverse engineering of the original Apple II Lode Runner. The reconstructed assembly builds the game binary and reconstructs the DOS 3.3 disk layout, including boot/levels/catalog and stale sector slack, to reproduce the reference disk byte-for-byte.

lode-runner-apple2-fschuhi-analysis.title: Lode Runner — Apple II research and core-game specification
lode-runner-apple2-fschuhi-analysis.upstream_name: Lode Runner — Apple II research and core-game specification
lode-runner-apple2-fschuhi-analysis.display_title: Lode Runner — Apple II research and core-game specification
subjects: Lode Runner — Apple II research and core-game specification
lode-runner-apple2-fschuhi-analysis.notes: Research layer built on XekriRedmane's byte-perfect Apple II Lode Runner reconstruction. It analyses implementation, data layout, timing and subsystem interactions and turns that understanding into a platform-neutral Core Game Spec, while preserving links back to the literate 6502 evidence.

lode-runner-bbc-0xc0de6502.title: lode-runner-disassembled
lode-runner-bbc-0xc0de6502.notes: Disassembly of the BBC Micro main Lode Runner binary (LODE1), published as labelled/commented BeebAsm-compatible 6502 source. The repository explicitly identifies the scope as the main binary rather than a complete disk reconstruction.

lotus-ste-enhancement.title: Lotus STE
lotus-ste-enhancement.notes: Reverse engineered ST-side routines and patch build add blitter graphics and sampled audio. Requires separately obtained Empire version game files. Builds a bootable image; full enhancements need STE with at least 1 MiB RAM, while blitter-equipped ST models run a subset.

lunar-jetman-spectrum.title: Lunar Jetman
lunar-jetman-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

lxa-linux-amiga-layer.title: lxa
lxa-linux-amiga-layer.notes: Runs AmigaOS command-line and application binaries using 68000 CPU emulation with Linux-backed AmigaOS libraries and filesystem calls. README documents building and running example programs; broad compatibility and RTG development are ongoing rather than established for all Amiga software.

m68k-assembler-disassembler-attackwave.title: m68k assembler/disassembler — Amiga Hunk aware
m68k-assembler-disassembler-attackwave.notes: Two-pass Rust assembler and disassembler with explicit 68000–68060 CPU limits, FPU/MMU decoding and Amiga Hunk relocation/symbol support. Repository documents Hunk output roundtrips and a cargo release build; these are tool-format claims, not a verified runtime minimum for an Amiga game.

m68k-reversing-toolkit-rmtew.title: M68k Reversing Toolkit — generated Amiga analysis
m68k-reversing-toolkit-rmtew.upstream_name: M68k Reversing Toolkit — generated Amiga analysis
m68k-reversing-toolkit-rmtew.display_title: M68k Reversing Toolkit — generated Amiga analysis
m68k-reversing-toolkit-rmtew.notes: LLM-written experimental toolkit under human direction: generated M68k/Amiga knowledge bases feed C assembler/disassembler and Python web/API orchestration, with per-target reports and round-trip validation. README explicitly discloses AI implementation; exact playable or byte-identical project outputs must be evaluated separately.

m68k-tools-grahambates.title: m68k-tools
m68k-tools-grahambates.notes: Motorola 68000 assembly tooling used across retro-development workflows: parser, formatter, cycle counter, static-analysis/lint libraries and language servers with CLI, VS Code and web front ends. Tracked as adjacent m68k development/analysis infrastructure rather than a platform-specific reconstruction project.

mama-llama-c64.title: Mama Llama
mama-llama-c64.notes: Llamasoft Source Project disassembly of Mama Llama; the collection describes this as a first-pass reconstruction separating game code from data and providing a runnable build.

manic-miner-spectrum-analyser.title: Manic Miner
manic-miner-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Manic Miner — ZX Spectrum analyser project

Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

manic-miner-bbc-tobylobster.title: ManicMiner
manic-miner-bbc-tobylobster.display_title: Manic Miner — BBC Micro byte-exact disassembly
manic-miner-bbc-tobylobster.notes: BBC Micro Manic Miner disassembly/reassembly with extensive commentary on loading, obfuscation, copy protection, graphics/collision behaviour and level formats. The ACME source reproduces the analysed preservation copy byte-for-byte; that input copy already bypasses the original paper-code check, although the original protection logic remains present in the game code.

maptapper-amiga-graphics-ripper.notes: Codetapper’s Windows application loads WinUAE savestates and memory dumps to find tiles, palettes, maps and Copper lists. marble-madness-ii-arcade-render-study.title: Marble Madness II
marble-madness-ii-arcade-render-study.display_title: Marble Madness II — arcade video-memory render study

remom-amiga.title: Master of Magic — ReMoM Amiga port

mastervamp-hitchhikr.title: MasterVamp
mastervamp-hitchhikr.notes: Beta emulator for Sega Master System, Game Gear and SG-1000 and CBS ColecoVision on Apollo Vampire Amiga accelerator cards; project README identifies beta status.

match-it-st-browser-port.title: Match-IT! browser port
match-it-st-browser-port.notes: Browser port and detailed analysis of Match-IT! using a released original 68000 source file and assets. Translates behavior, graphics and YM2149 music to JavaScript; this is a source-informed port, not a disassembly or byte-exact reconstruction of the ST binary.

matchpatch-amiga.title: MatchPatch
matchpatch-amiga.notes: Contains preserved original Devpac assembly plus Tetracorp analysis and extracted maps; tracked as an analysis-adjacent exception rather than reconstructed source.

albank1-matrix-c64-disassembly.title: Matrix
albank1-matrix-c64-disassembly.notes: Independent labelled disassembly of the C64 Matrix PRG and its BASIC stub that relocates code to a cartridge-like $8000 entry. matrix-c64.title: Matrix / Gridrunner 2

c64-spixs-jmazemaster.title: Maze Master
c64-spixs-jmazemaster.display_title: Maze Master — C64 cartridge study and Java remake
c64-spixs-jmazemaster.notes: C64 cartridge disassembly at c64_resources/source.asm alongside a Java/Swing recreation that cites ROM addresses and game labels. Maven build and run instructions are documented; source claims a complete logic reconstruction, while byte equality is not claimed.

winuae-gdb-mcp-axewater.title: mcp-winuae-emu
winuae-gdb-mcp-axewater.display_title: WinUAE MCP — Amiga memory and Copper debugger
winuae-gdb-mcp-axewater.notes: MCP server talks to a custom WinUAE GDB fork, exposing registers, memory, watchpoints, single stepping and Copper-list disassembly to AI assistants; requires separate WinUAE fork and user-supplied Kickstart ROM/configuration.

mega-man-3-nes-refreshing-lemonade.title: Mega Man 3

mega-man-4-nes-refreshing-lemonade.title: Mega Man 4

mega-man-5-nes-refreshing-lemonade.title: Mega Man 5

mega-man-6-nes-refreshing-lemonade.title: Mega Man 6

metagalactic-llamas-vic20.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1984 VIC-20 game Metagalactic Llamas: Battle at the Edge of Time; the Llamasoft Source Project describes it as mostly completely commented.

metal-gear-msx2-guillianseed.title: Metal Gear
metal-gear-msx2-guillianseed.display_title: Metal Gear — annotated MSX2 ROM reconstruction
metal-gear-msx2-guillianseed.notes: Fully annotated disassembly of Konami's 1987 RC750 MSX2 release. The README documents Sjasm builds for the Japanese and English ROMs and gives their expected CRC32 values.

metroid-nes-nmikstas.title: metroid-disassembly
metroid-nes-nmikstas.notes: NES Metroid disassembly split across the game's eight 16 KiB banks. metroid-nes-mstan-recomp.title: MetroidNESRecomp
metroid-nes-mstan-recomp.notes: Uses NESRecomp on Metroid (USA) to translate original 6502 code to native x64 C and run against simulated NES hardware. micro-painter-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Micro-Painter
micro-painter-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of Micro-Painter's Applesoft and Integer BASIC front ends plus PAINT and CURSOR machine-language routines, with SourceGen files/binaries and detailed analysis of zoom editing and flood-fill behavior.

vs-sr-cd32-microcosm.title: Microcosm — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation

midimaze-browser-source-port.title: MIDI Maze JS
midimaze-browser-source-port.display_title: MIDI Maze — browser port from reconstructed ST source
midimaze-browser-source-port.notes: Playable solo browser recreation derived line by line from sarnau’s reconstructed Atari ST C source. midi-maze-2-title-music-reconstruction.title: MIDI-MAZE II title music and player reconstruction
midi-maze-2-title-music-reconstruction.display_title: MIDI-MAZE II — Atari ST title music and player reconstruction

punchout-nes-nmikstas.title: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!!

missile-command-arcade-6502disassembly.title: Missile Command
missile-command-arcade-6502disassembly.display_title: Missile Command — arcade 6502 disassembly & hardware/gameplay analysis
missile-command-arcade-6502disassembly.notes: Missile Command rev 3 disassembly with SourceGen project files/binaries, binary-construction instructions and deep analysis of attack waves, unusual video memory, revision differences, bugs, rendering and game-state behavior.

monty-run-c64-dave-agent.display_title: Monty on the Run — C64 byte-perfect reconstruction & refactor

morpheus-c64-mwenge.title: Morpheus
morpheus-c64-mwenge.notes: Reverse-engineered, commented 6502 source with a 64tass/VICE build and documented playable result. Main game routines are labelled while some asset and minigame data remains to be annotated.Separate from the existing analysis-state entry where one exists.

mr-do-amiga-jotd.title: Mr. Do! — Amiga 68k translation
mr-do-amiga-jotd.notes: Project-specific 333 KB Z80 listing and 73 KB Amiga driver include Mr. Do! sprite handling and a distinct high-score filename. README describes Jail Break and the driver starts from a Dig Dug template; catalogued as incomplete conversion with no build/playability assertion.

mystic-dune-ii-trainer.title: MyStiC Dune II trainer menu
mystic-dune-ii-trainer.display_title: Dune II — MyStiC Amiga trainer reconstruction
mystic-dune-ii-trainer.notes: Source identifies Colorboy's MyStiC trainer menu, reconstructs Motorola 68000 instructions and embeds data regions reported byte-exact against a Ghidra export. Build command is documented, but original-binary matching and execution are not established.

vs-sr-cd32-myth.title: Myth — History in the Making — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-myth.display_title: Myth — History in the Making — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-myth.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Myth — History in the Making. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

nebulus-spectrum.title: Nebulus
nebulus-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Some progress.

np2debug-pc98-debugger.title: Neko Project II - Debug Edition
np2debug-pc98-debugger.display_title: Neko Project II Debug Edition — PC-98 binary debugger
np2debug-pc98-debugger.notes: Neko Project II fork designed to make modification of PC-98 binaries practical. It adds stepping, code and memory breakpoints, searching/modification, stack inspection and Shift-JIS display, and was tested specifically against Touhou 1–5 for translation-patch development.

neost-atari-emulator.title: NeoST
neost-atari-emulator.display_title: NeoST — Atari ST/STE emulator and debugger
neost-atari-emulator.notes: Chip-oriented ST/Mega ST/STE/Mega STE emulator using Moira 68000 and comparing hardware behavior with Hatari. Its debugger exposes symbols, disassembly, breakpoints, watchpoints and headless operation. The README advertises desktop, web and Android packages; it explicitly says the Android APK was tested under QEMU but not on a real device.

nesrecomp-static-recompiler.title: NESRecomp
nesrecomp-static-recompiler.notes: Translates NES ROM 6502 machine code into C and provides a PPU/APU/mapper runner; generated C alone is not a playable game. The 26 September master merge adds an opt-in cycle-accurate compiler/runtime with bounded interpreter fallback, trace-parity verification and documented nonzero-alignment limits; the same day's netplay merge adds rollback, multi-seat lobbies and deterministic state validation. README describes Windows x64 as mature, macOS as experimental and Linux as not fully tested; no minimum host CPU/RAM is stated.

nether-earth-spectrum.title: Nether Earth
nether-earth-spectrum.notes: Annotated disassembly that can be assembled back into a game binary using the included build script.

nevryon-bbc-reconstruction.title: Nevryon — BBC Micro binary reconstruction
nevryon-bbc-reconstruction.notes: Extracts and documents the BBC Micro game's loader, code, level tables, graphics and sound. README reports BeebAsm byte-identical rebuilding of four extracted binaries; the status of a complete playable disk is not established.

new-ghostbusters-ii-nes-g0me3.title: New Ghostbusters II
new-ghostbusters-ii-nes-g0me3.display_title: New Ghostbusters II (NES) — Back From Source
new-ghostbusters-ii-nes-g0me3.notes: The Back From Source repository includes annotated banked assembly, level/music material, notes and scripts assembling a NES image with DASM. RetroRE marks the effort partial. Byte identity and runnable minimums are not established by the examined files.

newtua-amiga-archive-decoders.title: newtua-formats
newtua-amiga-archive-decoders.notes: Multi-platform Rust decoder crates port legacy algorithms from The Unarchiver/XADMaster; the Amiga crate handles PowerPacker, LZX and DMS including encrypted DMS and FMS files. README excludes LZX block type 1 and DMS self-extracting wrappers. Distinct from xdms-rs and other single-format tools.

jotd-nibbler-amiga.title: Nibbler — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-nibbler-amiga.notes: OCS Amiga Nibbler remake; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

night-world-bbc-zornslemma.title: Night World
night-world-bbc-zornslemma.display_title: Night World — BBC Micro partial source reconstruction
night-world-bbc-zornslemma.notes: Partial BBC Micro Night World reconstruction. The build generates py8dis-derived assembly, reconstructs BASIC portions, reassembles with BeebAsm and verifies key rebuilt components against original binaries before producing a disc image; profiling and sprite-analysis material are also retained.

nitecrwl-atari-st.title: NiteCrawl
nitecrwl-atari-st.notes: Repository description calls this a decompiled Atari ST game; tree contains substantial C++ gameplay/rendering code, AES/VDI headers and a cross-build Makefile. Original binary identity, matching and runtime verification are undocumented, so those claims remain unknown.

octan-spectrum-analyser.title: Octan
octan-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Octan directory contains an approximately 342 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

oh-mummy-resurrected-cpc.title: Oh Mummy Resurrected
oh-mummy-resurrected-cpc.notes: CP Soft disassembled the original Oh Mummy and developed an enhanced Plus/GX4000 adaptation. The project's itch.io page explicitly states that no generative AI was used.

oktalyzer-amiga-hitchhikr.title: Oktalyzer
oktalyzer-amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Complete disassembly of the Amiga music tool Oktalyzer, with ongoing reconstruction and modernization. The project documents fixes for AGA/RTG, a new software-mixer replay, Vampire hardware-channel support, module compatibility work and a planned standalone replay routine.

albank1-omega-race-c64-disassembly.title: Omega Race
albank1-omega-race-c64-disassembly.notes: Cartridge listing identifies lives and C64 hardware register accesses; distinct analysis of a historical game that also has an original-source archive elsewhere. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

open-captive-yeager.title: OpenCaptive
open-captive-yeager.notes: Source-faithful modern reimplementation. README reports a playable DOS-based Captive compatibility slice and verified CD32 data and city-system slices for Liberation, while original navigation, full campaigns and parity remain active work. Amiga/ST ancestry must not be read as runtime parity for their versions.

dos-opencrystalcaves.title: OpenCrystalCaves
dos-opencrystalcaves.notes: Unofficial modern engine using original game data; README states episode 1 is playable while episodes 2/3, saving and some audio/UI behavior remain incomplete. CPU of original binary not independently established.

dos-openprototype.title: OpenPrototype
dos-openprototype.display_title: Prototype (1995) — DOS CD game reverse-engineered port
dos-openprototype.notes: From-scratch port of the 1995 DOS shooter; README reports all seven levels and ending playable using original disc image. Documents original programmer's format notes, manual Ghidra analysis, later AI-assisted implementation; modern code is not source-level decompilation.

amixcom-amiga.notes: Native classic-Amiga port of OpenXcom, the open-source X-COM reimplementation. The whole game runs on AmigaOS; the README explicitly credits Claude Code for development.

papple2-apple2-debugger.title: papple2
papple2-apple2-debugger.notes: Small Apple II emulator deliberately built as a reverse-engineering/debugging instrument rather than a general player. paradroid-bbc-kieranhj.title: Paradroid
paradroid-bbc-kieranhj.display_title: Paradroid — C64-to-BBC Micro faithful reverse-engineered port

paradroid90-nitro-music-drivers.title: Paradroid 90 / Nitro music-driver reconstruction

paranoimia-vector-logo-amiga.title: Paranoimia Vector Logo intro
paranoimia-vector-logo-amiga.notes: ReSource disassembly and commented modernization of Paranoimia vector-logo intro with both original-form and updated assembly. Author documents assembling and running on Amiga/emulator; no binary identity claim.

pc98-vn-research-valleybell.title: PC-98 Visual Novel/ADV engine research
pc98-vn-research-valleybell.display_title: PC-98 Visual Novel Research — engine disassembly and format toolkit

pce-analyser-8bit-analysers.title: PCE Analyser
pce-analyser-8bit-analysers.display_title: PCE Analyser — PC Engine/HuC6280 reverse-engineering toolkit

peasauce-disassembler-rmtew.title: Peasauce — interactive Amiga/ST/X68000 disassembler
peasauce-disassembler-rmtew.notes: Interactive Python/Qt disassembler that loads Amiga, Atari ST and X68000 68k executables, raw binaries with explicit addresses, and editable labels. README says m68k and executable-format support is not complete; no general byte-identical reassembly claim.

jotd-pengo-amiga.title: Pengo — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-pengo-amiga.notes: Original Pengo Z80 arcade game transcoded to 68k assembly; README credits Z80 reverse engineering and Z80→68k transcode.

penny-arcade-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Penny Arcade
penny-arcade-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Penny Arcade — Apple II mixed BASIC/assembly disassembly
penny-arcade-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of Bill Budge's 1979 Apple II Penny Arcade, whose Applesoft BASIC and assembly routines were embedded in a single cassette program. pentagram-tcdev-spectrum.title: Pentagram — tcdev

phantoms-five-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Phantoms Five
phantoms-five-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Phantoms Five disassembly covering the game and title sequence. The project provides SourceGen files/binaries and documents reconstruction of a suitable analysis binary from the cracked disk's custom loader layout.

pharaohs-curse-atari8-sarnau.title: Pharaoh's Curse
pharaohs-curse-atari8-sarnau.display_title: Pharaoh's Curse — Atari 8-bit disassembly & protection analysis
pharaohs-curse-atari8-sarnau.notes: Documented Atari 400/800 source reconstruction from protected ATX media. jotd-phoenix-amiga.title: Phoenix — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-phoenix-amiga.notes: ECS/AGA Phoenix remake using reverse engineering and transcode work; README notes that the original code was transcoded while documenting a remaining behavioural discrepancy.

phoenixbasic-gfa-basic-atari-st.title: PhoenixBasic — GFA BASIC 3.5 compatible interpreter

phr-crew-sin-intro-amiga.title: PHR-Crew The Sin Intro
phr-crew-sin-intro-amiga.notes: ReSource disassembly and modernization of PHR-Crew The Sin Intro with extracted assets and 68000 assembly. No explicit build verification or binary identity claim.

pitfall-ii-c64.title: Pitfall II
