evidence.excerpt: The x86-64 binaries need AVX2 (Intel Haswell 2013+, AMD Zen 2017+). On an older CPU, use png2amiga-windows-x86_64-compat.exe from the same release.

png2amiga-multiplatform-asset-converter.notes: Cross-platform image/asset converter for Amiga, Atari ST/STE, IBM PC, C64, Genesis, SNES Mode 7, Game Boy Advance, Sega Master System/Game Gear, Amstrad CPC/CPC Plus, Thomson and Commodore TED targets. v1.109.0 (25 September 2026) added SMS/GG and CPC/CPC Plus output modes with packed-output round-trip tests. The README documents native CMake builds, a WebAssembly web app and pre-built desktop releases; standard x86-64 binaries require AVX2, while a compatibility build is provided for older x86-64 CPUs.

jotd-pooyan-amiga.title: Pooyan — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-pooyan-amiga.notes: Pooyan arcade port for Amiga; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

vs-sr-cd32-powerdrive.title: Power Drive — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-powerdrive.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Power Drive. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

powerpacker-decompiled-lab313ru.title: PowerPacker 36.10 — decompiled compressor
powerpacker-decompiled-lab313ru.notes: Dr. MefistO states that the original PowerPacker library and compression algorithm, including password/encryption handling, were decompiled into a usable compressor/decompressor. The repository includes a Visual Studio project and test script; no Amiga-native rebuilt binary or byte-identity proof is established.

prehistorik-amiga-demo-browser-rewrite.title: Prehistorik Amiga demo — browser rewrite
prehistorik-amiga-demo-browser-rewrite.notes: Rewrites only the first-level playable Amiga Prehistorik demo from its ADF; the author README links a browser version. The reviewed README and complete source/tool tree do not identify the original executable CPU, so none is inferred from the Amiga/ADF label. This is not a full-game reconstruction or a DOS data port.

vs-sr-cd32-prey.title: Prey: An Alien Encounter — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-prey.display_title: Prey: An Alien Encounter — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-prey.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Prey: An Alien Encounter. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

programmers-aid-apple2-james-davis.title: Programmer's Aid #1
programmers-aid-apple2-james-davis.display_title: Programmer's Aid #1 — Apple II ROM disassembly
programmers-aid-apple2-james-davis.notes: James P. Davis annotated the Programmer’s Aid #1 ROM as separate listings covering high-resolution graphics, program renumbering and append, relocation, tape verification, RAM test and music. The pages identify Davis’s SourceGen analysis and link the original Apple manual as background. SourceGen project file and binaries are linked from the ROM index.

project-eon-yeager.title: Project Eon
project-eon-yeager.notes: Cross-platform reimplementation with separate Original and opt-in Modern modes. Recovery paths depend on verified original media evidence; source platforms and runtime fidelity vary by game/version, and a fully playable campaign is a goal rather than a verified claim.

pssst-spectrum.title: Pssst
pssst-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

psychedelia-colourspace-reconstruction.title: Psychedelia / Colourspace
psychedelia-colourspace-reconstruction.notes: Reverse-engineered and commented source collection for Jeff Minter's early light synthesizers: Psychedelia on C64/VIC-20/C16 and Colourspace on Atari 8-bit, with buildable versions for the documented platforms.

ptvpack-hitchhikr.title: PtvPack
ptvpack-hitchhikr.notes: ProTracker/NoiseTracker/FastTracker MOD packer and replay routine for Apollo Vampire hardware; README describes 1–16 channels and optional sample packing. Windows and Amiga command-line packers supplied.

puae-debugger-vscode.title: PUAE Debugger
puae-debugger-vscode.display_title: PUAE Debugger — Amiga source debugger & profiler
puae-debugger-vscode.notes: Amiga debugger/profiler built around the WinUAE-derived PUAE core. Supports Hunk/ELF debug information, source and instruction breakpoints, data watchpoints, reverse execution, CPU/DMA profiling, Copper/blitter inspection, memory reconstruction, standalone DAP use and headless MCP-driven emulator inspection.

pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.title: Pure C/Pascal help tools — Atari ST reconstruction
pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.upstream_name: Pure C/Pascal help tools — Atari ST reconstruction
pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.display_title: Pure C/Pascal help tools — Atari ST reconstruction
source_language: Pure C/Pascal help compiler and viewer executables
pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.notes: Compiler and viewer sources reconstructed from Pure C and Pure Pascal executables. An orig branch can compile to almost identical originals; master improves functionality. The decompiler is mostly based on a contemporary published article and should not be presented as binary-derived.

pushover-dos-browser.title: Pushover
source_language: Pushover DOS executable and game data
pushover-dos-browser.notes: Playable browser reimplementation based on the DOS executable and user-provided DOS assets, using static and live DOSBox tracing. Historical Amiga/ST releases are mentioned but their media are not analyzed or accepted; original data omission is normal bring-your-own-data design.

py8dis-zornslemma.title: py8dis
py8dis-zornslemma.notes: Programmable Python static-tracing disassembler supporting 6502, 65C02 and 8080 binaries. It handles runtime relocation, user-defined labels/data structures and optional input MD5 verification, and emits source for assemblers including beebasm, ACME, xa and z88dk-z80asm. It underpins several BBC Micro reconstruction projects discovered in the same graph.

c64-esshahn-pydisass6502.title: pyDisass6502
c64-esshahn-pydisass6502.notes: Python 6502/C64 PRG disassembler with opcode tables, optional user-specified code/data entry points and C64 hardware-map comments. README says early but functional, and documents command-line input/output and Fairlight example.

pyramid-warp-msx-enhanced-disassembly.title: Pyramid Warp
pyramid-warp-msx-enhanced-disassembly.display_title: Pyramid Warp — MSX disassembly and enhanced ROMs

runtime_profiles.name: Enhanced ROM
runtime_profiles.notes: The README states the enhanced variant moves RAM start to $E000 and requires 8 KB; this is not a requirement for the original ROM.

evidence.excerpt: Moved RAM start from $C000 to $E000 (RAM requirement is now 8KB)

pyramid-warp-msx-enhanced-disassembly.notes: Annotated 1983 T&E SOFT ROM assembles to the original verbatim. Enhanced and Enhanced+ variants change graphics, sound, rooms and difficulty; their outputs should not be described as byte-identical to the original. README states the enhanced RAM start is $E000 and its RAM requirement is 8 KB, but does not establish the original ROM's minimum.

pad-amiga-disassembler.title: Pyrdacor Amiga Disassembler (pad)
pad-amiga-disassembler.notes: Early-stage tool intended to translate compiled Amiga executables back into recompilable 68k assembly. README explicitly describes the desired output as a goal, not an achieved byte-identical reconstruction.

quazatron-spectrum-analyser.title: Quazatron
quazatron-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The directory contains a ~1.11 MB Analysis.json database, a ~353 KB exported Quazatron.asm listing, configuration/graphics metadata and custom Lua analysis/viewer scripts; tracked as binary-analysis/assembler-export work rather than claiming a byte-exact source reconstruction.

jotd-rally-x-amiga.title: Rally-X — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-rally-x-amiga.notes: Namco Rally-X Amiga port with explicit Z80 reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

rambo-nes-g0me3.title: Rambo
rambo-nes-g0me3.notes: The repository describes itself as Rambo (NES) Back From Source and contains reconstructed bank assembly, game data, levels, scripts, music/player material and build scripts. A NES image build path is present; runtime and byte identity remain unverified.

rambo-c64-ricardoquesada.title: Rambo: First Blood Part II
rambo-c64-ricardoquesada.display_title: Rambo: First Blood Part II — C64 disassembly & patchable reconstruction
rambo-c64-ricardoquesada.notes: Commented C64 Rambo disassembly with a build-and-run workflow and optional gameplay/hardware patches, including copy-protection removal, single-load conversion, gamepad weapon switching and rumble support. The README supplies a current disk binary and gameplay instructions.

rampage-spectrum.title: Rampage
rampage-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

ranarama-spectrum-analyser.title: Ranarama
ranarama-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Ranarama directory contains a 1361 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and exported Z80 assembly and several buffer/screen analysis scripts. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

rastan-spectrum-analyser.title: Rastan
rastan-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Rastan directory contains an approximately 466 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

rawgl-another-world-engine.title: raw(gl) — Another World engine reimplementation
rawgl-another-world-engine.notes: Reimplements the Another World virtual-machine/game engine. Primary README explicitly accepts original Amiga Bank*, Atari Bank* and Atari AW.TOS demo data, alongside DOS, 3DO and other editions; users supply data. Platform-specific exact behavioral parity is not asserted.

raw2iff-amiga-st-hitchhikr.title: raw2iff — Amiga/ST graphics converter
raw2iff-amiga-st-hitchhikr.notes: Plugin-based raw graphics to IFF ILBM converter, with explicit Atari ST interleaved input and Amiga planar/bitplane options. Author supplies Windows and Amiga executables and documents palette/offset/stride controls; this is asset extraction tooling rather than a game disassembly.

dos-rayman-disasm.title: rayman_disasm
dos-rayman-disasm.notes: README documents stripping a 16-bit DOS extender around a 32-bit game and the gog/ tree contains a large rayman_disasm.S listing. Research output is an analysis/disassembly, not a working port.

rdos-apple2-6502disassembly.title: RDOS
rdos-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of SSI's compact RDOS 3.3 disk operating system, with SourceGen project files/binaries and documentation of its filesystem and Applesoft ampersand-command interface. The author notes an earlier full RDOS 2.1 disassembly was used to develop ProDOS RDOS.

rec98-touhou-pc98.title: ReC98
rec98-touhou-pc98.display_title: ReC98 — bit-perfect Touhou PC-98 source reconstruction
rec98-touhou-pc98.notes: Reconstructs the first five Touhou games for NEC PC-9801 from their binaries. Upstream states that every commit builds executables indistinguishable from the originals; TH01 is complete while the remaining games continue to be reverse engineered and finalized.

dos-clyde-re.title: reclyde
dos-clyde-re.display_title: Clyde's Adventure — DOS executable and asset analysis
dos-clyde-re.notes: Partial executable disassembly and tools for RLE, EGA images and castle layouts; extractors recover some volumes and first six castles. Runnable refers to the analysis extractors, not a playable game reconstruction.

regenerator2000-commodore-disassembler.title: Regenerator 2000
regenerator2000-commodore-disassembler.display_title: Regenerator 2000 — Commodore 6502 disassembler, debugger & MCP RE workbench
regenerator2000-commodore-disassembler.notes: Modern interactive 6502 disassembler for Commodore 8-bit systems. It combines manual code/data/graphics analysis, VICE debugging, automatic packed-program emulation/unpacking, assembly/HTML export, headless round-trip assemble/diff verification and an MCP server with analysis skills for automated reverse engineering.

reject-st-demo-reconstruction.title: Reject demo — reconstructed Atari ST source
reject-st-demo-reconstruction.upstream_name: Reject demo — reconstructed Atari ST source
reject-st-demo-reconstruction.display_title: Reject demo — reconstructed Atari ST source

runtime_profiles.name: Patched Reject demo
runtime_profiles.notes: README also requires hard drive and colour display; emulator configuration can match the machine.

evidence.excerpt: An Atari ST or later with at least 1 megabytes of memory, TOS 1.04 minimum, a hard drive, and a colour display.

reject-st-demo-reconstruction.notes: Senior Dads recreated the lost source and original media from the Reject demo binary, then added music and graphics-mode support. README provides Devpac 3 or vasm/vlink build steps and a patched running version.

reminiscence-flashback-engine.title: REminiscence — Flashback engine reimplementation
reminiscence-flashback-engine.notes: Reimplements the Flashback engine and consumes original DOS, Amiga, Macintosh or PC-98 data files. The reviewed tree contains format/resource decoders rather than a native-instruction translator or executable loader, so a single source CPU is not applicable. Primary README is for release 0.5.6.

repton-2-gfoot-bbc.title: Repton 2 — BBC Micro disassembly
repton-2-gfoot-bbc.notes: A py8dis script annotates Repton 2's main executable and a Makefile drives disassembly/reassembly. The source includes an appended loader that reproduces selected initialization steps; no full disk or byte-exact claim is made here.

repton2-bbc-tobylobster.title: repton2disassembly
repton2-bbc-tobylobster.notes: Disassembly and reassembly of Repton 2's main BBC Micro executable. py8dis scripts generate annotated assembly, a fix-up pass targets xa, and the bundled binary folds initialization behaviour from the original D.REPA loader into a directly launchable form; because that output is intentionally transformed, the tracker does not mark it byte-exact.

dos-shortline-resl.title: reSL
dos-shortline-resl.notes: The original branch preserves per-function offsets into the v1.1 DOS binary; main has an SDL2 C/C++ port with touch controls and changes. Do not treat the modern executable as a byte-exact DOS reassembly.

resource-amiga-reassembler.title: ReSource
resource-amiga-reassembler.notes: Amiga ReSource reassembler/disassembler maintained from a resourced reconstruction of ReSource itself. Development notes describe regenerating assembly from ReSource project data and comparing rebuilt executables; documented assembler differences mean the rebuilt binary is not byte-identical.

resrc4-portable-amiga-hunk-disassembler.title: ReSrc4 — portable Amiga Hunk disassembler
resrc4-portable-amiga-hunk-disassembler.notes: Portable Amiga Hunk disassembler recognizing library calls and some jump tables, with 680x0 and FPU decoding. README reports testing against Civilization ECS, LightWave and an 020-era lha.exe, and documents partial Hunk coverage; the similarly named ReSource project is a separate record.

retro-io-amiga-atari-extractor.title: retro-io
retro-io-amiga-atari-extractor.display_title: retro-io — Amiga ADF and Atari ST/MSA extractor
retro-io-amiga-atari-extractor.notes: Java library and GUI with implemented ADF, ST and MSA extraction, common virtual disk API and ZIP export. README explicitly warns that format support may not be complete; image writing and web interface are planned, not implemented.

retroghidra-atari-st-loader.title: RetroGhidra — Atari ST executable loader
retroghidra-atari-st-loader.notes: Ghidra extension lists its Atari ST executable loader as done. Its Commodore Amiga Hunk loader only identifies files and does not load them yet; no Amiga analysis support is claimed.

return-mutant-camels-c64.title: Return of the Mutant Camels
return-mutant-camels-c64.notes: Llamasoft Source Project disassembly of Return of the Mutant Camels; the collection describes this as a first-pass reconstruction separating game code from data and providing a runnable build.

neuromancer-dos-reuromancer.title: Reuromancer
neuromancer-dos-reuromancer.notes: 64-bit Windows port of the 1988 DOS Neuromancer game. LibNeuroRoutines contains reverse-engineered general-purpose game algorithms and still includes chunks of original disassembled code adapted to x64 MASM, with a stated plan to replace them incrementally with equivalent C. A companion ResourceBrowser inspects and exports assets from the original DAT files.

revenge-mutant-camels-c64.title: Revenge of the Mutant Camels
revenge-mutant-camels-c64.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1984 C64 game Revenge of the Mutant Camels, with a reproducible 64tass build and playable browser version.

revs-bbc-micro-moxon.title: Revs — BBC Micro reconstruction
revs-bbc-micro-moxon.notes: Geoff Crammond's Revs reconstructed by hand from the BBC Micro binaries with multiple supported variants; the reference build is checksum-verified against the original.

flashback-rextract-amiga-to-st.title: RExtract — Flashback Amiga disk extractor
flashback-rextract-amiga-to-st.notes: Browser-side extraction of Flashback Amiga install disks into the DATA layout of the author’s Atari ST REminiscence port. Decodes IPF/ADF/ADZ and OFS/FFS; converts 21 MOD tracks to YM register streams. Requires user-supplied disks.

rick-dangerous-oracle-trainer.title: Rick Dangerous — Oracle trainer menu reconstruction
rick-dangerous-oracle-trainer.display_title: Rick Dangerous — Oracle trainer menu reconstruction
rick-dangerous-oracle-trainer.notes: Weetibix / Oracle is credited for the historical Oracle Rick Dangerous trainer menu. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header names Weetibix/Oracle and the reconstruction; labelled game patch addresses and Amiga OS/hardware calls are present. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

dos-rigelengine.title: RigelEngine
dos-rigelengine.display_title: Duke Nukem II — modern reverse-engineered engine
dos-rigelengine.notes: Separate from Duke2Reconstructed: modern C++ engine informed by original DOS disassembly; reads original game data and supports all four episodes. README directs readers to the same author's byte-exact reconstruction for historically faithful DOS code.

rip-and-tear-c64-demo-analysis.title: rip-and-tear
rip-and-tear-c64-demo-analysis.display_title: Rip and Tear — C64 demo effects analysis notes
rip-and-tear-c64-demo-analysis.notes: VICE save states and research notes documenting experimental reverse engineering of C64 demo effects; the README explicitly says the work is still limited in scope.

river-raid-spectrum.title: River Raid
river-raid-spectrum.notes: Annotated disassembly built from the original tape image; build process checks generated output against the game image and can apply fixes.

rnc-propack-decompiled-lab313ru.title: RNC ProPack — decompiled compressor
rnc-propack-decompiled-lab313ru.notes: Decompiled RNC ProPack compression tool with pack/unpack, search and extraction modes and a Makefile plus Visual Studio project. Its README notes original-game-specific packing parameters for Earthworm Jim and Aladdin; original tool CPU/platform is not specified there.

robin-of-the-wood-spectrum.title: Robin of the Wood
robin-of-the-wood-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

robocod-trsi-trainer.title: Robocod — TRSI trainer menu reconstruction
robocod-trsi-trainer.notes: TRSI is credited for the historical TRSI Robocod trainer menu. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header identifies the reconstructed Robocod trainer; assembly plus a separate music binary and assets are present. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

robocop-spectrum-analyser.title: Robocop
robocop-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Robocop directory contains an approximately 518 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

robocop-3-nes-g0me3.title: RoboCop 3
robocop-3-nes-g0me3.notes: The repository identifies itself as a RoboCop 3 NES Back From Source project and contains large annotated bank files, RAM/sound/sprite definitions, research notes and DASM build scripts. Reassembly is documented, but successful execution, playability and byte identity were not independently verified.

robotron-2084-apple2-fschuhi.title: Robotron 2084 — Apple II reverse engineering
robotron-2084-apple2-fschuhi.notes: Apple II Robotron 2084 reverse-engineering workbench and disassembly. The project evolved from a Python emulator/debugger with tracing and memory/call-tree tools to C#/Virtu and SourceGen-assisted analysis; its current disassembly is retained in the repository.

jotd-rocn-rope-amiga.title: Roc'n Rope — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-rocn-rope-amiga.notes: Roc'n Rope Amiga port; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

rockford-hidden-level-patcher.title: Rockford Patcher
rockford-hidden-level-patcher.display_title: Rockford — DOS hidden-level recovery and patcher
rockford-hidden-level-patcher.notes: Patches the DOS Rockford executable to unlock hidden levels and reconstructs additional theme tiles, values and graphics. Historical Amiga art is compared in the research, but the tool does not patch Amiga media.

rolling-thunder-amiga-jotd.title: Rolling Thunder — Amiga 68k translation
rolling-thunder-amiga-jotd.notes: Original dual-6809 and MCU listings, a game-specific 157 KB Amiga assembly driver and RollingThunderHD slave show substantial Namco System 86 to Amiga work. README still describes Jail Break, so its controls/completion claims are not attributed to this project. TODO documents sprite and interrupt problems; build and playability are unverified.

rscview-gem-resource-renderer.title: rscview — GEM resource renderer
rscview-gem-resource-renderer.notes: C project renders Atari GEM resource files to PNG and offers build snapshots/releases. Treat as an asset inspection tool; no claim that original resource editor source was reverse engineered.

rsi-cruncher-14-reconstructed.title: RSI Cruncher v1.4 — reconstructed Amiga source
rsi-cruncher-14-reconstructed.display_title: RSI Cruncher v1.4 — reconstructed Amiga source
rsi-cruncher-14-reconstructed.notes: Flash / Red Sector Inc. is credited for the historical RSI Cruncher v1.4 historical program. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header credits Flash/Red Sector Inc. and Volker Schwaberow's reconstruction; annotated I/O and compression routines follow. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

rusty-backup-amiga-atari.title: Rusty Backup
rusty-backup-amiga-atari.display_title: Rusty Backup — Amiga RDB and Atari AHDI image tooling
rusty-backup-amiga-atari.notes: Multi-platform vintage-disk backup and inspection suite. README details Amiga RDB and AFFS/PFS/SFS paths plus Atari AHDI/GEMDOS and ST/MSA; existing AHDI table editing remains browse-only, while new Atari root tables can be created. Physical floppy access is limited to OS block devices, not flux hardware.

swiv-amiga-re.title: S.W.I.V. Amiga disk reconstruction
swiv-amiga-re.notes: Measured reconstruction of the Amiga floppy boot chain, proprietary packers, graphics and maps. Browser disk explorer reads a user-supplied ADF locally; no original game disk distributed. The README describes tools and replay work, not a demonstrated complete Amiga binary rebuild.

sabotage-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Sabotage
sabotage-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Sabotage — Apple II game disassembly & engine analysis
sabotage-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Sabotage disassembly with SourceGen files/binaries and detailed analysis of entity structures, collision behavior, difficulty progression and XOR-rendered hi-res graphics.

saboteur-spectrum.title: Saboteur
saboteur-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

saboteur-spectrum-analyser.title: Saboteur
saboteur-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Saboteur directory contains an approximately 1041 KiB Analysis.json annotation database, plus custom room draw/viewer scripts; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

sabre-wulf-spectrum.title: Sabre Wulf
sabre-wulf-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

safari-guns-st-crack-research.title: Safari Guns — documented ST reconstruction
safari-guns-st-crack-research.notes: Project-specific source and detailed disk/protection analysis accompany a modified Safari Guns release. Includes loader and bug fixes, partial filing, hard-drive support and a 512 KiB configuration; Falcon/TT/CT60 claims are upstream and not independently run here. This is a patch/reconstruction, not complete original game source.

sanxion-c64-analyser.title: Sanxion
sanxion-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Sanxion directory contains an Analysis.json annotation database (71 KiB), saved analysis state (40 KiB), emulator save state and project configuration. Tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

sbasic-atari-st-source-analysis.title: SBasic — Atari ST source analysis
sbasic-atari-st-source-analysis.notes: Original programmer publishes his 1987/88 FBasic/SBasic assembly, annotated source and reconstructed documentation, along with a PRG and as68/link68 commands. Source provenance is original source, not binary-only recovery.

sci-companion-ide.title: SCI Companion — Sierra game IDE
sci-companion-ide.notes: IDE for Sierra SCI0 to SCI1.1 games; use with corresponding game files. Platform list reflects shared SCI resource formats, not a verified cross-platform build of this Windows program.

dos-ericoakford-sci-archive.title: SCI Decompilation Archive
dos-ericoakford-sci-archive.display_title: Sierra SCI games — older decompiled and tested script corpus
dos-ericoakford-sci-archive.notes: Earlier independent SCI Companion project corpus with title-specific game.ini, decompiled script source and occasional gameplay fixes; King's Quest I README reports completion testing but a moveButterfly caveat. Overlaps subjects with sluicebox/sci-scripts yet differs in versions, tooling history and human edits; no blanket script-build claim.

sierra-sci-tools-sluicebox.title: SCI Tools — decompiler and parsers
sierra-sci-tools-sluicebox.notes: Author-published script decompiler, annotators and resource parsers that generate the SCI Scripts corpus; shared SCI formats, not Amiga/ST native 68k decoding.

jotd-scramble-amiga.title: Scramble — Amiga arcade port

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga 500
runtime_profiles.notes: README requires 1 MB and states 50 fps even on a 68000 A500.

evidence.excerpt: any 68k CPU; Kickstart 1.3, 1MB memory

jotd-scramble-amiga.notes: 1:1 Amiga 500 port in 68k assembly, with original portrait layout, visuals, sounds and 50 fps target; README credits Scott Tunstall's arcade reverse-engineering work.

scuba-dive-spectrum.title: Scuba Dive
scuba-dive-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Work in progress.

scummvm-extraction-tools.title: ScummVM Tools — Amiga/ST extractors
scummvm-extraction-tools.notes: Project tool collection includes extract_agos for packed Amiga/ST Elvira 1/2, Waxworks and Simon the Sorcerer 1 files, plus Cinematique and other archive extractors. Entry indexes the collection and its documented Amiga/ST scope, not a claim that every tool supports both platforms.

dos-sdlpop.title: SDLPoP
dos-sdlpop.display_title: Prince of Persia — DOS-disassembly-derived SDL port
dos-sdlpop.notes: Port of DOS Prince of Persia 1.0 based on the author's separately published IDA disassembly, with later-version features and modern extensions. The Apple II original source is cited as supporting evidence, not the DOS code being catalogued.

swos-openswos.title: Sensible World of Soccer / OpenSWOS
swos-openswos.notes: Modern OpenSWOS work builds on reconstruction of the original Amiga SWOS binary.

seven-cities-of-gold-remaster.title: Seven Cities of Gold — reverse-engineered macOS remaster
seven-cities-of-gold-remaster.display_title: Seven Cities of Gold — reverse-engineered macOS remaster
seven-cities-of-gold-remaster.notes: In-progress macOS remaster of Seven Cities of Gold reconstructed from the original C64 disks. Current work recovers world generation, map/navigation behaviour, graphics and runtime-only presentation details, with ported routines checked against captured execution of the original.

shadowrun-genesis-defragged.title: Shadowrun Defragged
shadowrun-genesis-defragged.notes: Bug-fix/balance project backed by substantial reverse engineering of the Sega Genesis Shadowrun ROM. Its repository contains patch definitions with byte-level rationale, research notes, diagnostics tooling and a patch-builder framework; the RE pipeline used labelled sega2asm output to recover combat, spell and other game-system behaviour.

sheep-in-space-c64.title: Sheep in Space
sheep-in-space-c64.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1984 C64 game Sheep in Space, with a reproducible build and playable browser version.

sherlock-spectrum.title: Sherlock
sherlock-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

shirazmcp-hatari-debugger.title: ShirazMCP
shirazmcp-hatari-debugger.notes: Local Rust MCP server for Hatari with CPU/memory inspection, disassembly, xrefs, watchpoints, screen and sound extraction, depacking, profiling and live 68000 patching. Requires Hatari, a user-supplied TOS ROM and an X display; the README says there are no prebuilt releases and Windows is unsupported.

shufflepuck-cafe-reforged.title: Shufflepuck Café — reforged
shufflepuck-cafe-reforged.notes: Original ST disk data and 68000 code were analyzed to reconstruct graphics, sound, physics, AI, animation and menus for a playable browser version. README labels any inferred pieces RECONSTRUCTION; a web game is not a byte-identical ST executable.

sidecartridge-md-browser.title: SidecarTridge File & Download Manager
sidecartridge-md-browser.display_title: SidecarTridge — Atari ST disk image browser
sidecartridge-md-browser.notes: SidecarTridge Multi-device app serves a web UI for browsing ST images as folders, creating blank images and converting ST/MSA. Requires the SidecarTridge hardware; upstream calls its Booster loader alpha.

sidewinder-champs-intro.title: Sidewinder — The Champs intro reconstruction
sidewinder-champs-intro.notes: Dr. Pablo / The Champs is credited for the historical The Champs Sidewinder intro. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header identifies a reconstructed intro and gives a vasm -m68000 binary build command; bitplane files are included. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

sierra-sci-decompiled-scripts.title: Sierra SCI scripts — decompiled corpus
sierra-sci-decompiled-scripts.notes: More than 300 SCI game versions have decompiled and annotated scripts. Coverage is of the platform-shared SCI bytecode, not the native Amiga or ST interpreter; compilation depends on SCI Companion and game/version.

sim-city-nes-g0me3.title: Sim City (NES)
sim-city-nes-g0me3.display_title: Sim City (unreleased NES) — code analysis and restored build
sim-city-nes-g0me3.notes: Back From Source reconstruction of the unreleased NES Sim City prototype. The extensive primary README traces game and simulation engines, city tiles, unused functions and bugs, then documents code cleanup, restorations and gameplay fixes. The build script assembles a NES image; modified builds are not claimed byte-exact to the original.

sk6502-disassembly-components.title: sk6502
sk6502-disassembly-components.notes: SkoolKit components for the 6502, including assembler/disassembler, code/data control generation, cross-referenced HTML output and VICE snapshots. C64 examples use Lee Davison ROM annotations and a separately authored Skool Daze study; tool is catalogued independently of those subjects.

skool-daze-c64-sk6502.title: Skool Daze
skool-daze-c64-sk6502.display_title: Skool Daze — complete annotated C64 disassembly
skool-daze-c64-sk6502.notes: The examples/sdc64 tree contains a 518 KB instruction/data control file and extensive independently credited game annotations for C64 Skool Daze, rendered with sk6502/SkoolKit. This is a source-linked analysis project, not a claimed playable or byte-identical rebuild.

skool-daze-spectrum.title: Skool Daze
skool-daze-spectrum.notes: Complete maintained RAM disassembly; first public release recorded in 2008 and current source can generate assembler output.

smallest-gridrunner-st.title: Smallest Gridrunner — 256 KiB ST adaptation

runtime_profiles.name: 256 KiB ST configuration (Hatari tested)
runtime_profiles.notes: Author reports the rebuilt game running in Hatari configured with 256 KiB RAM; this is an emulator-tested configuration, with no real 260ST test claimed.

evidence.excerpt: In my testing I was able to run Gridrunner on the Hatari emulator with the following settings :- Only 256kiB of RAM.

smallest-gridrunner-st.notes: Modern VASM adaptation of mwenge’s existing Atari ST Gridrunner disassembly. Reworks hard-coded addresses for low-memory machines and adds a monochrome sprite editor; author reports running it in Hatari with 256 KiB RAM, or 512 KiB with TOS booted from floppy. This is a distinct derivative, not a new independently reverse-engineered original listing.

smugglers-cove-spectrum-bedazzle.title: Smuggler's Cove
smugglers-cove-spectrum-bedazzle.display_title: Smuggler's Cove — ZX Spectrum byte-exact disassembly
smugglers-cove-spectrum-bedazzle.notes: Complete recompilable disassembly of the 1983 ZX Spectrum text adventure. The reconstructed machine-code block is verified byte-identical to the original, all major engine/data formats are decoded, references are relocation-tested, and code/data classification is validated against an RZX gameplay trace. With the user-supplied original BASIC loader it round-trips to a working tape image.

solomons-key-nes-reconstruction.title: Solomon's Key — NES source reconstruction
solomons-key-nes-reconstruction.notes: Byte-identical ca65 source reconstruction of the USA and European NES releases of Solomon's Key. The project verifies full iNES images, runs direct runtime scenarios for both profiles, decodes multiple authoring/data models and provides profile-aware editing and round-trip validation tools.

son-shu-shi-st-protection-rework.title: Son Shu Shi — ST protection and loader rework
son-shu-shi-st-protection-rework.upstream_name: Son Shu Shi — ST protection and loader rework
son-shu-shi-st-protection-rework.display_title: Son Shu Shi — ST protection and loader rework
source_language: protected floppy tracks and game binary
son-shu-shi-st-protection-rework.notes: Documented IPL disk/protection analysis and source for loader changes, checksum removal, repacking, filing and machine compatibility; release images provided. Credits original ST and Amiga game programmers separately: this work examines the ST version, not Amiga executable code.

sonicarranger-sonicconv.title: SonicArranger packed format converter
sonicarranger-sonicconv.notes: Converts SonicArranger player-bundled binary song modules back to editable application format. Repository contains a host Python converter and a SAS/C Amiga implementation with compilation instructions.

space-eggs-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Space Eggs
space-eggs-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Space Eggs disassembly based on a commonly circulated 30.5KB cracked binary. The project publishes a disassembly listing and SourceGen project set and identifies unused data and remnants of the original copy protection.

speedball2-amiga.title: Speedball 2
speedball2-amiga.notes: Amiga reverse engineering informed by analysis of another platform version.

c64-gillham-speedscript.title: SpeedScript 3.2r2
c64-gillham-speedscript.notes: Transcribed Charles Brannon’s published original assembly from print and converted/modularized it to ca65; default output is author-reported byte-matching C64 3.2r2. Instant 80 and Easy Cursor variants also build. This is printed original-source restoration rather than binary RE.

spellbound-spectrum.title: Spellbound
spellbound-spectrum.notes: Complete 48K RAM disassembly by Philip M. Anderson; source preserved in Michael Cook's archive.

spellbound-128k-spectrum-analyser.title: Spellbound 128K
spellbound-128k-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Spellbound128K directory contains an approximately 1296 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus graphics-set metadata. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

splitting-images-spectrum.title: Splitting Images
splitting-images-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

spreadpoint-x-large-amiga.title: Spreadpoint X-Large demo
spreadpoint-x-large-amiga.notes: ReSource disassembly and slight modernization of Spreadpoint X-Large demo with extracted graphics and music. No explicit build verification or binary identity claim.

spy-hunter-c64.title: Spy Hunter
spy-hunter-c64.notes: Progressive annotated reconstruction targeting a byte-identical rebuild of the original 16KB cartridge.

spy-vs-spy-2-amiga-hitchhikr.title: Spy vs Spy II — Amiga disassembly
spy-vs-spy-2-amiga-hitchhikr.display_title: Spy vs Spy II — Amiga disassembly
spy-vs-spy-2-amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Amiga Spy vs Spy II disassembly. It is not described as complete overall, but includes all game and sound code and has a scripted ADF extraction, Capstone-assisted disassembly, reassembly and emulator-test workflow.

spy-vs-spy-3-amiga-hitchhikr.title: Spy vs Spy III — Amiga disassembly
spy-vs-spy-3-amiga-hitchhikr.display_title: Spy vs Spy III — Amiga disassembly
spy-vs-spy-3-amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Complete Amiga Spy vs Spy III game and sound-code disassembly with scripted extraction from original disk images, Capstone-assisted analysis, vasm reconstruction and emulator testing.

squirm-c64-unorig.title: Squirm
squirm-c64-unorig.notes: Reverse-engineered C64 Squirm source. The README describes an ongoing effort to work through and comment the code, with the decompiled output in 64tass syntax.

st-recover-floppy-imaging.title: ST Recover — floppy imaging
st-recover-floppy-imaging.notes: Reads ST floppies via PC drive into .ST images, including unusual sector layouts and damage recovery. README says USB drives handle standard 360/720 KB only; special formats require internal drive/driver. Protected malformed disks and 900 KB operation were not verified by author, despite broad summary.

st-remote-debugger-blagay.title: ST Remote Debugger — Visual C++ host
st-remote-debugger-blagay.upstream_name: ST Remote Debugger — Visual C++ host
st-remote-debugger-blagay.display_title: ST Remote Debugger — Visual C++ host
st-remote-debugger-blagay.notes: Host-side Visual C++ debugger source includes a 68k disassembler, memory/register requests and step/run/upload command protocol. Repository has no README or clear target-side source and references a relative external minIni path; build and working target connection remain unverified.

vt100-cartridge.title: ST VT100 Terminal Emulator cartridge
vt100-cartridge.display_title: ST VT100 — Atari ST terminal-emulator source reconstruction
vt100-cartridge.notes: All functions reconstructed into period-style C/assembly and checked against the original disassembly.

stage-swaptro-amiga-disassembly.title: Stage-Swaptro
stage-swaptro-amiga-disassembly.display_title: Stage-Swaptro — Amiga demo disassembly and variants
stage-swaptro-amiga-disassembly.notes: Reverse engineers the packed Stage swaptro extracted from Sanity's Velveteen 18 disk, documents its load address and memory map, and provides buildable 68000 source plus several patch-based visual/music variants. README includes a Makefile workflow for applying patches, assembling and making a floppy; game playability is not applicable to a demo.

amisc-amiga.title: StarCraft — AmiSC 68K
amisc-amiga.notes: Native Amiga 68k StarCraft port that reads the user's original MPQ-derived game data and supports playable skirmishes. The repository currently publishes binaries/documentation but not the port source, so implementation provenance cannot be audited from source.

starflight-st-asset-analysis.title: Starflight
starflight-st-asset-analysis.display_title: Starflight — Atari ST binary and asset analysis
starflight-st-asset-analysis.notes: Atari ST Starflight research repository with a Ghidra project and Python BTX, AGO and OMEGA font/tile readers. The code demonstrates concrete format analysis; it does not establish a compiled or playable game reconstruction.

starflight-reverse.title: Starflight Reverse
starflight-reverse.notes: Reverse engineering of the 1986 DOS game Starflight. The project exploits retained/encrypted Forth word names and the game's indirect-threaded representation to recover thousands of words, decode overlays and emit C representations of the recovered routines. A separate remastered successor, canadacow/starflight-reverse, builds on this recovered codebase with full Forth/assembly emulation and a new Vulkan presentation layer; it is tracked independently.

starflight-reverse-remastered.title: Starflight Reverse — Remastered
starflight-reverse-remastered.display_title: Starflight — Vulkan remaster from recovered Forth/x86 runtime
starflight-reverse-remastered.notes: Independent remastered successor to the s-macke Starflight reverse-engineering line. It retains/emulates the recovered Forth and assembly execution so the whole game is playable, while adding a new real-time Vulkan/rotoscoped presentation layer with switchable classic EGA/CGA output. Tracked separately from s-macke/starflight-reverse because this project is an RE-derived playable reimplementation/remaster rather than only the underlying disassembly/recovery work.

starquake-spectrum.title: Starquake
starquake-spectrum.notes: Ritchie Swann disassembly; README explicitly describes it as work in progress with routines/data still undocumented.

starquake-spectrum-analyser.title: Starquake
starquake-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Starquake directory contains a 3281 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and large annotation database plus decoded player/effect graphics. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

star-raiders-atari8-lwiest.title: StarRaiders
star-raiders-atari8-lwiest.display_title: Star Raiders — Atari 8-bit fully documented source reconstruction
star-raiders-atari8-lwiest.notes: Complete, extensively documented assembly-language reconstruction made directly from the 8 KB Star Raiders cartridge ROM and finished in September 2015. When scans of Atari's original source later resurfaced, the author compared them with the reconstruction and reports only a few trivial corrections, while retaining substantially richer explanatory documentation.

starship-commander-apple2-6502disassembl.title: Starship Commander
starship-commander-apple2-6502disassembl.display_title: Starship Commander — Apple II mixed-language disassembly
starship-commander-apple2-6502disassembl.notes: Apple II Starship Commander analysis spanning roughly two dozen Applesoft programs plus machine-language sound, graphics and font routines. The project provides commented BASIC listings, SourceGen projects for binaries and a cross-program variable map.

state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.title: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.upstream_name: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.display_title: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
subjects: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.notes: Reimplements the Spaceballs Amiga demo in C using its original graphics, animation and audio. README says the demo is complete but some timing is off; SDL2, mikmod and Python 3 are needed for the documented native build. No claim of original-source recovery or byte-identical output.

c64-mist64-static6502.title: static6502
c64-mist64-static6502.notes: Old static 6502-assembly-to-C translator used to generate the cbmbasic core. Repository explicitly says it should not be used for current work and points to libcpu as its successor; catalogued as historical tooling with that limitation.

stdl-atari-st-porting-library.title: STDL — Atari ST DirectMedia Layer
stdl-atari-st-porting-library.notes: Planar-native compatibility layer and converter for porting SDL 1.2 games to ST/STE, used by several ports. The README documents cross-compilation with m68k-atari-mint-gcc, runnable TOS examples under Hatari, byte-identical BLiTTER/CPU checks on target, and measured stock-ST/Mega-STE behavior. The 26 September update adds per-step YM tone/noise effects and preserves their millisecond timing at both 50 and 60 Hz. SDL source/assets are inputs to the porting library, so source CPU is not applicable.

stellar-7-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Stellar 7
stellar-7-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Stellar 7 — Apple II disassembly & engine analysis
stellar-7-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Detailed Apple II Stellar 7 disassembly covering the loader, title code, both game-engine portions, briefing/gameplay overlays and level/object data. The project publishes SourceGen files/binaries plus extensive analysis of 3D objects, mechanics and data structures.

albank1-stellar-dodger-c64-disassembly.title: Stellar Dodger
albank1-stellar-dodger-c64-disassembly.notes: PRG listing includes BASIC SYS loader and code/data annotation. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

stm32-usbfloppytracer-amiga-st.title: STM32 USB Floppy Tracer
stm32-usbfloppytracer-amiga-st.display_title: STM32 USB Floppy Tracer — Amiga/Atari physical disk imaging
stm32-usbfloppytracer-amiga-st.notes: STM32F407 firmware plus Rust host CLI/GUI reads ADF and ST and writes ADF, IPF, ST and experimental patched STX. Verifies written tracks. Weak-bit and some other protections remain experimental; README lists STX cases it cannot support and requires nightly Rust and external IPF parser.

storm-coming-up-amiga.title: Storm Coming Up intro
storm-coming-up-amiga.notes: ReSource-based disassembly and documented modernization of Storm Coming Up, including Copper/Blitter checkerboard analysis. Author states the supplied source assembles and runs.

stormbringer-spectrum.title: Stormbringer
stormbringer-spectrum.notes: Complete 48K RAM disassembly by Philip M. Anderson; source preserved in Michael Cook's archive.

stos-atari-basic-source.title: STOS BASIC
stos-atari-basic-source.display_title: STOS BASIC — Atari ST compiler and interpreter source
stos-atari-basic-source.notes: Mixed archive of historical STOS BASIC interpreter/compiler, extension and project assembly sources, including an orig tree and adapted src/compiler trees. Core STOS and compiler sources are explicitly 68000-oriented and emit/run native Atari ST code. Specialized Falcon and later-CPU extensions remain component-specific and do not change the core 68000 classification. The repository does not yet establish a verified end-to-end modern build or a single minimum runtime profile.

sttrans-stbook-analysis.title: STTRANS
sttrans-stbook-analysis.display_title: STTRANS — Atari STBook transfer protocol research
sttrans-stbook-analysis.notes: Research repository includes original STTRANS.PRG, its Ghidra analysis project and an 8.9 KB Python serial transfer companion implementing command, path and block/checksum handling. The public README has no detailed findings and no reconstructed STTRANS executable; this record describes the protocol/tooling work only.

stunt-car-racer-bbc-kieranhj.title: Stunt Car Racer
stunt-car-racer-bbc-kieranhj.display_title: Stunt Car Racer — C64-to-BBC Master reverse-engineered port
stunt-car-racer-bbc-kieranhj.notes: BBC Master 128 port derived from a raw C64 6502 disassembly. The team reverse engineered game functionality and data structures, rearranged them for the BBC memory map, and replaced or augmented graphics, sound and I/O for BBC hardware.

stunt-car-racer-ste-patches.title: Stunt Car Racer STE
stunt-car-racer-ste-patches.notes: Experimental blitter replacements for selected ST rendering routines. Make produces overlay binaries; run the unmodified game under Hatari and load patches into memory using the debugger. No standalone runnable disk image and no demonstrated performance improvement. STE with at least 1 MiB specified.

sundog-st-psystem.title: SunDog: Frozen Legacy
sundog-st-psystem.display_title: SunDog — Atari ST p-system runtime reconstruction
sundog-st-psystem.notes: Runs original Atari ST SunDog p-code and data from a user-supplied 360K ST disk image via a C p-system IV interpreter; recreates the few ST graphics assembly routines. The game code and assets are not distributed. Upstream documents Linux/macOS build paths.

dos-supaplex-binary-patches.title: Supaplex
dos-supaplex-binary-patches.notes: Assembly files patch portions of the original DOS executable via incbin; fixes include smooth scrolling, copy-protection bypass, input and sound changes. This is not a full game disassembly or reconstructed source tree.

jotd-super-bagman-amiga.title: Super Bagman — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-super-bagman-amiga.notes: Amiga version uses approximately 99% transcoded original code; README credits Z80 reverse engineering and Z80→68k transcode.

super-c-nes-vermiceli.title: Super C
super-c-nes-vermiceli.display_title: Super C — NES byte-exact annotated disassembly
super-c-nes-vermiceli.notes: Annotated NES Super C disassembly discovered through the Contra project's sibling link. Its README explicitly states that the build scripts reassemble the US ROM to a byte-for-byte match and can also build PAL Probotector II, with supporting bank/graphics/sound/debugging documentation.

smb3-nes-captainsouthbird.title: Super Mario Bros. 3
smb3-nes-captainsouthbird.display_title: Super Mario Bros. 3 — NES byte-exact disassembly
smb3-nes-captainsouthbird.notes: NESASM-based disassembly of Super Mario Bros. 3 US PRG1. The README explicitly states that it reassembles into a byte-for-byte perfect clone and is intended for internal research and technical ROM hacking; support files for NoDice/MusConv are included.

super-pacman-arcade-disassembly.title: Super Pac-Man
super-pacman-arcade-disassembly.notes: Project-specific Super Pac-Man 6809 listing and ROM-byte extraction exist. README still describes Mappy and the Amiga build references a missing super_pacman.68k; no completed Amiga game port or working build is inferred.

supercars3-amiga-remake-jotd.title: Supercars 3 — Super Cars I/II remake
supercars3-amiga-remake-jotd.notes: Java remake preserving the original Super Cars and Super Cars II circuits, using enhanced or extracted graphics/music while adding new cars, weapons, a circuit editor and levels. Primary readme lists 31 original circuits, host compatibility and known AI/physics differences; exact original media variants and degree of behavioral parity remain unverified.

superdiskindex-flux.title: SuperDiskIndex
superdiskindex-flux.notes: Experimental command-line tool analyzes SCP flux images from Greaseweazle, reports disk state and exports Amiga ADF/Atari images with file listings and block maps. README states Linux only and explicitly lists many known bugs.

vs-sr-cd32-superfrog.title: Superfrog — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-superfrog.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Superfrog. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

tai-pan-spectrum-analyser.title: Tai-Pan
tai-pan-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Tai-Pan directory contains an approximately 82 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

repton-electron-tape-protection.title: tape-protection-Repton
repton-electron-tape-protection.notes: Focused disassembly and commentary of the Acorn Electron tape protection used by Repton. It documents the deliberately obfuscated instruction stream, self-modifying/decryption logic, vector interception and handoff into decrypted code.

target-renegade-spectrum-analyser.title: Target Renegade
target-renegade-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Target Renegade — ZX Spectrum analyser project
target-renegade-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The TargetRenegade directory contains an approximately 610 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

task-force-amiga.title: Task Force
task-force-amiga.notes: Analysis of Mark Sheeky's 1994 Amiga freeware game; part of Tetracorp's broader reverse-engineering work.

tcb-star-wars-scroller.title: TCB Star-Wars Scroller
tcb-star-wars-scroller.notes: Reverse engineered and mostly annotated TCB Star-Wars Scroller from the unpacked standalone Atari ST demo, using Easy Rider and reassembly with vasm. The author says the distorted scroller section was not fully reversed; a modification restores quit behavior changed in the extracted version. No minimum runnable hardware or byte-identical output claim is established.

tearaway-thomas-dhp2.title: Tearaway Thomas
tearaway-thomas-dhp2.display_title: Tearaway Thomas — Amiga DHp2 unpacking research
tearaway-thomas-dhp2.notes: Contains packed and unpacked Tearaway Thomas data and a substantive Python DHp2 decompressor. The README calls it a partial reimplementation, but the public tree substantiates unpacking research only; no playable reconstruction is claimed.

tecmo-super-bowl-nes-bruddog.title: Tecmo Super Bowl
tecmo-super-bowl-nes-bruddog.display_title: Tecmo Super Bowl — exhaustive NES byte-exact disassembly
tecmo-super-bowl-nes-bruddog.notes: Exhaustive NES disassembly developed from an earlier raw/uncommented listing. The README states every instruction and memory location was reverse engineered, labeled and commented and that the source gives a byte-for-byte rebuild of the original game; supporting ROM maps and bug/unused-code documentation are included.

teletext-elite-moxon.title: Teletext Elite
teletext-elite-moxon.display_title: Teletext Elite — BBC Micro/Master Mode 7 conversion

runtime_profiles.name: BBC Micro
runtime_profiles.notes: Project explicitly targets BBC Micro.

evidence.quote: Teletext Elite on the BBC Micro

runtime_profiles.name: BBC Master 128
runtime_profiles.notes: Project explicitly targets BBC Master 128.

teletext-elite-moxon.notes: Full Elite converted to BBC teletext Mode 7. The project is built on source reconstructed from the BBC Micro disassembly and adds new teletext rendering code while preserving the complete game.

terramex-spectrum.title: Terramex
terramex-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: In progress.

tetracorp-fsuae-lua-shell.title: Tetracorp FS-UAE Lua shell patch
tetracorp-fsuae-lua-shell.notes: The project-specific page at /tools/fs-uae-lua.diff provides an FS-UAE Lua-shell patch based on cnvogelg’s 2015 upstream pull request; Tetracorp documents applying it to FS-UAE 3.1.66 to inspect Amiga memory and script live analysis. Build and current-version compatibility have not been independently verified.

tetrapack-amiga-reconstructed.title: Tetrapack v2.2 — reconstructed Amiga source
tetrapack-amiga-reconstructed.notes: Antiaction / Defjam is credited for the historical Tetrapack v2.2 historical cruncher. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header identifies reconstructed Tetrapack v2.2; assembly contains labelled RLE/LZ77 packing routines. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

tetris-nes-celestialamber.title: TetrisNESDisasm
tetris-nes-celestialamber.notes: NES Tetris disassembly with a reproducible build target for the known U.S. ROM; the README gives the target ROM MD5 explicitly, making the byte-exact claim verifiable without inferring runtime requirements.

abbey-of-crime-english-cpc.title: The Abbey of Crime (English translation)
abbey-of-crime-english-cpc.notes: English translation/patching project built from detailed CPC reverse engineering; repository also preserves a complete disassembly supplied during the project.

castles-dr-creep-c64.title: The Castles of Dr. Creep
castles-dr-creep-c64.notes: Commented reconstructed source including copy protection; repository description states a bit-for-bit identical recreation goal.

graphics-magician-picture-painter-apple2.title: The Graphics Magician Picture Painter
graphics-magician-picture-painter-apple2.display_title: Graphics Magician Picture Painter — Apple II graphics-tool disassembly
graphics-magician-picture-painter-apple2.notes: Disassembly of the single-hi-res PICDRAWH code from the 1984 Graphics Magician release, with SourceGen files/binaries and documentation of its compact drawing-command format, brushes, text and flood fill.

great-escape-spectrum.title: The Great Escape
great-escape-spectrum.notes: Annotated, reassemblable Spectrum reverse engineering with a separate C reimplementation effort.

the-hobbit-spectrum.title: The Hobbit
the-hobbit-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

king-of-chicago-hqc-intro.title: The King of Chicago — HQC intro reconstruction
king-of-chicago-hqc-intro.upstream_name: HQC The King of Chicago intro
king-of-chicago-hqc-intro.display_title: The King of Chicago — HQC intro reconstruction
subjects: HQC The King of Chicago intro
king-of-chicago-hqc-intro.notes: HQC is credited for the historical HQC The King of Chicago intro. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header identifies a reconstructed Amiga intro for The King of Chicago; annotated startup and hardware routines follow. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

zelda1-nes-aldonunez.title: The Legend of Zelda
zelda1-nes-aldonunez.display_title: The Legend of Zelda — NES complete disassembly
zelda1-nes-aldonunez.notes: Complete-disassembly project built from renewed reverse engineering with Mesen and a custom MLB/ROM processing tool. The ca65/ld65 build reconstructs an NES ROM and explicitly compares it with the original PRG0 ROM; byte exactness remains unset because the documentation describes the verifier rather than separately asserting the current checked result.

lords-of-midnight-spectrum-dos.title: The Lords of Midnight
